meaningShort: Dream (Svapna) is inward perception of real subtle forms shaped by Bhagavān Taijasa (seated in the throat/mind) out of latent waking impressions (vāsanās).
meaningDeep: Dream objects are real mental creations fashioned instantaneously by the Lord (`sandhye sṛṣṭir āha hi` — BS 3.2.1) from mental vāsanās to yield subtle karmic retribution or prophetic indications; only identifying them with gross external things is an error.

padaccheda.gloss: being fashioned out of impressions of waking perceptions
is Bhagavān in His Taijasa form

lakshanaDeva: घनप्रज्ञस्तथा प्राज्ञः । उपरतेन्द्रियमनोवृत्तेर्जीवस्य हृदये प्राज्ञालिङ्गितस्य स्वरूपसुखानुभवः सुषुप्तिः ।
lakshanaIast: ghanaprajñas tathā prājñaḥ | uparatendriyamanovṛtter jīvasya hṛdaye prājñāliṅgitasya svarūpasukhānubhavaḥ suṣuptiḥ |
meaningShort: Deep Sleep (Suṣupti) is the state where outer senses and mind subside and the Jīva, embraced by Bhagavān Prājña in the heart-lotus, intuits its bare self, time, and a glimpse of innate ease via Sākṣī.
meaningDeep: Even when all material instruments rest in Suṣupti, the Jīva does not merge into undifferentiated identity with Brahman; held closely by Prājña Hari in the hṛdaya-ākāśa, its Sākṣī continues to witness innate sukha and kāla, enabling the waking memory 'I slept peacefully.'

padaccheda.gloss: Bhagavān Prājña, who governs compact unmanifested consciousness
when sense and mental modifications have ceased
embraced by Lord Prājña in the heart

lakshanaDeva: निवृत्तेः सर्वदुःखानामीशानः प्रभुरव्ययः । सर्वदुःखानां निवृत्तेः कारणभूतस्तुरीयो देवो मोक्षदः सम्प्रकीर्तितः ।
lakshanaIast: nivṛtteḥ sarvaduḥkhānām īśānaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ | sarvaduḥkhānāṃ nivṛtteḥ kāraṇabhūtas turīyo devo mokṣadaḥ samprakīrtitaḥ |
meaningShort: Turīya is the fourth transcendent form of Bhagavān Hari who completely terminates all sorrow and bestows eternal liberation (Mokṣa).
meaningDeep: In Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad 1.10 (`nāntaḥprajñaṃ na bahiḥprajñam...`), Advaita reads Turīya as an attribute-less Ātman; Madhvācārya demonstrates from the verse's own epithets (`īśānaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ`) that Turīya is the supreme personal Lord Viṣṇu, sovereign remover of all bondage.

padaccheda.gloss: of the complete cessation of all sorrows
the Fourth resplendent form of Hari

lakshanaDeva: माहात्म्यज्ञानपूर्वस्तु सुदृढः सर्वतोऽधिकः । स्नेहो भक्तिरिति प्रोक्तस्तया मुक्तिर्न चान्यथा ॥
lakshanaIast: māhātmyajñānapūrvas tu sudṛḍhaḥ sarvato'dhikaḥ | sneho bhaktir iti proktas tayā muktir na cānyathā ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: भक्त्यर्थान्यखिलान्येव भक्तिर्मोक्षाय केवला । मुक्तानामपि भक्तिर्हि नित्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: bhaktyarthāny akhilāny eva bhaktir mokṣāya kevalā | muktānām api bhaktir hi nityānandasvarūpiṇī ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: All spiritual disciplines exist for the sake of Bhakti; Bhakti alone leads to liberation, and even among liberated souls Bhakti abides eternally as the very form of bliss.

meaningShort: Bhakti is unshakeable love for Bhagavān, preceded by true knowledge of His supreme majesty (māhātmya-jñāna) and surpassing love for all else — through it alone is liberation attained.
meaningDeep: Perhaps the single greatest verse in Tattvavāda soteriology (MBTN 1.85). Madhvācārya fuses knowledge and love into an indivisible whole: affection without knowledge of God's supremacy is mere sentiment, and dry knowledge without supreme love cannot win grace. Bhakti is simultaneously the means (sādhana) and continues in Mokṣa as parama-bhakti, an eternal outpouring of blissful love.

padaccheda.gloss: preceded and grounded in knowledge of the Lord's supreme majesty
unwavering across all trials and obstacles
surpassing attachment to oneself and all other beings
such flowing love is declared to be Bhakti
by that alone comes liberation, and never otherwise

lakshanaDeva: त्रिविधसांसारिकदुःखदर्शनेन सज्जनसङ्गत्या च इहामुत्रफलभोगविरागो वैराग्यम् ।
lakshanaIast: trividhasāṃsārikaduḥkhadarśanena sajjanasaṅgatyā ca ihāmutraphalabhogavirāgo vairāgyam |
meaningShort: Vairāgya (dispassion) is detachment from craving selfish enjoyments both here and in celestial realms, awakened through discerning the threefold sorrow of saṃsāra and keeping company with the wise.
meaningDeep: In Dvaita, Vairāgya is not hatred of the real world created by Viṣṇu, but relinquishment of egoistic possessiveness (mamakāra) and sensual craving so that all things are seen as belonging to Hari and engaged in His service.

padaccheda.gloss: by seeing the threefold afflictions of worldly existence
and through fellowship with saintly devotees
non-attachment to enjoyment of fruits here and hereafter

lakshanaDeva: सर्वतन्त्रस्वतन्त्रे हरौ स्वपारतन्त्र्यानुसन्धानपूर्वकं सर्वसमर्पणं तदेकाश्रयणं शरणागतिः ।
lakshanaIast: sarvatantrasvatantre harau svapāratantryānusandhānapūrvakaṃ sarvasamarpaṇaṃ tadekāśrayaṇaṃ śaraṇāgatiḥ |
meaningShort: Śaraṇāgati (wholehearted refuge) is seeking sole shelter in the all-independent Lord Hari and dedicating all actions and fruits to Him in vivid awareness of one's utter dependence.
meaningDeep: Grounded in Bhagavadgītā 18.66 (`sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja`), Madhvācārya explains 'parityajya' not as abandoning enjoined duties, but abandoning selfish claim to fruits (phala-tyāga) and false sense of independent agency (kartṛtvābhimāna-tyāga).

padaccheda.gloss: in Lord Hari, the sole Independent Ruler
with mindfulness of one's total ontological dependence
offering everything and taking sole refuge in Him

lakshanaDeva: सद्गुरूपदेशेन सच्छास्त्रार्थज्ञानरूपं श्रवणम् । अज्ञाननिवर्तकम् ।
lakshanaIast: sadgurūpadeśena sacchāstrārthajñānarūpaṃ śravaṇam | ajñānanivartakam |
meaningShort: Śravaṇa is receptive study of the true import of sacred scripture through the instruction of a qualified Guru, dispelling initial ignorance (ajñāna).
meaningDeep: In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka triad `śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ`, Śravaṇa removes simple lack of knowledge (ajñāna), Manana removes doubt and contrary error (saṃśaya-viparyaya), and Nididhyāsana culminates in direct vision (aparokṣa).

padaccheda.gloss: through instruction from a realized teacher
consisting in grasping the true meaning of authoritative śāstras

lakshanaDeva: श्रुतस्य तत्त्वस्य हृदीकरणाय मीमांसापरपर्यायो विचारो मननम् । संशयमिथ्याज्ञाननिरासकम् ।
lakshanaIast: śrutasya tattvasya hṛdīkaraṇāya mīmāṃsāparaparyāyo vicāro mananam | saṃśayamithyājñānanirāsakam |
meaningShort: Manana (rational inquiry / Mīmāṃsā) is systematic reflection with valid Nyāya canons to make heard scriptural truth one's own conviction by uprooting doubt and misconception.
meaningDeep: In Anuvyākhyāna under `athāto brahmajijñāsā`, Madhvācārya elevates Jijñāsā / Manana to sacred worship: employing rigorous logic in harmony with Śruti is indispensable because unsettled doubts block one-pointed meditation (dhyāna).

padaccheda.gloss: to internalize the reality learned through Śravaṇa

lakshanaDeva: इतरतिरस्कारपूर्वकभगवद्विषयकाखण्डस्मृतिर्ध्यानम् । तदेव निदिध्यासनम् ।
lakshanaIast: itaratiraskārapūrvakabhagavadviṣayakākhaṇḍasmṛtir dhyānam | tad eva nididhyāsanam |
meaningShort: Dhyāna (Nididhyāsana) is an unbroken, continuous stream of loving remembrance focused upon Bhagavān to the exclusion of all extraneous thoughts.
meaningDeep: Once Śravaṇa and Manana establish unshakeable certainty (`idam ittham iti niścaya`), the seeker practices Upāsanā/Dhyāna upon the Bimba-rūpa of Bhagavān suited to their innate yogyatā until Dhyāna ripens by grace into direct vision (Aparokṣa-jñāna).

padaccheda.gloss: setting aside all distracting non-divine thoughts
having the form and attributes of Bhagavān as object
an uninterrupted oil-like flow of remembrance

lakshanaDeva: शिष्यस्वरूपं सम्यग्ज्ञात्वा तद्योग्यविशिष्टभगवद्रूपविशेषविषयकविद्योपदेशकर्तारो नियतगुरवः ।
lakshanaIast: śiṣyasvarūpaṃ samyag jñātvā tadyogyaviśiṣṭabhagavadrūpaviśeṣaviṣayakavidyopadeśakartāro niyataguravaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: यस्य देवे परा भक्तिर्यथा देवे तथा गुरौ । तस्यैते कथिता ह्यर्थाः प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: yasya deve parā bhaktir yathā deve tathā gurau | tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Unto that high-souled seeker who bears supreme devotion to the Lord and fitting devotion to the Guru, these sacred truths shine forth.

meaningShort: The ordained Guru (Niyata-guru) is one who discerns the disciple's true spiritual nature and imparts meditation on the specific form of Bhagavān fitted to that soul's yogyatā.
meaningDeep: In Brahmasūtra Bhāṣya and Katha Upaniṣad Bhāṣya (`proktā'nyenaiva sujñānāya`), Madhvācārya emphasizes that Guru-prasāda is indispensable for liberation: Mukhyaprāṇa/Brahmā stands as the supreme created Guru of the cosmos, while Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa Himself is the Guru of all Gurus.

padaccheda.gloss: discerning accurately the disciple's innate capacity
the specific indwelling Bimba-form of the Lord suited to them

lakshanaDeva: तस्मादनाद्यनन्तं हि तारतम्यं चिदात्मनाम् । मुक्तानां च न हीयन्ते तारतम्यं च सर्वदा ॥
lakshanaIast: tasmād anādy anantaṃ hi tāratamyaṃ cidātmanām | muktānāṃ ca na hīyante tāratamyaṃ ca sarvadā ||
meaningShort: Tāratamya is the beginningless, eternal gradation of intrinsic knowledge, devotion, and bliss among sentient beings, free of all envy in Mokṣa.
meaningDeep: Just as vessels of varying sizes — from a small cup to an ocean — are each filled to their own 100% brim without envy or deficiency, every liberated soul enjoys complete fullness of its own svarūpa-ānanda in harmonious reverence toward higher tattvas and supreme Viṣṇu at the apex.

padaccheda.gloss: intrinsic gradation of excellence and capacity
persisting harmoniously forever even among the liberated

lakshanaDeva: मोक्षसाधनं च ज्ञानं योग्यापरोक्षरूपम् । स्वयोग्यबिम्बरूपभगवत्साक्षात्कारो ह्यपरोक्षज्ञानम् ।
lakshanaIast: mokṣasādhanaṃ ca jñānaṃ yogyāparokṣarūpam | svayogyabimbarūpabhagavatsākṣātkāro hy aparokṣajñānam |
meaningShort: Aparokṣa-jñāna is direct, immediate perceptual vision of one's indwelling Bimba-form of Bhagavān according to one's spiritual capacity — the proximate doorway to liberation.
meaningDeep: Mediate scriptural knowledge (parokṣa-jñāna) cannot by itself sever beginningless karmic bondage; when Dhyāna matures through supreme Bhakti and Viṣṇu's grace (`yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ`), the Lord unveils His radiant Bimba-form directly to the purified inner eye.

padaccheda.gloss: consisting in direct immediate vision fitted to one's capacity

lakshanaDeva: जीवस्य परमात्माधीनो बन्धः । ईश्वरेच्छाऽविद्याकामकर्मलिङ्गशरीरत्रिगुणात्मकमनःस्थूलशरीरादिरूपः सत्य एव ।
lakshanaIast: jīvasya paramātmādhīno bandhaḥ | īśvarecchā'vidyākāmakarmaliṅgaśarīratriguṇātmakamanaḥsthūlaśarīrādirūpaḥ satya eva |
meaningShort: Bondage (Bandha) is the Jīva's real — not illusory — entanglement in positive Avidyā, subtle sixteen-part Liṅga-śarīra, karma, and gross embodiment under the governance of Paramātman.
meaningDeep: Madhvācārya argues in Viṣṇutattvavinirṇaya and Tattvodyota that if bondage were merely imaginary (mithyā), mere verbal instruction would end it without needing divine grace (`bandhamithyātvaṃ na yuktimat`); because Bandha is real and forged by the Lord's Māyā-śakti (`parābhidhyānāt tu tirohitaṃ tato hy asya bandhaviparyayau` — BS 3.2.5), only the Lord's grace can unbind it.

padaccheda.gloss: bondage governed by the Supreme Lord
positive ignorance, desire, and karmic desert
consisting of the subtle and gross bodies

lakshanaDeva: षोडशकलोपेतस्य लिङ्गशरीरस्य विरजानदीस्नानेन जीवसम्बन्धनाशो लिङ्गभङ्गः ।
lakshanaIast: ṣoḍaśakalopetasya liṅgaśarīrasya virajānādīsnānena jīvasambandhanāśo liṅgabhaṅgaḥ |
meaningShort: Liṅgabhaṅga is the final sundering of the beginningless sixteen-part subtle body (liṅga-śarīra) through sacred immersion in the cosmic Virajā river on the threshold of Mokṣa.
meaningDeep: Every bound Jīva is encased from beginningless time in a subtle cocoon of ten subtle senses, five prāṇas, and subtle mind (ṣoḍaśa-kalā). When all prārabdha is exhausted and the soul ascends with Caturmukha Brahmā, bathing in the Lakṣmī-embodied Virajā river dissolves this last material veil forever.

padaccheda.gloss: by immersion in the transcendent Virajā river

lakshanaDeva: परमात्मप्रसादजः प्रकृत्यविद्यादिबन्धमोक्षः स्वरूपसुखानुभूतिश्च मुक्तिः ।
lakshanaIast: paramātmaprasādajaḥ prakṛtyavidyādibandhamokṣaḥ svarūpasukhānubhūtiś ca muktiḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: देहादेः सर्वतो मुक्ताः सर्वगं पुरुषोत्तमम् । प्राप्य तस्मिन् प्रविश्याथ मोदन्तेऽन्तर्बहिस्तथा ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: dehādeḥ sarvato muktāḥ sarvagaṃ puruṣottamam | prāpya tasmin praviśyātha modante'ntar bahis tathā ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Freed wholly from material bodies and veils, attaining the all-pervasive Puruṣottama, liberated souls rejoice inwardly and outwardly in eternal bliss.

meaningShort: Mokṣa is permanent release from Avidyā and Prakṛtic bondage through Paramātman's supreme grace, together with the unclouded manifestation and enjoyment of the soul's innate bliss.
meaningDeep: In Tattvavāda, Mokṣa is neither featureless dissolution of individuality nor mere negative absence of pain: retaining eternal personal distinctness (pañcabheda) and envy-free gradation (tāratamya), liberated souls enjoy Sālokya, Sāmīpya, Sārūpya, and Sāyujya in Vaikuṇṭha, Śvetadvīpa, and Anantāsana, overflowing with Parama-bhakti.

padaccheda.gloss: born of the supreme grace of Paramātman
total liberation from Prakṛti, Avidyā, and subtle bondage
and unimpeded experience of innate spiritual bliss

lakshanaDeva: प्रमाश्रयः प्रमाता । यथार्थज्ञानाश्रयश्चेतनः ।
lakshanaIast: pramāśrayaḥ pramātā | yathārthajñānāśrayaś cetanaḥ |
meaningShort: The Knower (Pramātā) is the conscious locus and subject in whom valid knowledge (pramā) inheres.
meaningDeep: In Tattvavāda epistemology, cognition never floats free without a real conscious subject (kartā/āśraya). Every sentient being — from the supreme omniscient Lord down to individual souls — is a real Pramātā whose Sākṣī guarantees the immediacy of self-awareness and truth-certitude.

padaccheda.gloss: the substratum or locus of valid cognition

lakshanaDeva: यथार्थज्ञानं प्रमितिः । केवला प्रमाणम् इति च ।
lakshanaIast: yathārthajñānaṃ pramitiḥ | kevalā pramāṇam iti ca |
meaningShort: Valid Cognition (Pramiti / Pramā) is knowledge that apprehends its object exactly as it exists in reality.
meaningDeep: Śrī Madhvācārya distinguishes Kevala-pramāṇa (valid cognition itself, i.e., Pramiti) from Anu-pramāṇa (the instrumental means such as perception, inference, and scripture that produce it). Unlike doubt (saṃśaya) or error (viparyaya), Pramiti is uncontradicted correspondence with the real (yathārthatva).

padaccheda.gloss: conforming to the object as it truly is

lakshanaDeva: प्रमितिविषयः प्रमेयम् । अनारोपितं तत्त्वमिति यावत् ।
lakshanaIast: pramitiviṣayaḥ prameyam | anāropitaṃ tattvam iti yāvat |
meaningShort: The Knowable (Prameya) is that which serves as the object of valid knowledge — coextensive with real existence (Tattva).
meaningDeep: Because valid cognition always reveals what truly is, 'being an object of valid knowledge' (pramiti-viṣayatva) and 'being real' (tattvatva) are coextensive in Tattvavāda. Supreme among all Prameyas is Bhagavān Viṣṇu, the ultimate purport of every Veda.

padaccheda.gloss: domain or object of valid knowledge
that which is rightly measurable / knowable (pra-√mā + -yat)

lakshanaDeva: तत्प्रतीतिजननयोग्यत्वं तात्पर्यम् । षड्भिर्लिङ्गैर्निर्णीतम् ।
lakshanaIast: tatpratītijananayogyatvaṃ tātparyam | ṣaḍbhir liṅgair nirṇītam |
meaningShort: Purport (Tātparya) is the objective fitness of a statement or text to generate coherent comprehension of a specific meaning, ascertained through the six hermeneutic canons.
meaningDeep: For Apauruṣeya Veda, where no human speaker's private wish exists, Tātparya is an objective semantic power established through the six Tātparya-liṅgas: upakrama-upasaṃhāra (opening and conclusion), abhyāsa (repetition), apūrvatā (novelty), phala (fruit), arthavāda (eulogy), and upapatti (rational fitness).

lakshanaDeva: तादात्म्यप्रतियोगिकोऽभावोऽन्योन्याभावः । धर्मस्वरूपो भेद एव ।
lakshanaIast: tādātmyapratiyogiko 'bhāvo 'nyonyābhāvaḥ | dharmasvarūpo bheda eva |
meaningShort: Mutual Non-Existence (Anyonyābhāva) is negation whose counterpositive is identity ('this is not that') — identical in Tattvavāda with the very essence (dharma-svarūpa) of each real entity.
meaningDeep: Unlike Nyāya, which treats Anyonyābhāva as a purely negative category separate from its locus, Śrī Madhvācārya demonstrates in Viṣṇutattvavinirṇaya that an entity's difference (bheda) from everything else is nothing other than its own positive essence (dharmi-svarūpa), differentiated without infinite regress via Viśeṣa.

lakshanaDeva: अन्योन्याभावभिन्नोऽभावः संसर्गाभावः । प्राक्प्रध्वंससदाभावभेदात् त्रिविधः ।
lakshanaIast: anyonyābhāvabhinno 'bhāvaḥ saṃsargābhāvaḥ | prākpradhvaṃsasadābhāvabhedāt trividhaḥ |
meaningShort: Relational Non-Existence (Saṃsargābhāva) is absence of occurrence or relation ('there is no pot on the ground'), comprising prior, posterior, and eternal non-existence.
meaningDeep: While Anyonyābhāva denies identity ('a pot is not a cloth'), Saṃsargābhāva denies relational presence and divides into three temporal modes: Prāgabhāva (prior absence before production), Pradhvaṃsābhāva (posterior absence after destruction), and Sadābhāva / Atyantābhāva (perpetual absence in all three times).

lakshanaDeva: पुरुषेण अर्थ्यते इति पुरुषार्थः । धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाश्चत्वारः ।
lakshanaIast: puruṣeṇa arthyate iti puruṣārthaḥ | dharmārthakāmamokṣāś catvāraḥ |
meaningShort: Puruṣārtha is that which is consciously sought by a sentient person — the fourfold canon of Dharma (righteousness), Artha (prosperity), Kāma (fulfillment), and Mokṣa (liberation).
meaningDeep: Classical śāstra arranges the four Puruṣārthas in an integrated hierarchy: Artha and Kāma remain wholesome only when governed by Dharma, while Dharma itself culminates in selfless devotion (Bhakti) to Viṣṇu and final liberation (Mokṣa — parama-puruṣārtha).

lakshanaDeva: धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ।
lakshanaIast: dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi bharatarṣabha |
meaningShort: Righteous Desire (Kāma) is aspiration, joy, and aesthetic fulfillment harmonized with Dharma — declared by Śrī Kṛṣṇa to be His own vibhūti.
meaningDeep: Whereas unbridled craving (kāma-krodha) binds the soul, Kāma that does not contravene Dharma sustains life, family, art, and ultimately turns into intense longing for Bhagavān (bhagavat-kāma).

lakshanaDeva: धर्ममूलो लोकयात्राहेतुः साधनसम्पदर्थपुरुषार्थः ।
lakshanaIast: dharmamūlo lokayātrāhetuḥ sādhanasampad arthapuruṣārthaḥ |
meaningShort: Artha (as a Puruṣārtha) is lawful material resource, polity, and sustenance rooted in Dharma that enables worldly life and charitable duty.
meaningDeep: In the Mahābhārata and Arthaśāstra traditions harmonized by Madhvācārya, wealth and governance have no autonomous license; acquired rightly and offered through yajña and dāna, Artha becomes an instrument of Dharma.

padaccheda.gloss: means of sustaining social and bodily life

lakshanaDeva: समत्वं योग उच्यते । योगश्चित्तवृत्तिनिरोधः । उपायो भगवत्प्राप्तौ योगः ।
lakshanaIast: samatvaṃ yoga ucyate | yogaś cittavṛttinirodhaḥ | upāyo bhagavatprāptau yogaḥ |
meaningShort: Yoga is inner equanimity in action, the stilling of restless mental modifications, and the disciplined spiritual means (upāya) of attaining Bhagavān.
meaningDeep: Derived from √yuj ('to yoke, concentrate, unite'), Yoga spans Karma-yoga (unattached performance of duty as worship), Aṣṭāṅga-dhyāna-yoga (one-pointed absorption), and Bhakti-yoga. In Gītābhāṣya, Madhvācārya glosses Yoga fundamentally as 'upāya' — the focused method leading to aparokṣa-jñāna of Viṣṇu.

padaccheda.gloss: evenness of mind in success and failure

lakshanaDeva: वेद्यतेऽनेन धर्मब्रह्मणी इति वेदः । अपौरुषेयं वाक्यम् ।
lakshanaIast: vedyate 'nena dharmabrahmaṇī iti vedaḥ | apauruṣeyaṃ vākyam |
meaningShort: The Veda (Śruti) is the unauthored (apauruṣeya) eternal corpus of sacred speech through which super-sensuous Dharma and supreme Brahman are known.
meaningDeep: From √vid ('to know'), the Veda comprises Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva saṃhitās along with their Brāhmaṇas, Āraṇyakas, and Upaniṣads. Being uncreated by any finite or infinite speaker and revealed identically in each cosmic cycle, its validity is intrinsic (svataḥ-pramāṇa).

lakshanaDeva: अथर्वणाङ्गिरोभिर्द्रष्टो ब्रह्मवेदः अथर्ववेदः ।
lakshanaIast: atharvaṇāṅgirobhir dṛṣṭo brahmavedaḥ atharvavedaḥ |
meaningShort: The Atharvaveda — the fourth canonical Veda beheld by the sages Atharvan and Aṅgiras, enshrining cosmic hymns and Upaniṣads such as Muṇḍaka, Māṇḍūkya, and Praśna.
meaningDeep: Serving as the canon of the supervising Brahmā priest in Vedic sacrifice, the Atharvaveda contains profound metaphysical sūktas (Skambha, Prāṇa, Pṛthivī) and three of the ten principal Upaniṣads commented upon directly by Śrī Madhvācārya.

padaccheda.gloss: by the seer-lineages of Atharvan and Aṅgiras
the Veda of the supervising Brahmā priest

lakshanaDeva: उपनीयात्मानं ब्रह्मणः सकाशं सादयत्यविद्यामिति उपनिषत् ।
lakshanaIast: upanīyātmānaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sakāśaṃ sādayaty avidyām iti upaniṣat |
meaningShort: Upaniṣad (Brahma-vidyā) is the sacred teaching seated near the Guru that leads the soul to Supreme Brahman and shatters spiritual ignorance.
meaningDeep: Built from upa ('near') + ni ('assuredly') + √sad ('to sit, loosen, destroy, attain'), Upaniṣad denotes both the wisdom of Brahman and the culminant Vedānta texts (Īśa, Kena, Kaṭha, Praśna, Muṇḍaka, Māṇḍūkya, Taittirīya, Aitareya, Chāndogya, Bṛhadāraṇyaka).

padaccheda.gloss: leading near (to the Guru and to Brahman)

lakshanaDeva: वर्णस्वरमात्राबलसामसान्तानप्रयोगोपदेशः शिक्षा । शिक्षा घ्राणं तु वेदस्य ।
lakshanaIast: varṇasvaramātrābalasāmasāntānaprayogopadeśaḥ śikṣā | śikṣā ghrāṇaṃ tu vedasya |
meaningShort: Śikṣā (Phonetics) is the first Vedāṅga teaching exact articulation of phonemes, pitch accents, vowel lengths, effort, and euphonic continuity.
meaningDeep: Celebrated in Taittirīya Upaniṣad 1.2 ('śīkṣāṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ: varṇaḥ svaraḥ mātrā balam sāma santānaḥ'), Śikṣā safeguards the sonic integrity of Vedic mantras across millennia without a single syllable's drift.

padaccheda.gloss: phoneme, pitch accent, and prosodic duration
articulatory effort, evenness, and sandhi junction

lakshanaDeva: वेदोदितकर्मणां आनुपूर्व्येण कल्पनाशास्त्रं कल्पः । हस्तौ कल्पोऽथ पठ्यते ।
lakshanaIast: vedoditakarmaṇām ānupūrvyeṇa kalpanāśāstraṃ kalpaḥ | hastau kalpo 'tha paṭhyate |
meaningShort: Kalpa is the Vedāṅga (likened to the two hands of the Veda) codifying the orderly performance of Vedic rites, domestic sacraments, geometry (Śulba), and Dharma.
meaningDeep: Divided into Śrauta, Gṛhya, Dharma, and Śulba sūtras, Kalpa translates Vedic injunctions into precise sacred action; in cosmology, 'kalpa' also denotes a single day of Caturmukha Brahmā spanning 1,000 mahāyugas.

padaccheda.gloss: of rites enjoined in the Veda

lakshanaDeva: व्याक्रियन्ते व्युत्पाद्यन्ते शब्दा अनेनेति व्याकरणम् । मुखं व्याकरणं स्मृतम् ।
lakshanaIast: vyākriyante vyutpādyante śabdā aneneti vyākaraṇam | mukhaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ smṛtam |
meaningShort: Vyākaraṇa (Grammar) — revered as the mouth of the Veda — is the generative science through which correct words are analyzed into roots (prakṛti) and affixes (pratyaya).
meaningDeep: Crowned by Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī (~4,000 algebraic sūtras), Kātyāyana's Vārttikas, and Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya, Sanskrit Vyākaraṇa is history's earliest formal generative system and an indispensable key to scriptural exegesis.

lakshanaDeva: अर्थावबोधे निरपेक्षतया पदजातं यत्रोक्तं तन्निरुक्तम् । निरुक्तं श्रोत्रमुच्यते ।
lakshanaIast: arthāvabodhe nirapekṣatayā padajātaṃ yatroktaṃ tan niruktam | niruktaṃ śrotram ucyate |
meaningShort: Nirukta (Etymology) — the ear of the Veda — is the science explaining why words signify their meanings by tracing every noun back to dynamic verbal roots (ākhyāta-ja).
meaningDeep: Codified by Yāska on the Vedic Nighaṇṭu, Nirukta provides the foundational principle wielded at full scale by Śrī Madhvācārya: because every Vedic word signifies sovereign attributes through root-meaning (mahāyoga), every name in the Veda ultimately proclaims Viṣṇu's infinite perfections.

padaccheda.gloss: for the comprehension of semantic meaning

lakshanaDeva: छन्दः पादौ तु वेदस्य । यदक्षरपरिमाणं तच्छन्दः । छादनात् छन्दः ।
lakshanaIast: chandaḥ pādau tu vedasya | yad akṣaraparimāṇaṃ tac chandaḥ | chādanāt chandaḥ |
meaningShort: Chandas (Prosody) — the two feet on which the Veda walks — is metered syllable-measure (such as Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Anuṣṭubh, and Bṛhatī) that shelters sacred meaning.
meaningDeep: Derived by Yāska and the Upaniṣads from √chad ('to cover, protect from mortality'), Chandas structures both Vedic sūktas via syllable count (akṣara-chandas) and classical kāvya via heavy-light cadence (guru-laghu vṛtta and mātrā).

padaccheda.gloss: because it shelters and clothes sacred truth

lakshanaDeva: ज्योतिषामयनं चक्षुः । कालविधानशास्त्रं ज्योतिषम् ।
lakshanaIast: jyotiṣām ayanaṃ cakṣuḥ | kālavidhānaśāstraṃ jyotiṣam |
meaningShort: Jyotiṣa (Astronomy & Mathematical Time-Reckoning) — the eye of the Veda — tracks the courses of sun, moon, and stars to determine sacred time.
meaningDeep: From jyotis ('luminary'), Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa of Lagadha and later Siddhānta treatises (Āryabhaṭa, Varāhamihira, Bhāskara) developed trigonometry, planetary motion models, and lunisolar intercalation for accurate temporal reckoning.

lakshanaDeva: अल्पाक्षरमसन्दिग्धं सारवद्विश्वतोमुखम् । अस्तोभमनवद्यं च सूत्रं सूत्रविदो विदुः ॥
lakshanaIast: alpākṣaram asandigdhaṃ sāravad viśvatomukham | astobham anavadyaṃ ca sūtraṃ sūtravido viduḥ ||
meaningShort: A Sūtra (Aphorism) is defined by six marks: minimal syllables, freedom from ambiguity, pregnant essence, universal applicability, zero filler particles, and faultlessness.
meaningDeep: Śrī Madhvācārya quotes this celebrated definition in his Brahmasūtrabhāṣya and Anuvyākhyāna, honoring Vedavyāsa's Brahmasūtras as the supreme 'nirṇāyaka' (decisive) thread stringing together all Vedic flowers.

lakshanaDeva: सूत्रार्थो वर्ण्यते यत्र पदैः सूत्रानुसारिभिः । स्वपदानि च वर्ण्यन्ते भाष्यं भाष्यविदो विदुः ॥
lakshanaIast: sūtrārtho varṇyate yatra padaiḥ sūtrānusāribhiḥ | svapadāni ca varṇyante bhāṣyaṃ bhāṣyavido viduḥ ||
meaningShort: A Bhāṣya (Primary Commentary) expounds the meaning of sūtras in phrasing faithful to the sūtras while also justifying and explaining its own interpretive terms.
meaningDeep: Śrī Madhvācārya authored four distinct commentaries on the Brahmasūtras alone (Brahmasūtrabhāṣya, Anuvyākhyāna, Nyāyavivaraṇa, and the terse 32-verse Aṇubhāṣya), exemplifying crystal-clear pramāṇa-grounded Bhāṣya craft.

padaccheda.gloss: by expressions faithful to the sūtra

lakshanaDeva: निरन्तरं पदव्याख्या यस्यां सा टीकेति स्मृता ।
lakshanaIast: nirantaraṃ padavyākhyā yasyāṃ sā ṭīketi smṛtā |
meaningShort: A Ṭīkā (Elucidative Sub-Commentary) unfolds the continuous word-by-word and logical import of a root text or Bhāṣya.
meaningDeep: In the Mādhva tradition, the title 'Ṭīkākāra' belongs uniquely to Śrī Jayatīrtha (1345–1388 CE), whose Nyāyasudhā and Tattvaprakāśikā unpacked every compressed sūtra and pramāṇa citation of Śrī Madhvācārya with unmatched dialectical grace.

padaccheda.gloss: commentary that makes hidden sense clear (√ṭīk)

lakshanaDeva: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणामुपदेशसमन्वितम् । पूर्ववृत्तं कथायुक्तमितिहासं प्रचक्षते ॥
lakshanaIast: dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇām upadeśasamanvitam | pūrvavṛttaṃ kathāyuktam itihāsaṃ pracakṣate ||
meaningShort: Itihāsa ('thus indeed it was' — iti-ha-āsa) is sacred historical epic narrating real past events woven with instruction in Dharma, Artha, Kāma, and Mokṣa.
meaningDeep: Comprising Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa and Vedavyāsa's Mahābhārata, Itihāsa together with Purāṇa amplifies and clarifies the Veda ('itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vedaṃ samupabṛṃhayet').

padaccheda.gloss: imbued with spiritual and ethical teaching

lakshanaDeva: सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च । वंशानुचरितं चैव पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् ॥
lakshanaIast: sargaś ca pratisargaś ca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca | vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam ||
meaningShort: A Purāṇa is characterized by five classical themes (pañca-lakṣaṇa): primary creation, secondary recreation, divine lineages, cycles of Manus, and deeds of royal dynasties.
meaningDeep: In the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (2.10.1), this expands to ten marks (daśa-lakṣaṇa) culminating in Āśraya — Supreme Viṣṇu as the sole independent refuge of all creation and liberation. Yāska also derives 'purāṇa' as 'purā navaṃ bhavati' — ancient yet ever fresh.

lakshanaDeva: महत्त्वाद्भारवत्त्वाच्च महाभारतमुच्यते । पञ्चमो वेद इत्युक्तः ।
lakshanaIast: mahattvād bhāravattvāc ca mahābhāratam ucyate | pañcamo veda ity uktaḥ |
meaningShort: The Mahābhārata — revered as the Fifth Veda — is so named for its vast magnitude (mahattva) and supreme spiritual weight (bhāravattva).
meaningDeep: In Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya, Śrī Madhvācārya reveals the three simultaneous semantic levels (trai-bhāṣā) of the Mahābhārata: āstika (historical narrative), manvādi (allegory of inner Dharma vs. Adharma led by Bhīma/Vāyu), and uparicara (every syllable proclaiming Nārāyaṇa's supremacy).

padaccheda.gloss: because of its vast scope (100,000 verses)
because of its profound philosophical weight

lakshanaDeva: रामस्यायनं चरितं यस्मिंस्तद् रामायणम् । वेदवेद्ये परे पुंसि जाते दशरथात्मजे ।
lakshanaIast: rāmasyāyanaṃ caritaṃ yasmiṃs tad rāmāyaṇam | vedavedye pare puṃsi jāte daśarathātmaje |
meaningShort: The Rāmāyaṇa ('the sacred course of Rāma') is the Ādikāvya in which the Veda itself manifested as poetry when the Supreme Person incarnated as Daśaratha's son.
meaningDeep: Śrī Madhvācārya opens Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya Chapters 3–9 with a luminous condensation of the Mūla-Rāmāyaṇa and Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, showing Rāma's spotless sovereignty and Hanumān's supreme bhakti and jñāna.

padaccheda.gloss: of Śrī Rāma, the Supreme Blissful Lord

lakshanaDeva: भगवता श्रीकृष्णेन गीता उपनिषत् भगवद्गीता । सर्वभारतार्थसङ्ग्रहः ।
lakshanaIast: bhagavatā śrīkṛṣṇena gītā upaniṣat bhagavadgītā | sarvabhāratārthasaṅgrahaḥ |
meaningShort: The Bhagavadgītā is the 700-verse Upaniṣad sung directly by Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa on Kurukṣetra, distilling the entire essence of the Veda and Mahābhārata.
meaningDeep: Śrī Madhvācārya dedicated two masterpieces to the Gītā — the Bhagavadgītābhāṣya and the Bhagavadgītātātparyanirṇaya — showing how detached svadharma, jñāna, and supreme bhakti unite without contradiction.

padaccheda.gloss: by the six-attribute-replete Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa

lakshanaDeva: चेतनेषु सर्वेषुोत्तमो भगवत्प्रियतमः प्राणनेता मुख्यप्राणः ।
lakshanaIast: cetaneṣu sarveṣūttamo bhagavatpriyatamaḥ prāṇanetā mukhyaprāṇaḥ |
meaningShort: Mukhyaprāṇa (Vāyu) is the supreme finite soul (Jīvottama) directly beneath Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī, presiding over vital breath, knowledge, strength, and devotion in every living being.
meaningDeep: Proclaimed in the Balittha Sūkta (Ṛgveda 1.141) and Chāndogya / Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣads, Mukhyaprāṇa incarnated in three epochs as Hanumān, Bhīmasena, and Ānandatīrtha (Śrī Madhvācārya) to uphold Tattvajñāna.

padaccheda.gloss: foremost, chief among all finite souls
leader of vital breath and spiritual vigor

englishGlosses: goddess of plenary speech and learning
lakshanaDeva: भृता विद्यावती वा वागभिमानिनी वायुपत्नी भारती ।
lakshanaIast: bhṛtā vidyāvatī vā vāgabhimāninī vāyupatnī bhāratī |
meaningShort: Bhāratī Devī — consort of Mukhyaprāṇa (Vāyu) — is the presiding deity of luminous speech, devotion, and plenary scriptural comprehension.
meaningDeep: Invoked alongside Iḷā and Sarasvatī in the Vedic Āprī hymns (Ṛgveda 1.13.9, 1.142.9), Bhāratī derives from bharata/bhāḥ ('radiance of knowledge') and stands alongside Sarasvatī at the pinnacle of Tāratamya below Brahmā-Vāyu.

padaccheda.gloss: rejoicing in the light of wisdom

lakshanaDeva: भगवदधीनेन जगत्सर्गकर्ता ऋजुगणज्येष्ठः चतुर्मुखो ब्रह्मा ।
lakshanaIast: bhagavadadhīnena jagatsargakartā ṛjugaṇajyeṣṭhaḥ caturmukho brahmā |
meaningShort: Caturmukha Brahmā (Hiraṇyagarbha) is the senior-most Ṛju soul appointed by Viṣṇu to fashion the manifest cosmos within the Brahmāṇḍa and impart the four Vedas.
meaningDeep: Tattvavāda carefully distinguishes 'Para-Brahman' (eternally independent Viṣṇu) from 'Kārya-Brahmā' (the four-faced soul sitting at the summit of finite Tāratamya, equal in rank to Mukhyaprāṇa, who attains sāyujya-mukti at the close of his hundred cosmic years).

padaccheda.gloss: entirely under the Sovereign Lord's power
four-faced reciter of the four Vedas

lakshanaDeva: वेदाल्मा विहगेश्वरो भगवद्वाहनः सुपर्णो गरुडः ।
lakshanaIast: vedātmā vihageśvaro bhagavadvāhanaḥ suparṇo garuḍaḥ |
meaningShort: Garuḍa (Suparṇa) is the Vedic eagle-lord whose wings embody the Sāman chants and who bears Bhagavān Viṣṇu across the cosmos.
meaningDeep: In Tāratamya, Garuḍa, Śeṣa, and Rudra stand immediately beneath Sarasvatī-Bhāratī. Derived from garut ('wing' of Vedic meter) + √ḍī ('to soar'), Garuḍa presides over citta/ahaṅkāra tattva in the cosmic hierarchy.

padaccheda.gloss: embodying the Vedic meters in his wings
he who soars on mighty wings

lakshanaDeva: कल्पान्तेऽपि शिष्यते भगवच्छय्यासनच्छत्ररूपः शेषः ।
lakshanaIast: kalpānte 'pi śiṣyate bhagavacchayyāsanacchatrarūpaḥ śeṣaḥ |
meaningShort: Śeṣa — the thousand-hooded lord who abides even at cosmic dissolution as Bhagavān's couch, throne, and canopy, and who upholds the earth and Vyākaraṇa (as Patañjali).
meaningDeep: Equal in Tāratamya rank with Garuḍa and Rudra, Śeṣa incarnates in service of the Lord as Lakṣmaṇa, Balarāma, and Patañjali (author of the Mahābhāṣya).

padaccheda.gloss: serpent-couch of Nārāyaṇa on the Milk Ocean

englishGlosses: auspicious lord of manas and cosmic dissolution
lakshanaDeva: रुजं द्रावयतीति रुद्रः । मनोऽभिमानी परमभागवतः शिवः ।
lakshanaIast: rujaṃ drāvayatīti rudraḥ | mano'bhimānī paramabhāgavataḥ śivaḥ |
meaningShort: Rudra (Śiva) — 'he who drives away sorrow and disease (rujaṃ drāvayati)' — is the presiding deity of Manas (mind), cosmic dissolution, and ascetic devotion to Viṣṇu.
meaningDeep: In Tattvavāda, Śiva is venerated alongside Garuḍa and Śeṣa as a supreme Vaiṣṇava ('vaiṣṇavānāṃ yathā śambhuḥ' — Bhāgavata 12.13.16); meanwhile, in supreme mahāyoga, Vedic names like 'Śiva' and 'Rudra' also signify Nārāyaṇa Himself as pure auspiciousness.

padaccheda.gloss: presiding deity of the mind principle

englishGlosses: goddess of wisdom and sacred river
lakshanaDeva: सरः प्रसरणं ज्ञानं तद्वती सरस्वती । चोदयित्री सूनृतानां चेतन्ती सुमतीनाम् ॥
lakshanaIast: saraḥ prasaraṇaṃ jñānaṃ tadvatī sarasvatī | codayitrī sūnṛtānāṃ cetantī sumatīnām ||
meaningShort: Sarasvatī — 'she who abounds in the flowing waters of wisdom (saras)' — is the Vedic inspirer of truthful, gracious speech and awakener of noble intellects.
meaningDeep: From √sṛ ('to flow') + -as (saras, 'flowing stream or expanse of knowledge') + -matup, Sarasvatī denotes the consort of Caturmukha Brahmā presiding over Vedic speech, the sacred Vedic river, and ultimately Bhagavān Himself as the ocean of all knowledge.

padaccheda.gloss: flowing stream of speech and knowledge (√sṛ)
of words that are both true and benevolent

lakshanaDeva: गायन्तं त्रायते यस्माद् गायत्रीत्यभिधीयते । गायत्री वा इदं सर्वं भूतं यदिदं किञ्च ॥
lakshanaIast: gāyantaṃ trāyate yasmād gāyatrīty abhidhīyate | gāyatrī vā idaṃ sarvaṃ bhūtaṃ yad idaṃ kiñca ||
meaningShort: Gāyatrī — 'that which protects and liberates (trāyate) the one who chants and meditates upon it (gāyantam)' — both the mother of Vedic meters and a name of Savitṛ-Nārāyaṇa.
meaningDeep: In Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.12 and Bṛhadāraṇyaka 5.14, Madhvācārya explains how 'Gāyatrī' primarily denotes Supreme Brahman dwelling inside the solar orb and inside the lotus of the heart, praised through Viśvāmitra's 24-syllable Tat-Savitur mantra (RV 3.62.10).

padaccheda.gloss: the saving Vedic meter and mantra

lakshanaDeva: सर्वस्य प्रसवितेति सविता । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ।
lakshanaIast: sarvasya prasaviteti savitā | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt |
meaningShort: Savitā (Savitṛ) — 'the Supreme Vivifier and Impeller of the entire universe' (√sū, prasava) who awakens and guides our intellects from within.
meaningDeep: While Savitā secondarily designates the solar deity Sūrya, Madhvācārya demonstrates in Ṛgbhāṣya (on RV 3.62.10) that the independent 'bhargaḥ' (radiant omniscient Lord) who impels even Sūrya and all intellects ('dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt') is Viṣṇu Himself.

padaccheda.gloss: of the entire cosmos and all souls
may He inspire and direct our understandings

englishGlosses: lord of cosmic order and waters
lakshanaDeva: वृणोतीति वरुणः । वरणीयतमो वा परमात्मा वरुणः ।
lakshanaIast: vṛṇotīti varuṇaḥ | varaṇīyatamo vā paramātman varuṇaḥ |
meaningShort: Varuṇa — 'He who envelops and regulates all worlds (vṛṇoti), and who is supremely worthy of choice (varaṇīya)' — guardian of Ṛta and waters, and in mahāyoga, Supreme Viṣṇu.
meaningDeep: From √vṛ ('to encompass, choose') + -unaन् (Uṇādi 3.53), Varuṇa presides over the western quarter, oceans, and moral-cosmic order (ṛta), while in Taittirīya Upaniṣad ('śaṃ no mitraḥ śaṃ varuṇaḥ') it also praises the all-enveloping Supreme Lord.

padaccheda.gloss: most worthy of being chosen and sought

lakshanaDeva: सूयते इति सोमः । उमायाः श्रियः पतिः सोमो वा परमात्मा ।
lakshanaIast: sūyate iti somaḥ | umāyāḥ śriyaḥ patiḥ somo vā paramātmā |
meaningShort: Soma — 'that which is pressed and distilled in Vedic sacrifice (√su)', the cooling Moon, and in mahāyoga 'Sa-Umā' — the Supreme Lord ever accompanied by Lakṣmī (Umā).
meaningDeep: Book 9 of the Ṛgveda (Pavamāna Maṇḍala) is devoted entirely to Soma; Madhvācārya and Yāska trace Soma both to √su ('to press out ambrosia / bring forth') and to sa + umā (the Lord united with Śrī/Lakṣmī, luminous wisdom).

padaccheda.gloss: is pressed forth as sacred ambrosia (√su)
ever united with Umā (Lakṣmī / Supreme Wisdom)

lakshanaDeva: श्रयति हरिं श्रयन्ते च तां मुक्ता इति श्रीः ।
lakshanaIast: śrayati hariṃ śrayante ca tāṃ muktā iti śrīḥ |
meaningShort: Śrī — 'She who eternally resorts to Hari alone, and to whom all liberated and noble beings resort for grace' (√śri, service and refuge).
meaningDeep: Celebrated in the Vedic Śrī-Sūkta, 'Śrī' denotes Mahālakṣmī (nitya-mukta, co-pervasive across space and time yet eternally devoted to Viṣṇu) and derivatively all spiritual luster, wisdom, royal dignity, and auspiciousness.

padaccheda.gloss: eternally serves and abides in Lord Hari (√śri)
all beings seek refuge in Her

lakshanaDeva: मायाः श्रियाः धवः पतिरिति माधवः । मौनाद्ध्यानाच्च योगाच्च विद्धि भारत माधवम् ॥
lakshanaIast: māyāḥ śriyāḥ dhavaḥ patir iti mādhavaḥ | maunād dhyānāc ca yogāc ca viddhi bhārata mādhavam ||
meaningShort: Mādhava — 'the eternal Consort (dhava) of Mā (Mahālakṣmī)', and He who is realized through contemplative silence (mauna), meditation (dhyāna), and yoga.
meaningDeep: The second of the twenty-four Keśavādi vyūha names, Mādhava unites two luminous derivations from the Mahābhārata (Udyogaparva 70.4) and Tantrasārasaṅgraha: Mā + dhava (Lord of Lakṣmī, Knowledge-Goddess) and Madhu-vidyā (Supreme Bliss known by sages).

padaccheda.gloss: of Mā, Goddess Lakṣmī (embodiment of measureless wisdom)

englishGlosses: bearer of Goddess Shri on His chest
lakshanaDeva: श्रियं वक्षसि धरतीति श्रीधरः ।
lakshanaIast: śriyaṃ vakṣasi dharatīti śrīdharaḥ |
meaningShort: Śrīdhara — 'He who bears Mahālakṣmī eternally upon His chest with supreme affection' (śrī + √dhṛ).
meaningDeep: One of the twelve monthly Āditya-Keśava forms, Śrīdhara signifies that all cosmic splendor, grace, and Vedic wisdom (Śrī) rest upon and are sustained solely by Viṣṇu.

lakshanaDeva: अधो न क्षीयते जातु यस्मात्तस्मादधोक्षजः । अक्षजं ऐन्द्रियं ज्ञानं तदधःकृतवान् वा ।
lakshanaIast: adho na kṣīyate jātu yasmāt tasmād adhokṣajaḥ | akṣajaṃ aindriyaṃ jñānaṃ tad adhaḥkṛtavān vā |
meaningShort: Adhokṣaja — 'He who never diminishes or falls downward (adho na kṣīyate), and before whom ordinary sense-born cognition (akṣaja) bows down without exhausting Him.'
meaningDeep: Expounded in Mahābhārata Udyogaparva (70.10) and Bhāgavata, Adhokṣaja captures Viṣṇu's dual majesty: completely unexhausted in sovereign fullness, and unreachable by ungraced material senses.

lakshanaDeva: इन्द्रस्यानुजो भूत्वा इन्द्रस्योपरि वर्तते इति उपेन्द्रः ।
lakshanaIast: indrasyānujo bhūtvā indrasyopari vartate iti upendraḥ |
meaningShort: Upendra — 'He who graciously appeared as Indra's younger brother (as Aditi's son Vāmana), and who simultaneously reigns supreme above (upari) Indra.'
meaningDeep: The Sanskrit prefix upa carries both proximity/younger-brotherhood (sāmīpya) and superiority (ādhikya), making Upendra a jewel of compact Sanskrit nirukti.

padaccheda.gloss: beside (as younger brother) and above (in supremacy)

lakshanaDeva: ज्ञानानन्दमयं देवं निर्मलस्फटिकाकृतिम् । आधारं सर्वविद्यानां हयग्रीवमुपास्महे ॥
lakshanaIast: jñānānandamayaṃ devaṃ nirmalasphaṭikākṛtim | ādhāraṃ sarvavidyānāṃ hayagrīvam upāsmahe ||
meaningShort: Hayagrīva — the crystal-radiant, horse-necked manifestation of Bhagavān Viṣṇu, constituted of pure consciousness and bliss, who rescued the Vedas and sustains all learning.
meaningDeep: Revered especially by Śrī Vādirāja Tīrtha and throughout the Pāñcarātra and Mahābhārata (Śāntiparva Hayagrīva-upākhyāna), 'haya' derives from √hi ('to impel knowledge forward'): He whose very voice breathes forth the uncreated Vedas.

padaccheda.gloss: whose essence is plenary knowledge and bliss
substratum of every branch of learning

lakshanaDeva: माद्यति मोदते प्रलयार्णवे वेदं गोपायतीति मत्स्यः ।
lakshanaIast: mādyati modate pralayārṇave vedaṃ gopāyatīti matsyaḥ |
meaningShort: Matsya — the inaugural Daśāvatāra who sports blissfully (mādyati/modate) across the cosmic deluge, retrieves the Vedas from Hayagrīva-daitya, and guides Vaivasvata Manu's ark.
meaningDeep: Derived from √mad ('to rejoice, delight'), Bhagavān's Matsya form demonstrates that even in universal dissolution His bliss is undiminished and His protection of Veda and satsajjanas never ceases.

padaccheda.gloss: amidst the waters of cosmic dissolution

lakshanaDeva: कौ उदके ऊर्मिषु तिष्ठन् मन्दरं धारयतीति कूर्मः ।
lakshanaIast: kau udake ūrmiṣu tiṣṭhan mandaraṃ dhārayatīti kūrmaḥ |
meaningShort: Kūrma — the second Daśāvatāra who effortlessly supported Mount Mandara on His vast shell within the Milk Ocean during the churning for Amṛta.
meaningDeep: Praised by Śrī Madhvācārya in Dvādaśastotra ('sukha-rūpa-tanū-manasā'calitaṃ mandaragiridhāriṇam'), Kūrma reveals Bhagavān as the unshakable foundation beneath every cosmic endeavor.

lakshanaDeva: वरान् अहन् दैत्यान् इति वराहः । वरम् आहरति महीं वेति वराहः ।
lakshanaIast: varān ahan daityān iti varāhaḥ | varam āharati mahīṃ veti varāhaḥ |
meaningShort: Varāha — 'He who struck down the arrogant demon Hiraṇyākṣa (varān ahan) and lifted up the precious Earth (varam āharati)' upon His tusk as Yajña-Varāha.
meaningDeep: Both Yāska (Nirukta 5.4) and the Bhāgavata (3.13–19) celebrate Varāha as the very embodiment of Vedic sacrifice (Yajña-puruṣa) whose every limb is a hymn, meter, and oblation.

padaccheda.gloss: retrieves and uplifts the choicest Earth (ā-√hṛ)

lakshanaDeva: परशुना दुष्टक्षत्रं निहत्य सज्जनान् रमयतीति परशुरामः ।
lakshanaIast: paraśunā duṣṭakṣatraṃ nihatya sajjanān ramayatīti paraśurāmaḥ |
meaningShort: Paraśurāma — the sage-warrior avatāra in the lineage of Bhṛgu who wielded the battle-axe (paraśu) to quell tyrannical rulers and bring peace and joy (rāma) to the righteous.
meaningDeep: Along the western coastal strip (Paraśurāma-kṣetra, including Udupi and Banavasi), Paraśurāma is especially revered as the establisher of sacred temples and protector of Vedic dharma.

padaccheda.gloss: with the gleaming axe of justice

lakshanaDeva: कल्कं कलिमलम् अस्यति नाशयतीति कल्किः ।
lakshanaIast: kalkaṃ kalimalam asyati nāśayatīti kalkiḥ |
meaningShort: Kalki — 'He who dispels the dross and spiritual darkness (kalka) of the Kali age' and re-inaugurates Kṛta-yuga righteousness.
meaningDeep: As the tenth Daśāvatāra foretold in Bhāgavata Purāṇa 12.2 and praised in Śrī Madhvācārya's Dvādaśastotra, Kalki embodies the certainty that adharma is temporally bounded and divine order always prevails.

englishGlosses: Lord standing on the brick for devotees
lakshanaDeva: विदा ज्ञानेन ठान् शून्यान् अज्ञानिनो लाति गृह्णाति अनुगृह्णातीति विट्ठलः ।
lakshanaIast: vidā jñānena ṭhān śūnyān ajñānino lāti gṛhṇāti anugṛhṇātīti viṭṭhalaḥ |
meaningShort: Viṭṭhala — 'He who through spiritual wisdom (vidā) graciously accepts and uplifts (lāti) even the destitute and ignorant (ṭhān)' — hands poised on His waist in Pandharpur.
meaningDeep: Celebrated across both the Haridāsa (Purandaradāsa, Vijayadāsa) and Vārkarī traditions, this classical akṣara-nirukti (vid + ṭha + √lā) illuminates how Supreme Brahman stands accessible to humble bhaktas.

padaccheda.gloss: those devoid of merit or knowledge (ekākṣara 'ṭha' = śūnya)

source.grantha: Padma Purāṇam & Haridāsa / Mādhva Nirukti Tradition
source.author: Purāṇa & Haridāsa Tradition

lakshanaDeva: सरति आकाशे इति सूर्यः । सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥
lakshanaIast: sarati ākāśe iti sūryaḥ | sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca ||
meaningShort: The Sun — the self-luminous celestial orb that courses across the firmament and animates all moving and stationary beings.
meaningDeep: Yāska derives `sūrya` in Nirukta 12.14 from √sṛ ('to move across space', `sarti ākāśe`), √sū ('to impel beings into action', `suvīrya` / `prasavitā`), or √svṛ ('to shine luminously'). Amarakośa (Digvarga) groups `sūrya` with `āditya`, `savitṛ`, `arka`, `bhānu`, `ravi`, `pūṣan`, and `divākara`. In Vedic and Tattvavāda exegesis (Ṛgbhāṣya & Chāndogyabhāṣya), Vivasvān Sūrya is the presiding deity of vision (`cakṣur-abhimānī`), while the supreme indwelling Ātman within the solar mandala is Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa (`ya eṣo'ntar āditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ`).

padaccheda.gloss: the Sun, impeller of light and life
vital principle of all that moves and stands

lakshanaDeva: चन्दति आह्लादयति लोकमिति चन्द्रः । हिमांशुश्चन्द्रमाश्चन्द्र इन्दुः कुमुदबान्धवः ॥
lakshanaIast: candati āhlādayati lokam iti candraḥ | himāṃśuś candramāś candra induḥ kumudabāndhavaḥ ||
meaningShort: The Moon — the cool-rayed celestial luminaire that gladdens living beings and nourishes night-blooming plants.
meaningDeep: Derived from √cadi ('āhlādane dīptau ca' — to gladden and shine softly; Nirukta 11.5), `candra` signifies cool, nectarous radiance in contrast to solar heat. Amarakośa lists `himāṃśu`, `candramas`, `indu`, `vidhu`, `soma`, `śaśadhara`, `niśāpati`, and `oṣadhīśa` (lord of medicinal herbs). In Puruṣasūkta (`candramā manaso jātaḥ`) and Madhvācārya's ontology, Soma-Candra presides over the human mind (`mano-'bhimānī`) and nourishes the plant kingdom with lunar `amṛta`.

padaccheda.gloss: delights the world with cool nectarous rays

lakshanaDeva: न क्षीयन्ते इति नक्षत्राणि । नक्षत्रमृक्षं भं तारा तारकाप्युडु वा स्त्रियाम् ॥
lakshanaIast: na kṣīyante iti nakṣatrāṇi | nakṣatram ṛkṣaṃ bhaṃ tārā tārakāpy uḍu vā striyām ||
meaningShort: A star or lunar mansion — an imperishable luminary fixed along the celestial ecliptic that marks cosmic time.
meaningDeep: In Nirukta 3.20 and Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, `nakṣatra` is traced either to √nakṣ ('gatikarman' — to traverse the vault) or `na kṣīyate` ('that which does not wane or perish from its station'). Amarakośa equates `nakṣatra` with `ṛkṣa`, `bha`, `tārā`, `tārakā`, and `uḍu`, designating both stars in general and the twenty-seven lunar asterisms (`aśvinī` to `revatī`) through which Candra measures months and seasons.

padaccheda.gloss: do not wane or slip from station (√kṣi)

lakshanaDeva: आसमन्तात् काशन्तेऽस्मिन् पदार्था इति आकाशः । शब्दगुणकमाकाशम् ॥
lakshanaIast: āsamantāt kāśante 'smin padārthā iti ākāśaḥ | śabdaguṇakam ākāśam ||
meaningShort: Space or ether — the all-encompassing expanse wherein all beings shine forth and whose distinctive attribute is sound.
meaningDeep: Derived from `ā` + √kāśṛ ('dīptau' — to shine all around), `ākāśa` is that open medium in which luminaries appear and bodies find room (`avakāśa-dātṛ`). Amarakośa (Vyomavarga) gives `vyoman`, `puṣkara`, `ambara`, `nabhas`, `antarikṣa`, `gagana`, `ananta`, and `kha`. Critically, Madhvācārya (Viṣṇutattvavinirṇaya & Tattvodyota) distinguishes eternal uncreated space (`avyākṛtākāśa`, locus of room) from the subtle created element `bhūtākāśa`, whose special quality (`viśeṣa-guṇa`) is `śabda` (Tarkasaṅgraha 14).

padaccheda.gloss: having sound (`śabda`) as its distinctive quality

lakshanaDeva: प्रथनात् पृथिवीत्याहुः । भूर्भूमिरचलानन्ता रसा विश्वम्भरा स्थिरा ॥
lakshanaIast: prathanāt pṛthivīty āhuḥ | bhūr bhūmir acalānantā rasā viśvambharā sthirā ||
meaningShort: The Earth — the broad, firm, all-sustaining terrestrial element characterized by stability and natural fragrance.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 1.14) derives `pṛthivī` from √prath ('vistāre' — to spread wide and firm: `prathanāt pṛthivī`). Amarakośa (Bhūmivarga) opens Kāṇḍa 2 with twenty-seven names including `bhū`, `bhūmi`, `acalā`, `viśvambharā`, `sthirā`, `dharā`, `dharitrī`, `dharaṇi`, `kṣiti`, and `vasundharā`. In Nyāya and Padārthasaṅgraha (`tatrādau gandhavatī pṛthivī`), earth is the dense mahābhūta distinguished by intrinsic `gandha` (fragrance) and presided over by Bhūdevī.

lakshanaDeva: शीतस्पर्शवत्यः आपः । आपः स्त्री भूम्नि वार्वारि सलिलं कमलं जलम् ॥
lakshanaIast: śītasparśavatyaḥ āpaḥ | āpaḥ strī bhūmni vār vāri salilaṃ kamalaṃ jalam ||
meaningShort: Water — the cool-touching, life-sustaining liquid element that flows, cleanses, and binds forms together.
meaningDeep: Lexically derived from √jal ('ghāte / āvaraṇe' — to cool heat or envelop thirst) alongside Vedic `ap` (always feminine plural `āpaḥ`, from √āp 'to pervade'), `jala` is catalogued in Amarakośa (Vārivarga) with `vāri`, `salila`, `payaḥ`, `kīlāla`, `amṛta`, `jīvana` ('life itself'), `bhuvana`, `udaka`, and `toya`. In Nyāya and Tattvavāda (`śītasparśavatyo āpaḥ`, TS 11), water possesses natural fluidity (`sāṃsiddhika-dravatva`), cool touch, and viscous cohesion (`sneha`), presided over by Varuṇa.

padaccheda.gloss: waters endowed with naturally cool touch

lakshanaDeva: उष्णस्पर्शवत् तेजः । तच्च चतुर्विधं भौमं दिव्यमौदर्यमाकरजं चेति ॥
lakshanaIast: uṣṇasparśavat tejaḥ | tac ca caturvidhaṃ bhaumaṃ divyam audaryam ākarajaṃ ceti ||
meaningShort: Luminous fire or radiance — the element of hot touch and brilliant color, manifesting as earthly flame, solar light, digestive heat, and mineral gold.
meaningDeep: From √tij ('niśāne' — to sharpen, kindle, blaze keenly), `tejas` denotes both the cosmic element of fire-light and spiritual splendor (`varcas`). Padārthasaṅgraha and Tarkasaṅgraha (12) define `tejas` as `uṣṇasparśavat` with dazzling white-bright color (`bhāsvara-śukla-rūpa`), dividing it into four domains: `bhauma` (terrestrial fire), `divya` (solar and lightning brilliance), `audarya` (digestive `vaiśvānara` fire), and `ākaraja` (lustrous metals like `suvarṇa`). In Bhagavadgītā 7.9, Kṛṣṇa declares `tejaś cāsmi vibhāvasau`.

padaccheda.gloss: the radiant element characterized by hot touch
digestive warmth and mine-born metallic gold

lakshanaDeva: वाति गच्छति इति वायुः । रूपरहितस्पर्शवान् वायुः ॥
lakshanaIast: vāti gacchati iti vāyuḥ | rūparahitasparśavān vāyuḥ ||
meaningShort: Wind or air — the invisible, ceaselessly moving atmospheric element known through touch and motion.
meaningDeep: Derived by Yāska (Nirukta 10.1) from √vā ('gatigandhanayoḥ' — to blow, move, and carry scent), `vāyu` is catalogued in Amarakośa (Svargavarga) alongside `śvasana`, `sparśana`, `mātariśvan`, `sadāgati`, `pṛṣadaśva`, `gandhavaha`, `anila`, `pavana`, and `marut`. Philosophically (`rūparahitaḥ sparśavān vāyuḥ`, TS 13), air lacks visible color yet bears temperate touch (`anuṣṇāśīta-sparśa`); in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tattvavāda, Mukhyaprāṇa Vāyu stands at the apex of finite souls (`jīvottama`), sustaining both cosmic motion (`pravaha`) and inward breath (`prāṇa`).

padaccheda.gloss: called `vāyu` because it blows and courses ceaselessly (√vā)
devoid of visible color or form

lakshanaDeva: मेहति सिञ्चति भूमिं जलेन इति मेघः । अभ्रं मेघो वारिवाहः स्तनयित्नुर्बलाहकः ॥
lakshanaIast: mehati siñcati bhūmiṃ jalena iti meghaḥ | abhraṃ megho vārivāhaḥ stanayitnur balāhakaḥ ||
meaningShort: A cloud — the sky-borne water-bearer that sprinkles the earth with life-giving rain.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 2.21: `meghaḥ kasmāt? mehatīti sataḥ`) derives `megha` from √mih ('secane' — to sprinkle or pour down moisture). Amarakośa (Vyomavarga) records `abhra`, `megha`, `vārivāha`, `stanayitnu`, `balāhaka`, `dhārādhara`, `jaladhara`, `taḍitvān`, `vārida`, `ambubhṛt`, and `jīmūta` — famously illustrating how adding `-da` ('giver') or `-dhara` ('bearer') to words for water yields cloud-synonyms. In Sanskrit *kāvya* (as in Kālidāsa's *Meghadūta*), the dark monsoon cloud is the archetypal herald of renewal and longing.

padaccheda.gloss: sprinkles and showers water upon the earth (√mih)

lakshanaDeva: वृष्यते सिच्यतेऽनया भूमिरिति वृष्टिः । अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ॥
lakshanaIast: vṛṣyate sicyate 'nayā bhūmir iti vṛṣṭiḥ | annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād annasambhavaḥ ||
meaningShort: Rain or shower — the sky-born downpour that moistens the soil and brings forth grain for all living creatures.
meaningDeep: Formed from √vṛṣ ('secane' — to rain, pour forth, engender fertility) with the feminine action suffix `-ktin` (Pāṇini 3.3.94), `vṛṣṭi` is paired in Amarakośa (Vyomavarga: `vṛṣṭir varṣaṃ`) with `āsāra` (driving torrent) and `śīkara` (fine spray). Bhagavadgītā 3.14 (`parjanyād annasambhavaḥ; yajñād bhavati parjanyaḥ`) situates `vṛṣṭi` at the heart of the cosmic wheel of reciprocity uniting human `yajña`, celestial gods, rainfall, harvests, and embodied life.

padaccheda.gloss: that whereby the earth is watered and fertilized (√vṛṣ)
from rain-clouds arises the sustenance of grain

lakshanaDeva: विद्योतते निमेषार्धमिति विद्युत् । तडित्सौदामिनी विद्युच्चञ्चला चपला अपि ॥
lakshanaIast: vidyotate nimeṣārdham iti vidyut | taḍit saudāminī vidyuc cañcalā capalā api ||
meaningShort: Lightning — the instantaneous celestial flash that blazes across storm-clouds in half the blink of an eye.
meaningDeep: Derived from `vi` + √dyut ('dīptau' — to flash vividly; Nirukta 7.21), `vidyut` is celebrated in Amarakośa (Vyomavarga) under evocative feminine epithets: `śampā`, `śatahradā`, `hrādinī`, `airāvatī`, `kṣaṇaprabhā` ('instant-gleam'), `taḍit`, `saudāminī`, `cañcalā`, and `capalā`. In Kena Upaniṣad 4.4 (`yad etad vidyuto vyadyutad ā itīn nyamīmiṣat`) and Nārāyaṇa Sūkta (`nīlatoyadamadhyasthā vidyullekheva bhāsvarā`), lightning serves as the supreme Upaniṣadic simile (`upamā`) for sudden, self-luminous spiritual illumination.

lakshanaDeva: समुद्रवन्त्यस्मादापः अभिद्रवन्त्येनं नद्य इति वा समुद्रः । समुद्रोऽब्धिरकूपारः पारावारः सरित्पतिः ॥
lakshanaIast: samudravanty asmād āpaḥ abhidravanty enaṃ nadya iti vā samudraḥ | samudro 'bdhir akūpāraḥ pārāvāraḥ saritpatiḥ ||
meaningShort: The ocean — the boundless, unfathomable treasury of waters into which all rivers flow without disturbing its fullness.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 2.10) derives `samudra` from `sam` + `ud` + √dru ('to surge upward with vapor') or `sam` + √und ('to moisten thoroughly'). Amarakośa (Vārivarga) supplies `abdhi`, `akūpāra`, `pārāvāra`, `saritpati` ('lord of rivers'), `udadhi`, `sindhu`, `sāgara`, `arṇava`, and `ratnākara` ('mine of jewels'). In Bhagavadgītā 2.70 (`āpūryamāṇam acalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat`) and Madhvācārya's `Samudra-stuti`, the ocean exemplifies bottomless serenity (`gāmbhīrya`) and plenitude.

padaccheda.gloss: waters surge up and gather completely (sam + ud + √dru / √und)
spanning near and far shores, lord of all rivers

lakshanaDeva: नदति शब्दायते इति नदी । तरङ्गिणी शैवलिनी तटिनी ह्रदिनी धुनी ॥
lakshanaIast: nadati śabdāyate iti nadī | taraṅgiṇī śaivalinī taṭinī hradinī dhunī ||
meaningShort: A river — a resonant, ever-flowing stream descending from mountain heights toward its union with the ocean.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 2.24: `nadyāḥ kasmāt? nadanā imā bhavanti śabdavatyaḥ`) derives `nadī` from √nad ('avyakte śabde' — to murmur and resound while coursing). Amarakośa (Vārivarga) lists `sarit` (from √sṛ, 'the flowing one'), `taraṅgiṇī`, `śaivalinī`, `taṭinī`, `hradinī`, `dhunī`, `srotasvinī`, `āpagā`, and `nimnagā` ('descending toward low ground'). Upaniṣadic philosophy (Muṇḍaka 3.2.8; Praśna 6.5) invokes rivers entering the sea — where Madhvācārya's bhāṣya carefully shows that the rivers remain ontologically real even when indistinguishable by ordinary gaze.

padaccheda.gloss: murmurs and resounds as it flows (√nad)

lakshanaDeva: सरति प्रसरति जलमत्रेति सरः । पद्माकरस्तडागोऽस्त्री कासारः सरसी सरः ॥
lakshanaIast: sarati prasarati jalam atreti saraḥ | padmākaras taḍāgo 'strī kāsāraḥ sarasī saraḥ ||
meaningShort: A lake or lotus-pool — a tranquil expanse of fresh water bordered by banks and teeming with aquatic blossoms.
meaningDeep: Formed from √sṛ ('gatau' — where ripples gently spread) with the neuter Uṇādi suffix `-asun`, `saras` denotes a natural or excavated body of clear water. Amarakośa (Vārivarga) groups `padmākara` ('mine of lotuses'), `taḍāga` (so called because waves strike its shore, `taṭam āhanti`), `kāsāra`, `sarasī`, `saras`, and `puṣkariṇī`. In Bhagavadgītā 10.24 (`sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ`) and classical poetry, a limpid autumn lake (`śaratsaras`) mirrors a mind stilled of turbidity (`prasāda`).

lakshanaDeva: तरति गच्छति अम्बुनि इति तरङ्गः । भङ्गस्तरङ्ग ऊर्मिर्वा स्त्रियां वीचिरथोत्कलिका ॥
lakshanaIast: tarati gacchati ambuni iti taraṅgaḥ | bhaṅgas taraṅga ūrmir vā striyāṃ vīcir athotkalikā ||
meaningShort: A wave or ripple — the rhythmic undulation coursing across the surface of rivers, lakes, and seas.
meaningDeep: Derived from √tṝ ('plavanataraṇayoḥ' — to cross or skim across water) with the Uṇādi suffix `-aṅgac`, `taraṅga` is paired in Amarakośa (Vārivarga) with `bhaṅga`, `ūrmi`, `vīci` (gentle wavelet), and `kallola` / `ullola` (towering ocean billow). In Nyāya epistemology (`vīcitaraṅga-nyāya`), concentric ripples expanding from a stone dropped in water explain how sound (`śabda`) propagates serially across `ākāśa` from source to ear.

padaccheda.gloss: skims and courses across the water (√tṝ)

lakshanaDeva: पर्ववान् इति पर्वतः । अद्रिर्गोत्रो गिरिर्ग्रावा शैलः शिलोच्चयः ॥
lakshanaIast: parvavān iti parvataḥ | adrir gotro girir grāvā śailaḥ śiloccayaḥ ||
meaningShort: A mountain — a majestic, immovable mass of tiered rock and ridges that anchors the earth and gathers rainclouds.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 1.20: `parvavān parvataḥ; parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇāter vā`) explains `parvata` as possessing `parvans` — massive joints, tiers, or ridges of stone. Amarakośa (Śailavarga) compiles `adri`, `gotra`, `giri`, `grāvan`, `śaila`, `śiloccaya`, `mahīdhra`, `bhūbhṛt` ('earth-supporter'), `ahārya`, `dhara`, and `acala` ('immovable'). In Nyāya logic (`parvato vahnimān dhūmāt`), the mountain is the canonical `pakṣa` of syllogistic inference, while in Bhagavadgītā 10.25 (`sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ`) it embodies unshakable steadiness.

padaccheda.gloss: possessing massive tiers and rocky joints (`parvan`)
rocky peak, towering mass of stone

lakshanaDeva: शिलति संहता भवति इति शिला । पाषाणप्रस्तरग्रावोपलाश्मानः शिला दृषत् ॥
lakshanaIast: śilati saṃhatā bhavati iti śilā | pāṣāṇaprastaragrāvopalāśmānaḥ śilā dṛṣat ||
meaningShort: A stone or rock — a dense, enduring mineral mass forming mountain crags, riverbeds, and sacred sculpted icons.
meaningDeep: Derived from √śil ('samādhau / saṅghāte' — to cohere firmly into a compact mass), `śilā` is grouped in Amarakośa (Śailavarga) with `pāṣāṇa`, `prastara`, `grāvan` (Vedic pressing-stone), `upala`, `aśman`, and `dṛṣad`. In Sanskrit epigraphy and education, `śilā-lekhā` ('inscription on stone') is the emblem of indelible permanence (`pāṣāṇa-rekhā`), while sacred river-worn `śālagrāma-śilā` stones are revered in Vaiṣṇava worship as self-manifest (`svayam-vyakta`) loci of Bhagavān Viṣṇu's presence.

padaccheda.gloss: coheres into a hard, compact mass

lakshanaDeva: गूहति संवृणोति इति गुहा । दरी तु कन्दरो वा स्त्री गुहा गेहं देवखातबिले ॥
lakshanaIast: gūhati saṃvṛṇoti iti guhā | darī tu kandaro vā strī guhā gehaṃ devakhātabile ||
meaningShort: A cave or cavern — a natural hollow in a mountain crag, and metaphorically the secret chamber of the spiritual heart.
meaningDeep: Derived from √guhū ('saṃvaraṇe' — to conceal, shelter, enclose) with suffix `-aṅ` + `-ṭāp` (Pāṇini 3.3.104), `guhā` signifies a sheltered natural recess (`devakhāta-bila`, 'hollow carved by nature, not human chisels'). Amarakośa (Śailavarga) pairs `guhā` with `darī`, `kandara`, and `gahvara`. Across Kaṭha Upaniṣad (`guhāṃ praviṣṭau paramē parārdhe`, 1.3.1) and Taittirīya Upaniṣad (`yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyām`, 2.1.1), `hṛdaya-guhā` designates the innermost sanctuary of consciousness where both `jīva` and `Paramātman` abide.

padaccheda.gloss: in a naturally hollowed mountain grotto

lakshanaDeva: वन्यते सेव्यते तापसैर्मृगैश्चेति वनम् । अटव्यरण्यं विपिनं गहनं काननं वनम् ॥
lakshanaIast: vanyate sevyate tāpasair mṛgaiś ceti vanam | aṭavy araṇyaṃ vipinaṃ gahanaṃ kānanaṃ vanam ||
meaningShort: A forest or grove — an untamed woodland sanctuary of trees, wildlife, and contemplative hermitages.
meaningDeep: Derived from √van ('sambhaktau' — to be cherished, resorted to, or abundantly fruitful; Nirukta 8.3), `vana` also carries the secondary sense of water and radiance in Vedic diction. Amarakośa (Vanauṣadhivarga) opens its botanical lexicon with `aṭavī`, `araṇya`, `vipina`, `gahana`, `kānana`, and `vana`, distinguishing wild forests from planted gardens (`udyāna`, `upavana`). In Indian civilization, the `vana` / `āraṇya` is the cradle of the Āraṇyakas, Upaniṣadic contemplation, and Vānaprastha serenity.

padaccheda.gloss: resorted to and cherished by sages and creatures (√van)

lakshanaDeva: वृश्च्यते छिद्यते इति वृक्षः । वृक्षो महीरुहः शाखी विटपी पादपस्तरुः ॥
lakshanaIast: vṛścyate chidyate iti vṛkṣaḥ | vṛkṣo mahīruhaḥ śākhī viṭapī pādapas taruḥ ||
meaningShort: A tree — a rooted, branching plant organism that drinks water through its roots and offers shade, blossoms, and fruit.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 2.6: `vṛkṣo vraścanāt`) derives `vṛkṣa` from √ovraścū ('chedane' — that which is felled or pruned for timber and sacred fuel) or √vṛ ('to cover the ground with shade'). Amarakośa (Vanauṣadhivarga) reveals a botanical anatomy through its synonyms: `mahīruha` ('sprouting from earth'), `śākhin` ('branch-bearer'), `viṭapin` ('bough-crowned'), `pādapa` ('drinking sap with its root-feet'), `taru` ('carrying creatures through heat'), `anokaha`, `kuṭa`, `śāla`, `palāśin`, and `druma`. Subhāṣitas revere trees as `satpuruṣā iva` — standing in scorching sun while shielding others in shade.

lakshanaDeva: मूलति प्रतिष्ठति अनेन तरुरिति मूलम् । मूलं बुध्नोऽङ्घ्रिनामकः आद्ये च कारणे मूलम् ॥
lakshanaIast: mūlati pratiṣṭhati anena tarur iti mūlam | mūlaṃ budhno 'ṅghrināmakaḥ ādye ca kāraṇe mūlam ||
meaningShort: A root or foundation — the subterranean anchor through which a plant draws nourishment, and by extension the primal cause or original text.
meaningDeep: Derived from √mūl ('pratiṣṭhāyām' — to stand firmly grounded), `mūla` denotes both the botanical root (`budhna`, `śiphā`, `pāda`) in Amarakośa 2.4.11 and, in Nānārthavarga (3.3), first origin (`ādya`), primary capital, and foundational scripture (`mūla-grantha`, as in Śrī Madhvācārya's thirty-seven *Sarvamūla Granthāḥ*). Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.3.1 and Bhagavadgītā 15.1 (`ūrdhvamūlam adhaḥśākham`) invert the tree metaphor to portray Brahman as the transcendent Root (`ūrdhva-mūla`) sustaining the cosmic `aśvattha`.

padaccheda.gloss: also signifying primal origin and root cause

lakshanaDeva: शाखति व्याप्नोति आकाशमिति शाखा । खशया रौहिणेयादिः शाखा वेदविभागयोः ॥
lakshanaIast: śākhati vyāpnoti ākāśam iti śākhā | khaśayā rauhiṇeyādiḥ śākhā vedavibhāgayoḥ ||
meaningShort: A branch or bough — a tree limb spreading into open space, and secondarily a traditional recensional school of the Vedas.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 6.32: `śākhā khaśayā bhavati, śaknoter vā`) ingeniously explains `śākhā` as `kha-śayā` ('resting in the sky') or from √śak / √śākh ('vyāptau' — to spread abroad). Amarakośa records `śākhā` both in Vanauṣadhivarga (2.4.11, alongside `latā` and `viṭapa`) and in Nānārthavarga (3.3.19) for tree-limbs, arms, and the living oral recensions (`śākhāḥ`, such as Śākala, Taittirīya, Kāṇva) through which the one eternal Veda branches out among sage lineages.

padaccheda.gloss: Nirukta etymon: reposing in the sky (`kha`)
signifying both tree-bough and Vedic recension

lakshanaDeva: पृणाति पूरयति तरुशोभामिति पर्णम् । पत्रं पलाशं छदनं दलं पर्णं छदः पुमान् ॥
lakshanaIast: pṛṇāti pūrayati taruśobhām iti parṇam | patraṃ palāśaṃ chadanaṃ dalaṃ parṇaṃ chadaḥ pumān ||
meaningShort: A leaf — the green, sun-catching blade of foliage that clothes and nourishes a plant.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 4.3: `parṇaṃ patanāt`) connects `parṇa` to √pat ('to flutter and fall seasonally') or √pṝ ('pālanapūraṇayoḥ' — to fill out and sustain the tree). Amarakośa (Vanauṣadhivarga) unites `patra` (also meaning manuscript leaf and bird-wing), `palāśa` (verdant blade), `chadana` / `chada` ('protective canopy'), `dala` ('unfolding petal/leaf'), and `parṇa`. In Bhagavadgītā 9.26 (`patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ`) and 15.1 (`chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni`), the humble leaf represents both pure devotional offering and Vedic meter.

padaccheda.gloss: fills out and sustains the tree's vitality (√pṝ)

lakshanaDeva: पुष्यति विकसति इति पुष्पम् । स्त्रियाम् बहुत्वे सुमनसः पुष्पं प्रसूनं कुसुमं सुमम् ॥
lakshanaIast: puṣyati vikasati iti puṣpam | striyām bahutve sumanasaḥ puṣpaṃ prasūnaṃ kusumaṃ sumam ||
meaningShort: A flower or blossom — the fragrant, unfolding bloom of a plant that heralds fruitfulness and graces worship.
meaningDeep: Derived from √puṣp ('vikasane' — to unfold, bloom, expand in beauty) with suffix `-pa`, `puṣpa` is listed in Amarakośa (Vanauṣadhivarga) alongside `sumanasaḥ` (feminine plural, 'gladdening the heart'), `prasūna` ('newly brought forth'), `kusuma`, and `suma`. Beyond natural botany and spring aesthetics (`puṣpasamaya` = `vasanta`), Sanskrit ethics celebrates the eight inward flowers (`aṣṭa-puṣpikā`) dearest to Viṣṇu — headed by `ahiṃsā`, `indriya-nigraha`, `dayā`, `kṣamā`, and `jñāna`.

lakshanaDeva: पद्यते जले शेते विकसति वा सूर्यकरैरिति पद्मम् । वा पुंसि पद्मं नलिनमरविन्दं महोत्पलम् ॥
lakshanaIast: padyate jale śete vikasati vā sūryakarair iti padmam | vā puṃsi padmaṃ nalinam aravindaṃ mahotpalam ||
meaningShort: The sacred day-lotus — rooted in mud yet rising unstained above the water to blossom at the touch of sunlight.
meaningDeep: Derived from √pad ('gatau' — rising cleanly from muddy depths) with Uṇādi `-man`, `padma` receives one of the richest synonym clusters in Amarakośa (Vārivarga 1.10.40–43): `nalina`, `aravinda`, `mahotpala`, `sahasrapatra`, `kamala`, `śatapatra`, `kuśeśaya`, `paṅkeruha` / `paṅkaja` ('mud-born'), `tāmarasa`, `sārasa`, `ambhoja`, and `rājīva`. In Bhagavadgītā 5.10 (`padmapatram ivāmbhasā`) its water-repellent leaf models detached action, while in Tattvavāda iconography it is the abode of Mahālakṣmī (`Padmā`) and emblem of Padmanābha.

padaccheda.gloss: rises in water and unfolds at solar rays (√pad)

lakshanaDeva: फलति निष्पद्यते इति फलम् । फलं सस्ये कृतार्थत्वे हेतुजाते च तद्वति ॥
lakshanaIast: phalati niṣpadyate iti phalam | phalaṃ sasye kṛtārthatve hetujāte ca tadvati ||
meaningShort: Fruit or result — the ripened seed-bearing produce of a tree, and universally the matured outcome of an action or cause.
meaningDeep: Derived from √phal ('niṣpattau' — to ripen, burst into fruition, succeed) with suffix `-ac` (Pāṇini 3.1.134), `phala` bridges nature and moral philosophy. Amarakośa treats botanical ripe fruit (`āma` = unripe, `pakva` = ripe `phala`) in Vanauṣadhivarga (2.4.18) and its semantic range — grain/crop (`sasya`), fulfillment (`kṛtārthatva`), and causal outcome (`hetujāta`) — in Nānārthavarga. Bhagavadgītā 2.47 (`karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana`) immortalizes `phala-tyāga` — performing duty as worship of Hari without selfish attachment to reward.

padaccheda.gloss: ripens and comes to mature completion (√phal)
in the sense of ripened produce and fulfilled purpose
and any effect born of a prior cause

lakshanaDeva: जायतेऽस्मादङ्कुर इति बीजम् । बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् ॥
lakshanaIast: jāyate 'smād aṅkura iti bījam | bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam ||
meaningShort: A seed or germ — the concentrated kernel inside a fruit that holds latent life and sprouts into a new organism.
meaningDeep: Traced by classical commentators (`vi` + √jan 'to generate anew' with loss of `-n` and vowel lengthening, `vijāyate 'smāt`) to the generative potency within every plant and lineage, `bīja` is defined in Amarakośa (Nānārthavarga) as `kāraṇa` (seminal cause), agricultural grain-seed, and germinal essence. In philosophical argument (`bījāṅkura-nyāya`), seed and sprout illustrate beginningless cyclical succession, while in Bhagavadgītā 7.10 and 10.39 (`yac cāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tad aham arjuna`), Bhagavān declares Himself the eternal efficient-animating Ground without whom nothing can germinate.

padaccheda.gloss: that from which the new sprout springs forth (vi + √jan)
the seminal germ of all beings

lakshanaDeva: लतति वेष्टते तरुमिति लता । वल्ली तु व्रततिर्लता प्रतानिनी वीरुध् च सा ॥
lakshanaIast: latati veṣṭate tarum iti latā | vallī tu vratatir latā pratāninī vīrudh ca sā ||
meaningShort: A creeper or climbing vine — a slender, supple plant that twines gracefully around a supporting tree.
meaningDeep: Derived from √lat ('veṣṭane / bālye' — to twine gracefully, sway tenderly), `latā` is grouped in Amarakośa (Vanauṣadhivarga) with `vallī`, `vallarī`, `vratati` (from √vṛt, 'winding upward'), `pratāninī` (tendril-spreading), and `vīrudh`. In Sanskrit poetics and devotional philosophy, `latā-vṛkṣa-nyāya` symbolizes delicate grace (`saukumārya`) and steadfast reliance — just as a flowering vine climbs skyward only by clasping an unshakable `kalpavṛkṣa`, the dependent `jīva` ascends through `bhakti-latā` clinging to the Supreme Lord.

padaccheda.gloss: twines and climbs around a supporting tree
twining vine, winding climber, supple creeper

lakshanaDeva: तृह्यते भक्ष्यते पशुभिरिति तृणम् । शष्पं बालतृणं घासो यवसं तृणमर्जुनम् ॥
lakshanaIast: tṛhyate bhakṣyate paśubhir iti tṛṇam | śaṣpaṃ bālatṛṇaṃ ghāso yavasaṃ tṛṇam arjunam ||
meaningShort: Grass or herbage — a humble blade of meadow turf that carpets the earth and sustains grazing creatures.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 1.12: `tṛṇaṃ tardanāt`) derives `tṛṇa` from √tṛd / √tṛh ('to prick upward through soil or be grazed by cattle'). Amarakośa (Vanauṣadhivarga, `tṛṇavarga` section) distinguishes tender young shoots (`śaṣpa`), meadow fodder (`ghāsa`, `yavasa`), sacred `darbha` / `kuśa`, and resilient `dūrvā` grass. In Kena Upaniṣad 3.4–10, Agni cannot burn nor Vāyu lift a single `tṛṇa` placed before them by Brahman — a famous parable quoted across Madhvācārya's works to prove that every finite agent's power depends wholly upon Paramātman.

padaccheda.gloss: grazed by animals or piercing upward from soil (√tṛh / √tṛd)

lakshanaDeva: उच्छति विवास्यति तम इति उषाः । प्रत्यूषोऽहर्मुखं कल्पमुषःप्रत्युषसी अपि ॥
lakshanaIast: ucchati vivāsyati tama iti uṣāḥ | pratyūṣo 'harmukhaṃ kalpam uṣaḥpratyuṣasī api ||
meaningShort: Dawn — the radiant flush of daybreak that dispels nocturnal darkness and awakens all living beings to action.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 2.18: `uṣāḥ kasmāt? ucchatīti satyāḥ`) derives `uṣas` from √vas ('vibhāte' — `ucchati`, to shine forth and banish gloom). Amarakośa (Kālavarga) pairs `uṣas` with `pratyūṣa`, `aharmukha` ('face of the day'), `kalpa`, and `prabhāta`. Celebrated in twenty exquisite hymns of the Ṛgveda (e.g. RV 1.113), Uṣā-devī is honored in Śrī Madhvācārya's Ṛgbhāṣya and Tantrasārasaṅgraha not merely as physical twilight, but as the presiding deity of spiritual awakening (`prabodha`) who prepares the mind for morning meditation (`brāhma-muhūrta`).

padaccheda.gloss: shines forth and drives away darkness (√vas → ucchati)
early daybreak, threshold of the day

lakshanaDeva: द्यति तमः खण्डयति इति दिनम् । घस्रो दिनाहनी वा तु क्लीबे दिवसवासरौ ॥
lakshanaIast: dyati tamaḥ khaṇḍayati iti dinam | ghasro dināhanī vā tu klībe divasavāsarau ||
meaningShort: Day or daytime — the sunlit span from sunrise to sunset that cleaves darkness and illumines worldly activity.
meaningDeep: Classical commentators (Kṣīrasvāmin & Bhānuji Dīkṣita) derive `dina` from √do ('avakhāṇḍane' — `dyati tamaḥ`, that which cuts through nocturnal gloom) or √dī ('dīptau' — to shine brightly). Amarakośa (Kālavarga) groups `ghasra`, `dina`, `ahan` ('that which is never abandoned by time', `na jahāti`), `divasa` (from √div, 'luminous expanse'), and `vāsara`. In astronomical and dharmaśāstric reckoning, a civil `sāvana-dina` spans from one sunrise to the next, comprising thirty `muhūrtas`.

lakshanaDeva: सम्यक् ध्यायन्त्यस्यां ब्रह्म इति सन्ध्या । सन्ध्या पित्र्या प्रदोषश्च रजन्याः प्रथमे मुखे ॥
lakshanaIast: samyak dhyāyanty asyāṃ brahma iti sandhyā | sandhyā pitryā pradoṣaś ca rajanyāḥ prathame mukhe ||
meaningShort: Twilight — the liminal juncture uniting day and night, revered as the sacred hour for meditative worship.
meaningDeep: Formed either from `sam` + √dhā ('sandhīyate aho-rātram atra' — where day and night are joined together) or `sam` + √dhyai ('samyak dhyāyanti' — the hour when sages meditate intently upon the Supreme), `sandhyā` denotes dawn, noon, and evening transitions (`tri-sandhyā`). Amarakośa (Kālavarga) pairs evening twilight with `pitryā` and `pradoṣa`. In Vaidika and Tattvavāda daily discipline (`sandhyāvandana`), the worshiper contemplates Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa dwelling within the solar orb via the Savitṛ-Gāyatrī mantra.

padaccheda.gloss: at the opening threshold of night

lakshanaDeva: राति सुखं विश्रामं च भूतेभ्य इति रात्रिः । निशा निशीथिनी रात्रिस्त्रियामा क्षणदा क्षपा ॥
lakshanaIast: rāti sukhaṃ viśrāmaṃ ca bhūtebhya iti rātriḥ | niśā niśīthinī rātris triyāmā kṣaṇadā kṣapā ||
meaningShort: Night — the tranquil starlit interval from dusk to dawn that bestows rest and restoration upon all living beings.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 2.18) and Uṇādi-sūtra (4.67: `rāter ṭriḥ`) derive `rātri` from √rā ('dāne' — she who bestows peaceful repose upon weary creatures) or √ram ('to bring activity to rest'). Amarakośa (Kālavarga) offers poetic synonyms: `niśā`, `niśīthinī`, `triyāmā` ('spanning three central watches'), `kṣaṇadā` ('giver of restful leisure'), `kṣapā`, `vibhāvarī` ('star-bright'), `tamisrā`, `rajanī`, and `śarvarī`. Bhagavadgītā 2.69 (`yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī`) contrasts worldly slumber with the sage's inward wakefulness.

padaccheda.gloss: stiller of motion, deep midnight-bearer, night

lakshanaDeva: इयर्ति क्रमेण गच्छति इति ऋतुः । मासौ द्वौ द्वौ स्मृतावृतू षड्भिः संवत्सरो मतः ॥
lakshanaIast: iyarti krameṇa gacchati iti ṛtuḥ | māsau dvau dvau smṛtāv ṛtū ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃvatsaro mataḥ ||
meaningShort: A season — an orderly two-month division of the solar-lunar year moving in harmonious cosmic rhythm.
meaningDeep: Derived from √ṛ ('gatau' — `iyarti`, to move in unerring sequence; Uṇādi 1.71), `ṛtu` shares its root with Vedic `ṛta` (cosmic order). Amarakośa (Kālavarga 1.4.13–20) defines each `ṛtu` as a pair of lunar months (`dvau dvau māsau rtuḥ`), enumerating the classical six-season (`ṣaḍ-ṛtu`) wheel of India: `vasanta` (spring), `grīṣma` (summer), `varṣāḥ` (monsoon), `śarad` (autumn), `hemanta` (early winter), and `śiśira` (late frost). In Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and Āyurveda (`ṛtucaryā`), living in attunement with the seasons sustains health and dharma.

padaccheda.gloss: each pair of months constitutes one season
six seasons complete the full year

lakshanaDeva: वसन्त्यस्मिन् सुखं प्राणिनः कामानदयश्चेति वसन्तः । वसन्ते पुष्पसमयः सुरभिः कुसुमाकरः ॥
lakshanaIast: vasanty asmin sukhaṃ prāṇinaḥ kāmādayaś ceti vasantaḥ | vasante puṣpasamayaḥ surabhiḥ kusumākaraḥ ||
meaningShort: Spring — the fragrant vernal season of Caitra and Vaiśākha when groves burst into blossom and cuckoos sing.
meaningDeep: Formed from √vas ('nivāse / kāntau' — wherein beauty, joy, and mild breezes dwell) with the Uṇādi suffix `-jhac` (`-anta`, Uṇādi 3.128), `vasanta` spans the lunar months `caitra` (`madhu`) and `vaiśākha` (`mādhava`). Amarakośa (Kālavarga 1.4.18) names it `puṣpasamaya` ('flower-tide') and `surabhi` ('fragrant one'), while Bhagavadgītā 10.35 crowns it first among seasons: `ṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ` ('among seasons I am flower-bearing Spring') — interpreted in Madhvācārya's Gītābhāṣya as manifesting Bhagavān's joyous creative abundance.

padaccheda.gloss: wherein creatures dwell in mild delight (√vas)
season of blossoms, the fragrant one

lakshanaDeva: शृणाति पङ्कं मेघं च इति शरत् । स्यादृतुः प्रावृषोर्ध्वं स्त्री शरत् ॥
lakshanaIast: śṛṇāti paṅkaṃ meghaṃ ca iti śarat | syād ṛtuḥ prāvṛṣordhvaṃ strī śarat ||
meaningShort: Autumn — the crystalline post-monsoon season of Āśvina and Kārttika famed for cloudless skies, silver moonlight, and clear waters.
meaningDeep: Yāska (Nirukta 4.25: `śarat śṛtā asyām oṣadhayo bhavanti`) and Uṇādi-sūtra (1.127) derive `śarad` from √śṝ ('hiṃsāyām' — dispersing dark storm-clouds and mud) or √śrā ('pāke' — ripening crops and herbs). Following the rains (`prāvṛṣordhvam`, AK 1.4.19), `śarad` unveils spotless skies, blooming lotuses, and radiant full moons (`śaraccandra`). Because Vedic prayers measure human longevity by clear autumns (`jīvema śaradaḥ śatam`, RV 7.66.16), `śarad` also serves in Amarakośa as a classical synonym for an entire year.

padaccheda.gloss: clears away mire and dark storm-clouds (√śṝ)
the luminous season following the monsoon rains
autumn; by metonymy, a year of life

lakshanaDeva: हिममस्यास्तीति हेमन्तः । मार्गशीर्षसहाः पौषस्तैषश्च द्वौ तु हेमन्तः ॥
lakshanaIast: himam asyāstīti hemantaḥ | mārgaśīrṣasahāḥ pauṣas taiṣaś ca dvau tu hemantaḥ ||
meaningShort: Winter — the cool, mist-veiled harvest season spanning the lunar months of Mārgaśīrṣa and Pauṣa.
meaningDeep: Derived from √hi / `hima` (frost, cool dew; Nirukta 4.27) via Uṇādi 3.128 (`heman` + `-ta`), `hemanta` marks the onset of crisp cold across Mārgaśīrṣa (`sahas`) and Pauṣa (`sahasyā`), followed by deep frost (`śiśira`). Amarakośa (Kālavarga 1.4.16–17) pairs these two cold months as `hemanta`. Notably, its opening month `mārgaśīrṣa` is celebrated in Bhagavadgītā 10.35 (`māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'ham`) as a season of ripened golden grain, clear morning mist, and heightened digestive and contemplative vigor.

padaccheda.gloss: characterized by cool dew and frost (`hima`)
spanning the months Mārgaśīrṣa and Pauṣa

lakshanaDeva: वर्षति कामं कालं वा इति वर्षः । संवत्सरो वत्सरोऽब्दो हायनोऽस्त्री शरत्समाः ॥
lakshanaIast: varṣati kāmaṃ kālaṃ vā iti varṣaḥ | saṃvatsaro vatsaro 'bdo hāyano 'strī śaratsamāḥ ||
meaningShort: A year (and in feminine plural `varṣāḥ`, the monsoon season) — a complete annual cycle measured by the return of the rains.
meaningDeep: From √vṛṣ ('secane' — to rain down), `varṣa` reflects the agrarian insight of classical India: a full year (`saṃvatsara`) is counted from one monsoon cycle to the next, just as `abda` literally means 'cloud/water-giver'.
