meaningDeep: Because its true underlying stem in the svarādi-gaṇa (1.1.37) ends in r (punar, not *punas!), its sandhi differs crucially from s-final words: before vowels and voiced consonants r remains even after a (punar api, punar gacchati), and before r-initial words the first r drops with compensatory lengthening by Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.14 & 6.3.111 (punar + ramate → punā ramate; punar + racayati → punā racayati). Iterated punaḥ punaḥ expresses continual repetition, while kiṃ punaḥ means 'how much more so!'.

padaccheda.gloss: punar in the sense of repetition ('again', Amarakośa 3.4.16)
and in contrastive distinction ('on the other hand')

lakshanaDeva: शनैर्मन्दं क्रमेणाव्ययम् — शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया (शनैः पन्थाः शनैः कन्था शनैः पर्वतलंघनम्) ॥
lakshanaIast: śanair mandaṃ krameṇāvyayam — śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā (śanaiḥ panthāḥ śanaiḥ kanthā śanaiḥ parvatalaṅghanam) ||
meaningShort: Slowly, gently, gradually — the svarādi adverb of patient, step-by-step mastery.
meaningDeep: Preserved as a fossilized archaic instrumental plural in the svarādi-gaṇa (Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.37: uccais, nīcais, śanais), śanaiḥ embodies measured, unhurried steadiness both in yogic meditation — Bhagavadgītā 6.25: śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā ('step by step let one attain stillness through an intellect held firm by fortitude') — and in the famous subhāṣita teaching that learning, mountain-climbing, and dharma are mastered gradually (śanair vidyā śanair arthaḥ).

padaccheda.gloss: step by step let one grow tranquil (Bhagavadgītā 6.25)

lakshanaDeva: शीघ्रं त्वरितमाशु क्षिप्रमरं द्रुतं सत्वरं चपलं तूर्णमविलम्बितम् — क्रियाविशेषणमव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: śīghraṃ tvaritam āśu kṣipram araṃ drutaṃ satvaraṃ capalaṃ tūrṇam avilambitam — kriyāviśeṣaṇam avyayam |
meaningShort: Quickly, swiftly, without delay (āśu / kṣipram / drutam / satvaram).
meaningDeep: Grouped in Amarakośa 1.1.65's celebrated ten-word cluster for swiftness (śīghram, tvaritam, āśu, kṣipram, aram, drutam, satvaram, tūrṇam, avilambitam; cf. Gītā 4.12 kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā), adverbial accusative śīghram (kriyāviśeṣaṇānāṃ karmatvaṃ napuṃsakatvaṃ ca) and svarādi/neuter āśu (cognate with Greek ōkys, whence āśukavi 'extempore poet') are polar opposites of śanaiḥ / ciram.

lakshanaDeva: सप्तम्यास्त्रल् · इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ (अत्रेह च) — अस्मिन् देशे विषये वात्रेति त्रलन्तमव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: saptamyās tral · idamo'nvādeśe'ś anudāttas tṛtīyādau (atreha ca) — asmin deśe viṣaye vātreti tralantam avyayam |
meaningShort: Here, in this place, or regarding this topic — locative-sense taddhita avyaya (idam → a + tral).
meaningDeep: Derived by Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.10 (saptamyās tral, attaching -tra in the sense of the seventh/locative case to pronominal stems, with idam replaced by a- via 2.4.32 / 5.3.11 idamo haḥ → iha alongside atra), atra functions both spatially ('here in this spot / earthly realm', contrasted with amutra 'in the yonder world') and discursively throughout Sanskrit commentaries (atra ucyate = 'On this point it is replied...'; atrabhavān = 'this venerable gentleman here').

padaccheda.gloss: suffix -tra attaches in locative sense (idam + tral = atra, Aṣṭ. 5.3.10)
in this place or in this matter

lakshanaDeva: तदः सप्तम्यास्त्रल् — तस्मिन् देशे विषये समुदाये वा तत्रेत्यव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: tadaḥ saptamyās tral — tasmin deśe viṣaye samudāye vā tatrety avyayam |
meaningShort: There, in that place, or 'among those' — locative taddhita avyaya (tad + tral) paired with yatra.
meaningDeep: Formed from demonstrative tad + tral by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.10 (answering relative yatra, 'where... there', as in the closing verse of the Bhagavadgītā 18.78: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ | tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama), tatra is equally ubiquitous in śāstric division-prose as a partitive nirdhāraṇa-saptamī ('among those just listed': pramāṇāni pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ; tatra pratyakṣam...).

padaccheda.gloss: in that place / among them (locative taddhita, Aṣṭ. 5.3.10)

lakshanaDeva: कु तिहोः · क्वाति — किमः सप्तम्यां त्रलतिभ्यां कुत्र क्व चेति प्रश्नवाचकमव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: ku tihoḥ · kvāti — kimaḥ saptamyāṃ tralatibhyāṃ kutra kva ceti praśnavācakam avyayam |
meaningShort: Where? Whither? — interrogative locative avyayas (kutra and kva) derived from kim.
meaningDeep: Pāṇini derives both synonyms from interrogative kim: before t/h-initial taddhitas like -tral, kim becomes ku- by Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.2.104 (ku tihoḥ → kutra, 'where?'), whereas before suffix -at (5.3.12 kimo't) kim becomes kva- by 7.2.105 (kvāti → kva, 'where?'). Repeated in consecutive clauses, kva... kva expresses breathtaking incongruity, immortalized in Kālidāsa's Raghuvaṃśa 1.2: kva sūryaprabhavo vaṃśaḥ kva cālpaviṣayā matiḥ ('How vast the gulf between the dynasty born of the Sun and my slender-compassed mind!').

lakshanaDeva: सर्वस्मिन् देशे विषये च सर्वत्र — समं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तिष्ठन्तं परमेश्वरं सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
lakshanaIast: sarvasmin deśe viṣaye ca sarvatra — samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaraṃ sarvatra samadarśanaḥ ||
meaningShort: Everywhere, in every place or case — universal locative avyaya (sarva + tral).
meaningDeep: Derived from sarva + tral by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.10 (sarvasmin deśe kāle viṣaye vā), sarvatra expresses both spatial omnipresence (Īśvara's vyāpti throughout creation; Bhagavadgītā 6.29 sarvatra samadarśanaḥ & 13.13 sarvataḥpāṇipādaṃ tat) and universal rule-application in Pāṇinian grammar (e.g., Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.122 sarvatra vibhāṣā goḥ — 'everywhere, both in Veda and spoken Sanskrit').

padaccheda.gloss: beholding the supreme Lord equally everywhere (Gītā 6.29)

lakshanaDeva: स्वरन्तरिति स्वरादिष्वव्ययम् — मध्येऽभ्यन्तरे चान्तर्बहिश्च तत्सर्वं व्याप्य नारायणः स्थितः ॥
lakshanaIast: svar antar iti svarādiṣv avyayam — madhye'bhyantare cāntar bahiś ca tat sarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ ||
meaningShort: Within, inside, in the core — the r-final svarādi avyaya forming antaryāmin ('Inner Controller') and antaḥkaraṇa.
meaningDeep: Second word of Pāṇini's svarādi-gaṇa (Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.37; cognate with Latin inter) with underlying r-stem antar (hence antar-ātman, antaryāmin, antargata, and before r: antā-rāṣṭrīya by 8.3.14 & 6.3.111; distinct from masculine noun antaḥ = 'end/border'!), antar governs the genitive or locative for 'within / between' and shines in Nārāyaṇasūkta 5: antar bahiś ca tat sarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ ('Pervading all this both inwardly and outwardly, Nārāyaṇa abides').

padaccheda.gloss: within, inside, in the midst (svarādi r-final avyaya)

lakshanaDeva: अपादाने पञ्चमी बहिर्योगे — बाह्ये बहिः स्वरादिपठितमव्ययं ग्रामाद् बहिः ।
lakshanaIast: apādāne pañcamī bahiryoge — bāhye bahiḥ svarādipathitam avyayaṃ grāmād bahiḥ |
meaningShort: Outside, externally — governing the ablative case (grāmād bahiḥ) and opposed to antaḥ.
meaningDeep: Listed in the svarādi-gaṇa (1.1.37; taddhita adjective bāhya, 'external', via 4.1.85 dityadityādityapatyuttarapadāṇ ṇyaḥ + vārttika bahiṣaṣ ṭilopo yañ ca), bahis regularly governs the fifth (ablative) case by Kātyāyana's vārttika on Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.3.29 (jugupsāvirāmapramādārthānām upasaṅkhyānam / bahiryoge pañcamī: grāmād bahiḥ, 'outside the village'). In Yoga and Vedānta, bahiraṅga-sādhana ('external disciplines' like yama-niyama) prepares for antaraṅga-sādhana (dhāraṇā, dhyāna, samādhi).

padaccheda.gloss: construes with the ablative case (grāmād bahiḥ)

lakshanaDeva: उपर्युपरिष्टादूर्ध्वार्थे — उभसर्वतसोः कार्या धिगुपर्यादिषु त्रिषु द्वितीयाऽम्रेडितान्तेषु (उपर्युपरि लोकं हरेरुपरि वा) ।
lakshanaIast: upary upariṣṭād ūrdhvārthe — ubhasarvatasoḥ kāryā dhiguparyādiṣu triṣu dvitīyā'mreḍitānteṣu (upary upari lokaṃ harer upari vā) |
meaningShort: Above, over, upon — governing the genitive singly (vṛkṣasya upari) and the accusative when doubled (upary upari).
meaningDeep: Formed with spatial taddhita -ril (cognate with Greek hyper and Latin super; alongside upariṣṭāt by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.31 upary upariṣṭāt), upari ordinarily construes with the sixth/genitive case (gṛhasya upari, 'above the house') or at the end of compounds (sarvopari), whereas when reduplicated in intensive proximity (āmreḍita: upary upari) Kātyāyana's famous vārttika on 2.3.2 prescribes the accusative case (upary upari lokaṃ hariḥ, 'immediately/supremely above the cosmos abides Hari').

lakshanaDeva: अधोऽधस्तादधोभागे — वृक्षस्याधोऽधो भूमिं चेति षष्ठीद्वितीयायोगि दिगव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: adho'dhastād adhobhāge — vṛkṣasyādho'dho bhūmiṃ ceti ṣaṣṭhīdvitīyāyogi digavyayam |
meaningShort: Below, beneath, downward — the directional counterpart of upari.
meaningDeep: Listed among directional avyayas (alongside adhastāt by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.27 dikśabdebhyaḥ saptamīpañcamīprathamābhyo digdeśakāleṣv astātiḥ / 5.3.39 pūrvādharāvaraṇāsi puradhavaṃś caiṣām), adhas governs the genitive when single (vṛkṣasya adhaḥ, 'beneath the tree') and the accusative when doubled as āmreḍita (adho'dho bhūmim, 'deep beneath the earth'). In Bhagavadgītā 15.1–2, the cosmic aśvattha tree extends its branches adhaś cordhvam ('both downward and upward').

padaccheda.gloss: below, underneath, in the lower region
deep below the ground (+ accusative when doubled)

lakshanaDeva: पूर्वाधरावरणासि पुरधवंश्चैषाम् (पुरस्तात्पुरतश्च) — अग्रेऽग्रतः पुरतोऽभिमुखे च षष्ठीयोगि ।
lakshanaIast: pūrvādharāvaraṇāsi puradhavaṃś caiṣām (purastāt purataś ca) — agre'grataḥ purato'bhimukhe ca ṣaṣṭhīyogi |
meaningShort: In front of, ahead, or before one's presence (agre / agrataḥ / purastāt).
meaningDeep: Formed from pūrva (substituted by pura- per Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.39) with directional suffix -tas (5.3.7 pañcamyās tasil / 5.3.40 astāti ca → purataḥ and purastāt), and paired with fossilized locative agre / agrataḥ ('at the forefront / in the beginning', cf. sadāgre vasate lakṣmīḥ and Chāndogya 6.2.1 sad eva somyedam agra āsīt), purataḥ construes with the genitive case (guroḥ purataḥ, 'in front of the preceptor').

lakshanaDeva: अपरस्यार्धपश्चभावो वक्तव्यः (पश्चात्) — पृष्ठतः पश्चाच्च पृष्ठभागे कालानन्तर्ये च ।
lakshanaIast: aparasyārdhapaścabhāvo vaktavyaḥ (paścāt) — pṛṣṭhataḥ paścāc ca pṛṣṭhabhāge kālānantarye ca |
meaningShort: Behind, at the rear (pṛṣṭhataḥ), and subsequently / behind / westward (paścāt).
meaningDeep: Combining pṛṣṭha ('back') + tasil (pṛṣṭhataḥ, 'behind / behind one's back', e.g., pratyakṣe gurustutiḥ pṛṣṭhato nindā; pṛṣṭhataḥ kuru = 'leave behind / disregard') with nipātana-derived paścāt (from apara → paśca + āti by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.32 paśca paścā ca cchandasi), these two avyayas cover spatial rear (gṛhasya pṛṣṭhataḥ / grāmāt paścāt, governing genitive or ablative) as well as temporal sequence ('afterwards, later').

padaccheda.gloss: behind, at the back of (pṛṣṭha + tasil)

lakshanaDeva: किमः प्रकारवचने थमुः — केन प्रकारेण इति कथमव्ययं प्रश्नसंभ्रमाक्षेपे ।
lakshanaIast: kimaḥ prakāravacane thamuḥ — kena prakāreṇa iti katham avyayaṃ praśnasaṃbhramākṣepe |
meaningShort: How? In what manner? — the interrogative adverb of manner formed from kim + thamu.
meaningDeep: While yad and tad take -thāl (yathā, tathā), Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.25 (kimaś ca — kimaḥ thamuḥ) attaches suffix thamu (-tham) specifically to interrogative kim (substituted by ka- via 7.2.103), yielding katham ('in what manner? how?'; parallel to idam + thamu → ittham, 'thus'). With api or cit it forms katham api / kathaṃcit ('somehow, with great difficulty'), and in rhetorical questions expresses astonishment or impossibility (kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṅkhye... pratiyotsyāmi, Bhagavadgītā 2.4).

lakshanaDeva: कस्मै प्रयोजनायेति किमर्थम् · किमः पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् कुत इति हेतौ प्रभवे च प्रश्नः ।
lakshanaIast: kasmai prayojanāyeti kimartham · kimaḥ pañcamyās tasil kuta iti hetau prabhave ca praśnaḥ |
meaningShort: Why / for what purpose? (kimartham) and Whence / on what logical ground? (kutaḥ).
meaningDeep: Sanskrit distinguishes final-purpose 'why?' — kimartham (adverbial compound: kaḥ arthaḥ prayojanaṃ yasya tat, 'for what aim/prayojana?') — from causal/ablative 'whence / why?' — kutaḥ (derived from kim → ku + ablative tasil by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.7 pañcamyās tasil & 7.2.104 ku tihoḥ). Throughout Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, and Vedānta bhāṣyas, a terse single-word kutaḥ? ('Why? What is your hetu?') challenges an opponent to state their logical reason, answered immediately by yataḥ... or an ablative hetu.

padaccheda.gloss: from where? on what logical ground? (Aṣṭ. 5.3.7 & 7.2.104)

lakshanaDeva: यदः पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — यस्माद् देशाद्धेतोर्वेति यतः (यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायन्ते) ।
lakshanaIast: yadaḥ pañcamyās tasil — yasmād deśād dhetor veti yataḥ (yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante) |
meaningShort: From whom/which, whence, or because — ablative taddhita avyaya (yad + tasil) opening Brahman's cosmic lakṣaṇa.
meaningDeep: Formed from relative yad + tasil by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.7 (pañcamyās tasil, functioning interchangeably with ablative yasmāt across all genders and numbers!), yataḥ expresses both origin/source — most famously in Taittirīya Upaniṣad 3.1 (cited under Brahmasūtra 1.1.2 janmādy asya yataḥ): yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante ('That from Whom indeed these beings are born') — and logical reason ('because / since', paired with tataḥ / ataḥ, 'therefore').

padaccheda.gloss: from whom/which, whence, because (ablative taddhita, Aṣṭ. 5.3.7)
He from Whom come the birth, sustenance, and dissolution of this cosmos (BS 1.1.2)

lakshanaDeva: तदः पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तस्माद् देशात् कालाद्धेतोर्वा तत इत्यव्ययम् (अतश्चेदंमिमोः) ।
lakshanaIast: tadaḥ pañcamyās tasil — tasmād deśāt kālād dhetor vā tata ity avyayam (ataś cedam-imoḥ) |
meaningShort: From there, thereafter, therefore — the ablative correlative avyaya (tad + tasil; proximal twin ataḥ).
meaningDeep: Derived from tad + tasil by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.7 (parallel to idam + tasil → ataḥ, 'hence / therefore', opening Brahmasūtra 1.1.1 athāto brahmajijñāsā), tataḥ spans every function of the Sanskrit fifth case: spatial departure ('from that place'), temporal succession in narrative ('thereupon / next': tataḥ kim?), comparative ablative ('greater than that': tato'py adhikam), and inferential conclusion ('therefore', answering yataḥ).

lakshanaDeva: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — सार्धं साकं समं सह तृतीयाविभक्तियोगि सहार्थवाचकमव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: sahayukte'pradhāne — sārdhaṃ sākaṃ samaṃ saha tṛtīyāvibhaktiyogi sahārthavācakam avyayam |
meaningShort: With, together with (sākam / sārdham / samam) — governing the instrumental case of the accompanying party.
meaningDeep: Pāṇini's quintessential upapada-vibhakti rule Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.3.19 (sahayukte'pradhāne) ordains that when saha or any of its synonyms (Amarakośa 3.4.9: sārdham, sākam, samam) expresses accompaniment, the secondary/accompanying person takes the third (instrumental) case while the verb agrees solely with the primary subject (putreṇa saha āgataḥ pitā). In compounds saha contracts optionally to sa- by 6.3.78 (sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām / 6.3.82 vopasarjanasya → saputraḥ), and shines in the Upaniṣadic peace-invocation saha nāv avatu, saha nau bhunaktu, saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai.

padaccheda.gloss: the accompanying party with saha takes the instrumental case (Aṣṭ. 2.3.19)

lakshanaDeva: पृथग्विनानानाभिस्तृतीयान्यतरस्याम् · अन्यारादितरर्ते... पञ्चमी — विना द्वितीयातृतीयापञ्चमीयोगि ऋते च द्वितीयापञ्चमीयोगि ।
lakshanaIast: pṛthagvinānānābhis tṛtīyānyatarasyām · anyārāditararte... pañcamī — vinā dvitīyātṛtīyāpañcamīyogi ṛte ca dvitīyāpañcamīyogi |
meaningShort: Without, apart from — vinā construing freely with accusative, instrumental, or ablative, and ṛte with ablative or accusative.
meaningDeep: By Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.3.32 (pṛthagvinānānābhis tṛtīyānyatarasyām, drawing both pañcamī from 2.3.28 and dvitīyā from 2.3.31), vinā ('without') gracefully accepts three cases interchangeably: jñānaṃ vinā / jñānena vinā / jñānād vinā na muktiḥ ('without knowledge there is no liberation'; similarly vātaṃ/vātena/vātād vinā). Its Vedic-classical twin ṛte ('except for / without', Amarakośa 3.4.9) governs the ablative by 2.3.29 (jñānād ṛte na muktiḥ) or accusative.

lakshanaDeva: प्रतिः प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदानयोर्यस्मात् · लक्षणेत्थम्भूताख्यानभागवीप्सासु प्रतिपर्यनवः — द्वितीयापञ्चमीयोगी कर्मप्रवचनीयः ।
lakshanaIast: pratiḥ pratinidhipratidānayor yasmāt · lakṣaṇetthambhūtākhyānabhāgavīpsāsu pratiparyanavaḥ — dvitīyāpañcamīyogī karmapravacanīyaḥ |
meaningShort: Towards, regarding, each, or in return — Pāṇini's karmapravacanīya particle governing the accusative.
meaningDeep: Functioning both as a verbal prefix (upasarga: prativadati 'replies', pratibimba 'reflection') and as an adpositional karmapravacanīya (Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.90 lakṣaṇetthambhūtākhyānabhāgavīpsāsu pratiparyanavaḥ), prati governs the accusative case by 2.3.8 (karmapravacanīyayukte dvitīyā) in the senses of direction ('toward the tree': vṛkṣaṃ prati vidyotate vidyut), kindness toward (dīnān prati dayāluḥ), and distributiveness ('tree by tree': vṛkṣaṃ vṛkṣaṃ prati, compounding into avyayībhāva pratidinam 'daily', pratyekam 'each one'), while taking ablative for substitution/exchange (1.4.92, 2.3.11).

padaccheda.gloss: prati is a karmapravacanīya in direction, sign, share, and 'each' (Aṣṭ. 1.4.90)

lakshanaDeva: नमःस्वस्तिस्वाहास्वधालंवषड्योगाच्च · अलंखल्वोः प्रतिषेधयोः प्राचां क्त्वा — वारणे तृतीयाक्त्वायोगि सामर्थ्ये चतुर्थीयोग्यव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: namaḥsvastisvāhāsvadhālaṃvaṣaḍyogāc ca · alaṃkhalvoḥ pratiṣedhayoḥ prācāṃ ktvā — vāraṇe tṛtīyāktvāyogi sāmarthye caturthīyogy avyayam |
meaningShort: Enough! Cease! (+ instrumental or ktvā) AND capable / a match for (+ dative) — a dual-case masterpiece of Sanskrit syntax.
meaningDeep: Amarakośa 3.4.10 (alaṃ bhūṣaṇaparyāptiśaktivāraṇavācakam) identifies four senses of alam that split cleanly by grammatical case: (1) vāraṇa / pratiṣedha ('Enough of! Stop!'): governs the instrumental (alaṃ vivādena, 'Enough of dispute!') or gerund ktvā by Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.18 (alaṃ hasitvā, 'Stop laughing!'); (2) paryāpti / śakti ('sufficient / capable of'): governs the dative by 2.3.16 (daityebhyo harir alam, 'Hari alone suffices to vanquish the demons'); and (3) bhūṣaṇa ('adornment'), compounded with √kṛ as gati by 1.4.64 (bhūṣaṇe'lam → alaṅkaroti, alaṅkāra).

padaccheda.gloss: signifying ornament, sufficiency, capability, and prohibition (Amarakośa 3.4.10)
+ 3rd case for 'enough of!'; + 4th case for 'a match for'

lakshanaDeva: निषेधवाक्यालङ्कारजिज्ञासानुनये खलु · नूनं तर्केऽर्थनिश्चये — प्रसिद्धौ निश्चये च निपाताव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: niṣedhavākyālaṅkārajijñāsānunaye khalu · nūnaṃ tarke'rthaniścaye — prasiddhau niścaye ca nipātāvyayam |
meaningShort: Indeed, surely, as everyone knows (khalu), and certainly / methinks (nūnam).
meaningDeep: Catalogued in Amarakośa 3.4.13 & 3.4.6, khalu is one of classical Sanskrit drama and śāstra's subtlest discourse particles: appealing to shared recognition ('indeed / after all': sarvaṃ khalv idaṃ brahma, Chāndogya 3.14.1; ratna-śabda-vācyāni khalu...), softening an entreaty (anunaya), or prohibiting with ktvā by Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.18 (khalu kṛtvā, 'pray do not do so'). Its companion nūnam expresses either firm certainty (niścaya) or poetic conjecture (utprekṣā / tarka: nūnaṃ...).

padaccheda.gloss: khalu marks prohibition, grace, inquiry, conciliation, and well-known truth (Amarakośa 3.4.13)
nūnam marks poetic surmise and certainty (Amarakośa 3.4.6)

lakshanaDeva: चायदिहन्तचेदिति पक्षान्तरे — संभावनार्थे यदीति सवाक्यादिके चेदिति पदात्परं निपाताव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: cāyadihantaced iti pakṣāntare — saṃbhāvanārthe yadīti savākyādike ced iti padāt paraṃ nipātāvyayam |
meaningShort: If, in case — clause-openable yadi and enclitic cet introducing conditional protases and śāstric objections.
meaningDeep: Included in Pāṇini's cādi-gaṇa (1.4.57; triggering accent retention on the protasis finite verb by 8.1.30 nipātair yadyadihantakuvinneccaccaṇkaccidyatrayuktam), yadi may stand freely at the head of a conditional clause (yadi... tarhi / tadā, often with optative vidhiliṅ or conditional lṛṅ), whereas enclitic cet never begins a clause and in Sanskrit philosophical prose crystallizes into the ultra-concise dialectical formula: iti cet — na ('If an opponent objects thus [iti cet] — we reply: No [na], because...').

padaccheda.gloss: 'if it be argued thus — not so!' (canonical śāstra formula)

lakshanaDeva: एतदोऽन् — तदो र्हिलौ च (तर्हि कर्हि यर्हि) यदीत्यस्य प्रतिसम्बन्धि निपाताव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: etado'n — tado rhilau ca (tarhi karhi yarhi) yadīty asya pratisambandhi nipātāvyayam |
meaningShort: Then, in that case — the conditional apodosis correlative (tad + rhil) paired naturally with yadi.
meaningDeep: Derived from demonstrative tad via taddhita suffix rhil by Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.16 & 5.3.20–21 (forming the classic rhil-triad yarhi 'when', karhi 'when?', tarhi 'then', alongside etarhi 'nowadays'), tarhi originally denoted time ('at that time') and specialized in classical śāstra and spoken Sanskrit as the crisp logical correlative of yadi: yadi megho varṣati, tarhi mayūro nṛtyati ('If the cloud rains, then the peacock dances').

padaccheda.gloss: then, in that case (taddhita avyaya, Aṣṭ. 5.3.20–21)

lakshanaDeva: एवमाम्बाढमित्यभ्युपगमे — ओमेवं परं बाढमिति स्वीकारनिश्चयवाचकमव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: evam āmbāḍham ity abhyupagame — om evaṃ paraṃ bāḍham iti svīkāraniścayavācakam avyayam |
meaningShort: Yes! Assuredly! Agreed! — classical Sanskrit's particles of wholehearted assent (abhyupagama / svīkāra).
meaningDeep: Amarakośa 3.4.2 & 3.4.15 group Sanskrit's affirmative particles of assent: ām ('Yes! Indeed', also marking sudden recollection), bāḍham (historically kta of √bādh/√vah → 'firmly, assuredly, by all means!', ubiquitous in Sanskrit drama and Śaṅkara/Jayatīrtha dialogues when granting a premise: bāḍham, satyam evaitat), and Vedic-Upaniṣadic om (Chāndogya 1.1.8: oṃ ity etad akṣaram anujñā, 'This syllable Oṃ is solemn assent').

padaccheda.gloss: 'Yes! Certainly!' in the sense of assent and agreement (Amarakośa 3.4.15)

lakshanaDeva: नमःस्वस्तिस्वाहास्वधालंवषड्योगाच्च — हरये नमो गुरवे नम इति चतुर्थीविभक्तियोगि प्रह्वत्ववाचि स्वराद्यव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: namaḥsvastisvāhāsvadhālaṃvaṣaḍyogāc ca — haraye namo gurave nama iti caturthīvibhaktiyogi prahvatvavāci svarādyavyayam |
meaningShort: Reverent salutation, homage unto — governing the dative case by Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.3.16 (namaḥ + caturthī).
meaningDeep: Listed in Pāṇini's svarādi-gaṇa (1.1.37, derived from √nam 'to bow') and heading Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.3.16 (namaḥsvastisvāhāsvadhālaṃvaṣaḍyogāc ca), namaḥ requires the fourth (dative) case of the one saluted when used alone (śrīgurave namaḥ, nārāyaṇāya namaḥ, namas te = tubhyaṃ namaḥ; though with finite verb karoti it may govern the accusative: devaṃ namaskaroti, 1.4.70 ādarānādarayoḥ sadasatī + gati-kāraka). Spiritual nirukti also reads na mama ('not mine — all belongs to the Lord'), dissolving ahaṅkāra.

padaccheda.gloss: in construction with namaḥ, the fourth (dative) case applies (Aṣṭ. 2.3.16)
'nothing is selfishly mine' — devotional nirukti of surrender

lakshanaDeva: स्वस्त्याशीःक्षेमपुण्यादौ · नमःस्वस्तिस्वाहास्वधालंवषड्योगाच्च — प्रजाभ्यः स्वस्तीति चतुर्थीयोगि मङ्गलाव्ययम् ।
lakshanaIast: svasty āśīḥkṣemapuṇyādau · namaḥsvastisvāhāsvadhālaṃvaṣaḍyogāc ca — prajābhyaḥ svastīti caturthīyogi maṅgalāvyayam |
meaningShort: Well-being, auspicious blessing unto (+ dative) — transparent fusion of su + asti ('well-being').
meaningDeep: Etymologically transparent to Yāska and Pāṇini as su + asti ('well-being / auspicious existence', listed in svarādi-gaṇa 1.1.37; whence svastika, 'emblem of auspicious well-being', via su + asti + ka), svasti is paired immediately with namaḥ in Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.3.16 to govern the dative case of the recipient of benediction: svasti prajābhyaḥ paripālayantāṃ nyāyena mārgeṇa mahīṃ mahīśāḥ ('May auspicious well-being rest upon all beings!'), and Vedic svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ.

padaccheda.gloss: in benediction, safety, and merit (+ dative, Amarakośa 3.4.11 & Aṣṭ. 2.3.16)

lakshanaDeva: ओतत्ववाची ह्योङ्कारो वक्त्यसौ तद्गुणोतताम् । स एव ब्रह्मशब्दार्थो नारायणपदोदितः ॥
lakshanaIast: otatvavācī hy oṅkāro vakty asau tadguṇotatām | sa eva brahmaśabdārtho nārāyaṇapadoditaḥ ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: अकारेणाधिकं प्रोक्तमुकारेणोच्चमुच्यते । तथा मितं सर्ववेदैर्मकारेणाभिधीयते ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: akāreṇādhikaṃ proktam ukāreṇoccam ucyate | tathā mitaṃ sarvavedair makāreṇābhidhīyate ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: By 'a' is declared He who exceeds all; by 'u' He who stands loftiest; by 'm' He who is known through all Vedas — thus 'Oṃ' signifies the Supreme Being.

meaningShort: Oṅkāra (Praṇava) signifies He in whom infinite auspicious attributes are woven ('ota') and in whom the entire cosmos is sustained — the exact import of 'Brahman' and 'Nārāyaṇa'.
meaningDeep: Across Anuvyākhyāna 1.1.9, Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.2 (`om aśeṣaguṇādhāra iti nārāyaṇo'py asau`), Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.1.1, and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.3–4, Madhvācārya unfolds both the monolithic root-meaning of Oṃ (from √av 'to protect / weave / fill' → `ota-tva`) and its eightfold Praṇava-kalā structure (a, u, m, bindu, nāda, kalā, śānta, atiśānta) expressing the eight forms Viśva, Taijasa, Prājña, Turīya, Ātman, Antarātman, Paramātman, and Jñānātman.

padaccheda.gloss: proclaims His being replete with infinite auspicious qualities
and expressed by the supreme name 'Nārāyaṇa'

lakshanaDeva: अरीणां दोषसङ्घानां नताऽभावः प्रकीर्तितः । गुणानामपिचोतत्वमयनं गम्यतैव च ॥ ओमशेषगुणाधार इति नारायणोऽप्यसौ ।
lakshanaIast: arīṇāṃ doṣasaṅghānāṃ natā'bhāvaḥ prakīrtitaḥ | guṇānām api cotatvam ayanaṃ gamyataiva ca || om aśeṣaguṇādhāra iti nārāyaṇo'py asau |

secondaryLakshana.deva: नाराज्जातानि तत्त्वानि नाराणीति विदुर्बुधाः । तान्येवायनमस्येति तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: nārāj jātāni tattvāni nārāṇīti vidur budhāḥ | tāny evāyanam asyeti tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: The tattvas and souls sustained by Lord Nara are called 'Nārāḥ'; because He abides in them as their indwelling refuge and is their supreme goal ('ayana'), He is revered as Nārāyaṇa.

meaningShort: Nārāyaṇa is the Defectless Ocean of Infinite Auspicious Attributes (`nāra` = limitless virtues / absence of flaws `na-ari`), the Indwelling Substratum and Ultimate Goal (`ayana`) of all beings and scriptures.
meaningDeep: Madhvācārya demonstrates multi-layered mahāyoga in 'Nārāyaṇa': (1) `nāra` (auspicious guṇas never perishing, `na rīyante`) + `ayana` (supreme abode/substratum); (2) `na` (negation) + `ara` (defects/blemishes) + `ayana` (supreme goal of the liberated); (3) the Indweller of all sentient souls and waters (`āpo nārā iti proktāḥ`). Every Sarvamūla maṅgala-śloka salutes Nārāyaṇa as `nikhilapūrṇaguṇaikadehaṃ nirdoṣam`.

padaccheda.gloss: abode of imperishable auspicious attributes and refuge of souls
wholly devoid of defects (`ara`) and approachable by the wise

lakshanaDeva: व्याप्तृत्वाद् विष्णुरुद्दिष्टो देशतः कालतस्तथा । गुणैश्च सर्वतः पूर्णो वेवेष्टि व्यापको हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: vyāptṛtvād viṣṇur uddiṣṭo deśataḥ kālatas tathā | guṇaiś ca sarvataḥ pūrṇo veveṣṭi vyāpako hariḥ ||
meaningShort: Viṣṇu (from √viṣḷ 'vyāptau' — to pervade) is He who possesses plenary threefold pervasion across all space, all time, and all auspicious attributes without limit.
meaningDeep: While Avyākṛtākāśa and Prakṛti pervade space and eternal flow of time (`deśataḥ kālataḥ`), they are utterly deficient in conscious attributes (`guṇataḥ apūrṇam`). Even Mahālakṣmī, though co-extensive in space and time (`deśakālābhyām eva samavyāptā` — PS 2.2), is surpassed infinitely in quality (`guṇataḥ`). Only Viṣṇu is `deśataḥ kālato guṇataś ca aparicchinnaḥ` — unbounded in space, time, and excellence.

padaccheda.gloss: called Viṣṇu from absolute pervasion (`√viṣḷ vyāptau`)
unbounded in space and in eternity
and infinitely plenary in every excellence

lakshanaDeva: वसन्ति यत्र भूतानि वस्ते सर्वं जगच्च यः । द्योतनात् क्रीडनाच्चैव वासुदेवः स ईरितः ॥
lakshanaIast: vasanti yatra bhūtāni vaste sarvaṃ jagac ca yaḥ | dyotanāt krīḍanāc caiva vāsudevaḥ sa īritaḥ ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: वासुदेवो व्यपः स्मृतो यस्माद् व्यपगतस्थाता जगति प्रलये विभुः ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: vāsudevo vyapaḥ smṛto yasmād vyapagatasthātā jagati pralaye vibhuḥ |
secondaryLakshana.translation: Vāsudeva is remembered as transcendent protector who abides supreme even when the manifest cosmos dissolves at pralaya, and as bestower of liberation (`nijamuktipadapradātā` — MBTN 1.6).

meaningShort: Vāsudeva is He in whom all beings dwell ('vasanti'), who envelops and shelters the cosmos ('vaste'), and who shines, sports, and bestows liberation ('deva').
meaningDeep: First of the four primal Vyūha manifestations (Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha), Vāsudeva is specifically revered by Madhvācārya in MBTN 1.6 (`vāsudevanāmā babhūva nijamuktipadapradātā`) as the bestower of pristine Mokṣa, as well as Beloved Son of Vasudeva in Dvārakā.

padaccheda.gloss: universal abode and enveloping shelter of all beings
self-luminous, sporting in creation, and bestower of mokṣa

lakshanaDeva: ऐश्वर्यस्य समग्रस्य वीर्यस्य यशसः श्रियः । ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश्चैव षण्णां भग इतीरणा ॥ तद्वान् भगवान् ।
lakshanaIast: aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ | jñānavairāgyayoś caiva ṣaṇṇāṃ bhaga itīraṇā || tadvān bhagavān |
meaningShort: Bhagavān is He who eternally possesses 'Bhaga' in plenary completeness ('samagra') — unconditioned sovereignty, valour, renown, splendour, omniscience, and detachment.
meaningDeep: Citing Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6.5.74 and MBTN 1.24 (`ṣāḍguṇyavigrahaḥ supūrṇaguṇaikadehaḥ`), Madhvācārya underscores the word `samagrasya` (total, limitless): while exalted beings may be called 'bhagavān' figuratively, Viṣṇu alone bears the title primarily without metaphor.

padaccheda.gloss: of complete, limitless lordship, prowess, glory, and divine wealth
together with omniscience and detachment — these six
constitute Bhaga; their eternal Possessor is Bhagavān

lakshanaDeva: ब्रह्मशब्दश्च विष्ण्वाख्यो नान्यत्र क्वचिदिष्यते । बृहत्त्वाद् बृंहणत्वाच्च गुणपूर्णत्वतो हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: brahmaśabdaś ca viṣṇvākhyo nānyatra kvacid iṣyate | bṛhattvād bṛṃhaṇatvāc ca guṇapūrṇatvato hariḥ ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: ब्रह्मैव गुणपूर्णत्वात् सत्यं साधुस्वरूपतः ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: brahmaiva guṇapūrṇatvāt satyaṃ sādhusvarūpataḥ |
secondaryLakshana.translation: He alone is Brahman by virtue of infinite plenitude of attributes (`guṇapūrṇatvāt`), and Satya by virtue of faultless excellence.

meaningShort: Brahman (from √bṛh 'to be vast / plenary') denotes Bhagavān Viṣṇu as infinitely replete with all auspicious attributes ('guṇa-pūrṇatva') and nourisher of all beings.
meaningDeep: In Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 1.1.1 (`brahmaśabdasya viṣṇāv eva rūḍhiḥ / mahāyogaḥ`) and Anuvyākhyāna, Madhvācārya turns Advaita's nirguṇa-brahman upside down: the very etymology of 'Brahman' (`bṛhanto hy asmin guṇāḥ`) demands infinite positive attributes (`guṇa-pūrṇatva`), never attribute-less vacuity!

padaccheda.gloss: from infinite vastness in space, time, and attributes
and from nourishing and sustaining all worlds
Brahman signifies Plenary Completeness of Excellences

lakshanaDeva: आततत्वाच्च मातृत्वादात्मा हि परमो हरिः । यच्चाप्नोति यदादत्ते यच्चात्ति विषयानिह ॥
lakshanaIast: ātatatvāc ca mātṛtvād ātmā hi paramo hariḥ | yac cāpnoti yad ādatte yac cātti viṣayān iha ||
meaningShort: Ātman primarily denotes Supreme Hari because He pervades all ('ātata'), measures and fashions all ('mātṛ'), obtains all ('āpnoti'), withdraws all ('ādatte'), and enjoys auspiciousness.
meaningDeep: Whenever Upaniṣadic mahāvākyas speak of the Supreme Ātman (`aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvam`, `ayam ātmā brahma`), Madhvācārya cites this classical Vedic nirukti (`ātata + mātṛ`) to show that Paramātman Hari is the chief referent (`mukhyārtha`) of 'Ātman' as the Sovereign Owner and Inner Pervader of every individual jīvātman.

padaccheda.gloss: and because He is the omniscient knower, measurer, and motherly sustainer (`√mā`)
Supreme Hari alone is primarily called Ātman

source.author: Śrī Madhvācārya
source.locator: BSB 1.3.1; Mahābhārata Nirukti cited in Sarvamūla

lakshanaDeva: स पूर्णत्वात् पुमान्नाम पौरुषे सूक्त ईरितः । पुरि शेते इति पुरुषोऽन्तर्यामिरूपस्याख्या ॥
lakshanaIast: sa pūrṇatvāt pumān nāma pauruṣe sūkta īritaḥ | puri śete iti puruṣo'ntaryāmirūpasyākhyā ||
meaningShort: Puruṣa / Pumān denotes Bhagavān both from absolute plenitude ('pūrṇatvāt') in the Puruṣa Sūkta and from reclining as Inner Ruler within the heart-city of all beings ('puri śete').
meaningDeep: Combining Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.5 (`sa pūrṇatvāt pumān nāma`), Muṇḍaka Bhāṣya 3.5 (`vāsudevaḥ pumān nāmā pūrṇatvāt`), and Aitareya Bhāṣya 2.2.1 (`puruṣa ity antaryāmirūpasyākhyā, puri śete iti`), Madhvācārya shows how cosmic transcendence (Pūrṇa) and intimate immanence (Antaryāmī) meet in Puruṣottama.

padaccheda.gloss: and because He abides in the lotus-city of every body
the sacred name of the Indwelling Lord

lakshanaDeva: अपरं त्वक्षरं या सा प्रकृतिर्जडरूपिका । अक्षरं परमं श्रीस्तु परतः परमक्षरम् ॥ वासुदेवः परानन्द इति त्रिविधमक्षरम् ।
lakshanaIast: aparaṃ tv akṣaraṃ yā sā prakṛtir jaḍarūpikā | akṣaraṃ paramaṃ śrīs tu parataḥ param akṣaram || vāsudevaḥ parānanda iti trividham akṣaram |
meaningShort: Akṣara (the Imperishable, `na kṣarati` / `aśnute`) is threefold in Vedic usage: lower insentient Prakṛti, higher sentient Śrī (Mahālakṣmī), and the Supreme Imperishable beyond the imperishable — Vāsudeva.
meaningDeep: This landmark verse in Muṇḍaka Bhāṣya 3.2 resolves every apparent contradiction across the Upaniṣads and Bhagavadgītā 15.16–18 (`kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate | uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ`): all bound souls are Kṣara (having mutable bodies), Śrī-tattva is Kūṭastha-Akṣara, and Viṣṇu is `akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ`.

padaccheda.gloss: the lower unperishing substrate is insentient Prakṛti
the higher sentient Imperishable is Goddess Śrī
the Supreme Imperishable beyond even Śrī is Vāsudeva

lakshanaDeva: हरत्यघमशेषेण भक्तानां जन्मबन्धनम् । यज्ञभागान् हरत्यग्र्यस्तस्माद्धरिरितीरितः ॥
lakshanaIast: haraty agham aśeṣeṇa bhaktānāṃ janmabandhanam | yajñabhāgān haraty agryas tasmād dharir itīritaḥ ||
meaningShort: Hari (from √hṛ 'haraṇe') is He who completely removes the sins, sorrows, and karmic bondage of devotees, receives the foremost share of all sacrifices, and withdraws the cosmos at dissolution.
meaningDeep: Throughout Sarvamūla, 'Hari' is Madhvācārya's most beloved personal name for the Supreme (`sarvottamo harir idaṃ tu tadājñayaiva` — MBTN 1.29), uniting compassionate soteriology (removing duḥkha and pāpa) with ritual and cosmic sovereignty.

padaccheda.gloss: takes away sin and sorrow without remainder (`√hṛ`)
and receives all Vedic offerings — hence Hari

lakshanaDeva: कृषिः सत्तावाचकः शब्दो णश्च निर्वृतिवाचकः । तयोरैक्यं परं ब्रह्म कृष्ण इत्यभिधीयते ॥
lakshanaIast: kṛṣiḥ sattāvācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛtivācakaḥ | tayor aikyaṃ paraṃ brahma kṛṣṇa ity abhidhīyate ||
meaningShort: 'Kṛṣ' signifies sovereign, all-attracting Being (sattā / aiśvarya) and 'ṇa' signifies supreme Bliss (nirvṛti); their indivisible unity — Parabrahman — is named Kṛṣṇa.
meaningDeep: Grounded in Mahābhārata Udyogaparva 70.5 and Madhvācārya's Gītābhāṣya / MBTN, Kṛṣṇa also draws (`karṣati`) the hearts of devotees and ploughs away (`nikṛṣati`) all sins. Through Viśeṣa, Sovereign Existence (`kṛṣ`) and Infinite Bliss (`ṇa`) are wholly identical in Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

padaccheda.gloss: the verbal base 'kṛṣ' signifying supreme Being and drawing power
and the syllable 'ṇa' signifying plenary Bliss
their non-different unity is Supreme Brahman, Kṛṣṇa

lakshanaDeva: रमन्ते योगिनोऽनन्ते नित्यानन्दे चिदात्मनि । इति रामपदेनासौ परं ब्रह्माभिधीयते ॥
lakshanaIast: ramante yogino'nante nityānande cidātmani | iti rāmapadenāsau paraṃ brahmābhidhīyate ||
meaningShort: Because realized yogis delight ('ramante') in Him — the Infinite, Eternally Blissful Consciousness — Parabrahman is celebrated by the name Rāma.
meaningDeep: In Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya (Chapters 3–9, the Rāmāyaṇa-saṅgraha) and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9, Madhvācārya reveres Śrī Mūlarāma (whose ancient icon he consecrated in the Udupi/uttara sampradāya) as `nirdoṣapūrṇaguṇavigraha` — any seeming human grief in Rāmāvatāra is purely `asurāṇāṃ mohāya` (MBTN 1.37).

padaccheda.gloss: hence Supreme Brahman is named Rāma

lakshanaDeva: नराणां जीवानां सिंह इव सर्वोत्तमो भयहर्ता नृहरिर्नरसिंहः ।
lakshanaIast: narāṇāṃ jīvānāṃ siṃha iva sarvottamo bhayahartā nṛharir narasiṃhaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: उग्रं वीरं महाविष्णुं ज्वलन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् । नृसिंहं भीषणं भद्रं मृत्युमृत्युं नमाम्यहम् ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ugraṃ vīraṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ jvalantaṃ sarvatomukham | nṛsiṃhaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhadraṃ mṛtyumṛtyuṃ namāmy aham ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Formidable, heroic, Mahāviṣṇu blazing on all sides, terrifying to evil yet supremely auspicious, the Death even of Death — I bow to Nṛsiṃha.

meaningShort: Narasiṃha is both the transcendent Man-Lion Avatāra whose nails effortlessly tore apart Hiraṇyakaśipu, and the Supreme Sovereign ('siṃha') over all sentient beings ('nara'), Death unto Death.
meaningDeep: Madhvācārya opened his Viṣṇustuti with the thunderous two-verse *Nakhastuti* (`pāntv asmān puruhūtavairibalavanmātaṅgamādyadghaṭā...`), celebrating the blazing fingernails of Śrī Narasiṃha as infinite Consciousness-Power (`lakṣmīkānta-samantato'pi kalayan naivaiṣituste samam`).

padaccheda.gloss: Supreme Lion-Sovereign over all beings; transcendent Man-Lion
remover of terror and conqueror of death itself

lakshanaDeva: कपिलो भगवानजः प्रोवाच ब्रह्मणे विद्याः । कं सुखं ज्ञानं च पिलति ददातीति कपिलः ॥
lakshanaIast: kapilo bhagavān ajaḥ provāca brahmaṇe vidyāḥ | kaṃ sukhaṃ jñānaṃ ca pilati dadātīti kapilaḥ ||
meaningShort: Kapila is the unborn Jñānāvatāra of Viṣṇu who imparts bliss ('ka') and true liberating wisdom, and of golden-tawny solar radiance ('kapila-varṇa').
meaningDeep: In Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.9 and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('ka' → Kapila), Madhvācārya distinguishes Bhagavān Vāsudeva-Kapila (son of Kardama and Devahūti, teacher of real theistic Sāṅkhya) from any later atheistic distortion.

padaccheda.gloss: who bestows and illumines — hence Kapila

lakshanaDeva: हन्ति समस्तान् दोषान् सारं च गृह्णातीति हंसः परमात्मा । सोऽहं स एवाहमस्मीति नियामकः ॥
lakshanaIast: hanti samastān doṣān sāraṃ ca gṛhṇātīti haṃsaḥ paramātmā | so'haṃ sa evāham asmīti niyāmakaḥ ||
meaningShort: Haṃsa is the Immaculate Swan-Avatāra of Paramātman who destroys ('hanti') all blemishes and accepts only pure devotion ('sāra'), the primal Guru of the Haṃsa-sampradāya.
meaningDeep: In Yatipraṇavakalpa and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10, Madhvācārya explains `Haṃsa` / `So'ham` not as jīva-brahma identity, but as meditating on He ('saḥ') who is the Unabandoned ('a-heya' → `aham`) Inner Sovereign free of every defect.

padaccheda.gloss: discerns and accepts pure essence — Bhagavān Haṃsa

lakshanaDeva: सङ्कर्षणश्च स बभूव पुनः सुनित्यः संहारकारणवपुः । सम्यक् कर्षति जगदिति सङ्कर्षणः ॥
lakshanaIast: saṅkarṣaṇaś ca sa babhūva punaḥ sunityaḥ saṃhārakāraṇavapuḥ | samyak karṣati jagad iti saṅkarṣaṇaḥ ||
meaningShort: Saṅkarṣaṇa is the second eternal Vyūha form of Bhagavān who draws ('saṅkarṣati') the cosmos back into Himself during dissolution and presides over Jīva-tattva and Ahaṅkāra.
meaningDeep: In Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya 1.7 and Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.1.13 (`saṅkarṣaṇaḥ suvarnāmā`), Saṅkarṣaṇa (accompanied by Jayā-rūpā Lakṣmī) orchestrates cosmic withdrawal without any internal difference from Vāsudeva, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha.

padaccheda.gloss: draws the manifest universe back at dissolution (`sam + √kṛṣ`)
eternal causal form of cosmic withdrawal

lakshanaDeva: प्रकृष्टद्युम्नतेजोवान् सृष्टिहेतोः प्रद्युम्नतामुपगतः कृतितां च देवी ।
lakshanaIast: prakṛṣṭadyumnatejovān sṛṣṭihetoḥ pradyumnatām upagataḥ kṛtitāṃ ca devī |
meaningShort: Pradyumna (from `pra + dyumna` — pre-eminent radiance and wealth) is the third eternal Vyūha form of Bhagavān who initiates cosmic creation and awakens knowledge.
meaningDeep: Accompanied by Kṛti-rūpā Ramā (MBTN 1.7), Bhagavān Pradyumna brings forth sentient beings into manifest creation and illumines the intellect (`bhuvo nāmā bāhū pradyumna īritaḥ` — TTB 1.1.13).

padaccheda.gloss: possessing supreme spiritual effulgence and opulence
causal Vyūha form presiding over creation

lakshanaDeva: न केनचिन्निरुध्यत इत्यनिरुद्धः । स्थित्यै पुनः स भगवाननिरुद्धनामा देवी च शान्तिरभवत् ॥
lakshanaIast: na kenacin nirudhyata ity aniruddhaḥ | sthityai punaḥ sa bhagavān aniruddhanāmā devī ca śāntir abhavat ||
meaningShort: Aniruddha ('He whose will and power are obstructed by none') is the fourth eternal Vyūha form of Bhagavān, presiding with Śānti-devī over cosmic preservation and protection.
meaningDeep: In MBTN 1.8–9 and Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.1.18 (`ya eṣa hṛdayākāśas tv aniruddhas tu tadgataḥ`), Aniruddha shelters disembodied souls with their karmas, fashions their bodies from Brahmā downward, and sustains every breath.

padaccheda.gloss: Vyūha form sustaining and protecting the worlds

lakshanaDeva: कश्च ईशश्च केशौ ब्रह्मरुद्रौ तौ वशे वर्तयति प्रेरयति चेति केशवः । अंशुभिर्भासयतीति वा ॥
lakshanaIast: kaś ca īśaś ca keśau brahmarudrau tau vaśe vartayati prerayati ceti keśavaḥ | aṃśubhir bhāsayatīti vā ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: स वायुः प्रकृतिश्चैव विष्टब्धौ केशवेन हि । विशेषतो बृहत्प्राणो भगवांस्तत्र केशवः ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: sa vāyuḥ prakṛtiś caiva viṣṭabdhau keśavena hi | viśeṣato bṛhatprāṇo bhagavāṃs tatra keśavaḥ ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Both Mukhyaprāṇa Vāyu and Prakṛti are upheld by Keśava; pre-eminently, Lord Keśava is the Supreme Prāṇa.

meaningShort: Keśava is He who governs and empowers both 'Ka' (Caturmukha Brahmā) and 'Īśa' (Rudra), and whose luminous rays ('keśāḥ') illumine sun, moon, and cosmos.
meaningDeep: First of the twelve Dvādaśa-mūrtis governing the twelve months and ūrdhvapuṇḍra mudrās (TSS 1.13), Keśava encapsulates Tāratamya in a single three-syllable name: `Ka` (Brahmā) + `Īśa` (Śiva) + `va` (their Master and Impeller).

padaccheda.gloss: He who rules and impels them both is Keśava

englishGlosses: Lord of Vedic speech and Earth
lakshanaDeva: गोभिर्वेदैर्विन्द्यते ज्ञायते, गां भूमिं वेदान् वा विन्दति रक्षतीति गोविन्दः ।
lakshanaIast: gobhir vedair vindyate jñāyate, gāṃ bhūmiṃ vedān vā vindati rakṣatīti govindaḥ |
meaningShort: Govinda is He who is known through the 'Go's (sacred Vedic words) and who rescues and sustains the Earth, the Vedas, the senses, and cows.
meaningDeep: In Sanskrit 'go' signifies Vedic speech, earth, rays of light, senses, and cattle: Govinda is therefore the epistemological goal of all Vedic śabda (`sarva-vedānta-vedya`), the Varāha rescuer of Earth, and Gopāla of Vraja.

padaccheda.gloss: attained and known through sacred Vedic hymns ('go')
rescues and rules Earth, speech, and senses — Govinda

lakshanaDeva: मधुनामानमसुरं सूदयति, कर्मफलमधूनि वा भक्तानां संपादयति शोधयतीति मधुसूदनः ।
lakshanaIast: madhunāmānam asuraṃ sūdayati, karmaphalamadhūni vā bhaktānāṃ saṃpādayati śodhayatīti madhusūdanaḥ |
meaningShort: Madhusūdana is the Slayer of the demon Madhu who stole the Vedas, and the Destroyer of seductive, binding karmic attachments ('madhu').
meaningDeep: Fifth of the Dvādaśa-nāmas and recurrent epithet in the Bhagavadgītā, Madhusūdana removes tamasic delusion (Madhu-kaiṭabha) so that pure Vedic wisdom shines unhindered.

padaccheda.gloss: the demon Madhu and delusive karmic intoxication

lakshanaDeva: त्रीन् लोकान् त्रीन् वेदान् गुणत्रयं च विक्रमतेऽतिक्रम्य व्याप्नोतीति त्रिविक्रमः ।
lakshanaIast: trīn lokān trīn vedān guṇatrayaṃ ca vikramate'tikramya vyāpnotīti trivikramaḥ |
meaningShort: Trivikrama is He who strode across the three worlds with three cosmic steps and whose glory pervades and transcends the three Vedas and three Guṇas.
meaningDeep: Celebrated in the Vedic Viṣṇu-sūkta (`idaṃ viṣṇur vicakrame tredhā nidadhe padam`) and Madhvācārya's namesake Pandit Trivikrama Paṇḍitācārya's *Vāyustuti*, Trivikrama's lotus-foot pierced the shell of Brahmāṇḍa, releasing the purifying Virajā-Gaṅgā.

padaccheda.gloss: the three worlds, three times, and three Vedas
measures and pervades in three strides — Trivikrama

lakshanaDeva: वामं वरणीयं भक्ताभिलषितं नयति ददातीति, मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासत इति च वामनः ।
lakshanaIast: vāmaṃ varaṇīyaṃ bhaktābhilaṣitaṃ nayati dadātīti, madhye vāmanam āsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsata iti ca vāmanaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: नमो भगवते तस्मै सर्वतः परमाय ते । सर्वप्राणिहृदिस्थाय वामनाय नमो नमः ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: namo bhagavate tasmai sarvataḥ paramāya te | sarvaprāṇihṛdisthāya vāmanāya namo namaḥ ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Salutations unto Bhagavān Vāmana, Supreme above all, seated in the hearts of all living beings!

meaningShort: Vāmana is both the enchanting Brahmācārī Avatāra and the adorable ('vāma' = lovely/choiceworthy) thumb-sized Bimba Lord seated in the centre of the heart-lotus, worshipped by all the senses and deities.
meaningDeep: Look at how Madhvācārya opens his Kaṭha Upaniṣad Bhāṣya (`sarvaprāṇihṛdisthāya vāmanāya namo namaḥ`): commenting on Kaṭha 2.2.3 (`madhye vāmanam āsīnam`), he derives Vāmana from `vāma` (auspicious beauty and liberation) + `√nī` (to lead/bestow).

padaccheda.gloss: leads devotees to supreme beauty and bliss
adorable Lord seated in the heart of every being

lakshanaDeva: हृषीकाणामिन्द्रियाणामीशः प्रेरकः, हर्षयितृसूर्यचन्द्रादितेजसामीशो वा हृषीकेशः ।
lakshanaIast: hṛṣīkāṇām indriyāṇām īśaḥ prerakaḥ, harṣayitṛsūryacandrāditejasām īśo vā hṛṣīkeśaḥ |
meaningShort: Hṛṣīkeśa is the Sovereign Master and Inner Director of all cognitive and motor faculties ('hṛṣīkāṇi') as well as the gladdening rays of sun and moon.
meaningDeep: In Bhagavadgītābhāṣya, Arjuna's addressing Kṛṣṇa as 'Hṛṣīkeśa' carries profound philosophical weight: He who rules every sense and mind from within alone knows how to steady the bewildered seeker's buddhi.

padaccheda.gloss: of all senses, mind, and cosmic luminaries

lakshanaDeva: जगत्कारणभूतं पद्मं नाभौ यस्य स पद्मनाभः । हृत्पद्ममध्यगतो वा ॥
lakshanaIast: jagatkāraṇabhūtaṃ padmaṃ nābhau yasya sa padmanābhaḥ | hṛtpadmamadhyagato vā ||
meaningShort: Padmanābha is He from whose navel sprang the golden cosmic lotus bearing Caturmukha Brahmā, and who shines in the nave ('nābhi') of the devotee's heart-lotus.
meaningDeep: Revered in Padārthasaṅgraha 2.14 (`tadodake śayānasya bhagavato nābheḥ padmam abhūt`) and as tenth of the Dvādaśa-mūrtis, Padmanābha unites macrocosmic genesis with microcosmic hṛdaya-upāsanā.

padaccheda.gloss: arising from whose navel / seated in whose centre

lakshanaDeva: दाम्ना भक्त्या यशोदया बद्ध उदरो यस्य, दमादिसाधनैरुदारधीभिर्वेद्यो वा दामोदरः ।
lakshanaIast: dāmnā bhaktyā yaśodayā baddha udaro yasya, damādisādhanair udāradhībhir vedyo vā dāmodaraḥ |
meaningShort: Dāmodara is He who graciously allowed Yaśodā's cord of love ('dāma') to bind His waist, who holds all worlds ('dāmāni') in His belly ('udara'), and who is realized through spiritual discipline ('dama').
meaningDeep: Crowning the Dvādaśa-mūrtis (TSS 1.13), Dāmodara exemplifies `bhakta-parādhīnatva` without compromising `svātantrya`: the Unbound Infinite lets pure love tie Him (`dāmodaratvaṃ bhaktavaśyatvam`).

padaccheda.gloss: bound by love's cord; or holding all worlds ('dāmāni')

lakshanaDeva: स्वरूपतः शक्तितो ज्ञानसुखादिगुणतश्च कदापि न च्यवत इत्यच्युतः । भक्तांश्च न च्यावयति ॥
lakshanaIast: svarūpataḥ śaktito jñānasukhādiguṇataś ca kadāpi na cyavata ity acyutaḥ | bhaktāṃś ca na cyāvayati ||
meaningShort: Acyuta ('the Unfallen / Inexhaustible') is He who never suffers diminution or lapse from His essence, bliss, knowledge, or power — and who never lets His devotees fall.
meaningDeep: Saluted by Madhvācārya in the opening of Aitareya Bhāṣya (`nārāyaṇaṃ nikhilapūrṇaguṇaikadehaṃ sarvajñam acyutam apetasamastadoṣam`), Acyuta refutes every theory that Brahman undergoes real modification or self-forgetting in avatāras or creation.

padaccheda.gloss: never lapses or diminishes in essence or attributes (`a-cyuta`)
and never permits His refugees to perish

englishGlosses: Vanquisher of evil and Refuge of devotees
lakshanaDeva: मुख्यतः सर्वशब्दैश्च वाच्य एको जनार्दनः । जनानसुरानर्दयति जनैर्याच्यते मोक्षायेति जनार्दनः ॥
lakshanaIast: mukhyataḥ sarvaśabdaiś ca vācya eko janārdanaḥ | janān asurān ardayati janair yācyate mokṣāyeti janārdanaḥ ||
meaningShort: Janārdana (from `jana + √ard` 'gatau yācane hiṃsāyāṃ ca') is He who crushes wicked forces, terminates rebirth ('jana'), and is entreated by wise seekers for liberation.
meaningDeep: In Anubhāṣya 1.6 (`mukhyataḥ sarvaśabdaiś ca vācya eko janārdanaḥ`) and Aitareya Bhāṣya 2.1.21 (`prāṇādhāro janārdanaḥ`), Madhvācārya chooses 'Janārdana' to proclaim `sarvaśabdavācyatva` — the supreme referent of all language.

padaccheda.gloss: vanquishes evil beings and ends rebirth
besought by seekers for supreme felicity

lakshanaDeva: मुकुं मोक्षं नित्यसुखं च ददातीति मुकुन्दः ।
lakshanaIast: mukuṃ mokṣaṃ nityasukhaṃ ca dadātīti mukundaḥ |
meaningShort: Mukunda is the gracious Bestower ('da') of liberation ('muku') and eternal spiritual bliss.
meaningDeep: While lesser deities can grant worldly boons within the jurisdiction allotted to them by Hari, 'Mukunda' (`viṣṇur hi dātā mokṣasya` — MBTN 1.78; `mukundaprasādād imaṃ mokṣam` — PS colophon) signifies that Viṣṇu alone holds the key to final release.

englishGlosses: Plenary Lord of the waking state
lakshanaDeva: बहिःप्रज्ञो विभुर्विश्वः । पूर्णत्वाद् विवेशनाच्च विश्वो भगवान् ॥
lakshanaIast: bahiḥprajño vibhur viśvaḥ | pūrṇatvād viveśanāc ca viśvo bhagavān ||
meaningShort: Viśva (first name of the Viṣṇusahasranāma and first pāda of Māṇḍūkya) is Bhagavān as Plenary Fullness who enters all cosmos and governs waking consciousness from the right eye.
meaningDeep: Against interpretations that reduce 'Viśva' to the bound waking ego, Madhvācārya proves in Māṇḍūkya Bhāṣya 1.7 (`eka eva tridhā smṛtaḥ`) that Viśva is the omnipotent Lord ('vibhuḥ') who enables the Jīva's waking experience.

padaccheda.gloss: the all-pervasive Lord directing outward waking cognition
named Viśva from absolute fullness and entry (`√viś`)

englishGlosses: Luminous Lord of the dream state
lakshanaDeva: अन्तःप्रज्ञस्तु तैजसः । स्वप्रकाशाज्ञानानन्दतेजोमयत्वात् स्वप्नप्रवर्तकस्तैजसो हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: antaḥprajñas tu taijasaḥ | svaprakāśājñānānandatejomayatvāt svapnapravartakas taijaso hariḥ ||
meaningShort: Taijasa is the self-luminous ('tejomaya') second Māṇḍūkya form of Bhagavān Hari who illumines inward dream-cognition without external sun or lamps.
meaningDeep: Seated in the throat/manas, Bhagavān Taijasa fashions and illuminates dream-worlds from the Jīva's subtle vāsanās by His own self-effulgent Consciousness (`svayaṃjyotiḥ`).

padaccheda.gloss: consisting of pure self-luminosity — Lord Taijasa

lakshanaDeva: घनप्रज्ञस्तथा प्राज्ञ एक एव त्रिधा स्मृतः । प्रकृष्टज्ञस्वरूपत्वाद् हृदयाकाशगः प्राज्ञो हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: ghanaprajñas tathā prājña eka eva tridhā smṛtaḥ | prakṛṣṭajñasvarūpatvād hṛdayākāśagaḥ prājño hariḥ ||
meaningShort: Prājña ('Supreme Omniscient One', from `prakarṣeṇa jānāti`) is the third Māṇḍūkya form of Bhagavān seated in the heart-lotus, embracing the soul in deep sleep and revered as its Bimba-rūpa.
meaningDeep: In Brahmasūtra 1.3.42 (`suṣuptyutkrāntyor bhedena`) and Padārthasaṅgraha 4.5.3 (`bimbarūpaṃ ca prājñarūpam`), Prājña is explicitly distinguished from the ignorant individual soul (`prājñena ātmanā sampariṣvaktaḥ` — Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.3.21): He is the omniscient Beloved who holds the sleeping soul in restorative peace.

lakshanaDeva: सर्वस्य हि प्रणेतृत्वात् प्राणो नारायणः परः । वायुकेशवयोः प्राणनाम सर्वप्रणायनात् ॥
lakshanaIast: sarvasya hi praṇetṛtvāt prāṇo nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ | vāyukeśavayoḥ prāṇanāma sarvapraṇāyanāt ||
meaningShort: Prāṇa (from `pra + √an` / `pra + √nī` — supreme leader and animator of all) primarily denotes Supreme Nārāyaṇa (`bṛhat-prāṇaḥ keśavaḥ`) and secondarily Mukhyaprāṇa Vāyu, highest of all Jīvas.
meaningDeep: In Māṇḍūkya Bhāṣya 1.12, Aitareya Bhāṣya 2.1.15, and Brahmasūtra 1.1.23 (`ata eva prāṇaḥ`), Madhvācārya clarifies the dual Vedic usage of 'Prāṇa': where supreme independence and mokṣa-giving are taught, Prāṇa is Viṣṇu Himself; as foremost servant, mediator (`jīvanopāya`), and future Brahmā, Prāṇa is Mukhyaprāṇa Vāyu.

padaccheda.gloss: from leading, animating, and directing every being
Supreme Nārāyaṇa (and under Him, Mukhyaprāṇa Vāyu) is Prāṇa

lakshanaDeva: अग्निशब्दोऽयमग्र एवाभिपूज्यताम् । अग्र्यत्वमग्रनेतृत्वमत्तिमङ्गागनेतृताम् ॥ वक्ति विष्णोः ।
lakshanaIast: agniśabdo'yam agra evābhipūjyatām | agryatvam agranetṛtvam attim aṅgāganetṛtām || vakti viṣṇoḥ |
meaningShort: Commenting on the very first word of the Ṛgveda (`agnim īḷe`), Madhvācārya derives 'Agni' as naming Supreme Viṣṇu: Foremost in worship, Supreme Leader ('agra-nī'), Cosmic Devourer at pralaya ('atti'), and Mover of body and limbs ('aṅga-netṛ').
meaningDeep: In Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.1 and Anubhāṣya 1.2 (`praṇetā jyotir ityādyaiḥ prasiddhair anyavastuṣu | ucyate viṣṇur evaikaḥ`), Madhvācārya demonstrates his golden hermeneutic of Vedic polysemy: every Vedic deity-name denotes its cosmic god by ordinary convention, AND supremely denotes Nārāyaṇa (indwelling that god) by plenitude of root-qualities!

padaccheda.gloss: being supreme first (`agrya`) and foremost leader (`agra-nī`)
consuming offerings and worlds at dissolution (`√ad`)
actuating every limb and organ without stumbling

lakshanaDeva: स इन्द्रः परमैश्वर्यादशत्रुः समवर्जनात् । इदं पश्यतीति वा परमात्मेन्द्रः ॥
lakshanaIast: sa indraḥ paramaiśvaryād aśatruḥ samavarjanāt | idaṃ paśyatīti vā paramātmendraḥ ||
meaningShort: In Vedic nirukti, 'Indra' primarily denotes Paramātman Viṣṇu from His absolute supreme sovereignty ('paramaiśvaryāt' — √ind) and direct vision of reality ('idam adarśam' — Aitareya 1.3.14).
meaningDeep: In Bṛhadāraṇyaka Bhāṣya 1.6.19 and MBTN 1.100–101 (citing ṚV 6.47.16–17), Madhvācārya shows how Vedic Indra-hymns proclaim the Supreme Peerless Ruler (`aśatruḥ samavarjanāt`) who humbles the proud and uplifts the humble.

padaccheda.gloss: named Indra from supreme, independent sovereignty (`√ind`)
rival-free, having none equal to Him

lakshanaDeva: तत्तु पूर्णत्वतः पूषा विष्णुर्दर्शयति स्वयम् । सत्यधर्माय भक्ताय सूर्यमण्डलगं मुखम् ॥
lakshanaIast: tat tu pūrṇatvataḥ pūṣā viṣṇur darśayati svayam | satyadharmāya bhaktāya sūryamaṇḍalagaṃ mukham ||
meaningShort: In Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad 15 (`pūṣann ekarṣe`), 'Pūṣan' denotes Bhagavān Viṣṇu by virtue of His plenary fullness ('pūrṇatvataḥ') and universal nourishment (`√puṣ`), dwelling within the golden solar orb.
meaningDeep: Commenting on `hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukham`, Madhvācārya reveals that the dazzling solar disk veils the blissful lotus-face of Satya-Nārāyaṇa, which Lord Pūṣan Himself unveils unto His true devotee.

padaccheda.gloss: called Pūṣan from infinite plenitude and nourishing all worlds
Lord Viṣṇu shining within the solar orb

englishGlosses: exalted Sama chant and Supreme Hari
lakshanaDeva: उच्छब्दवाच्याः प्राणाद्या वागाद्या गीरितीरिताः । अन्नाद्या थमिति प्रोक्तास्तेषूद्गीथो हरिः स्थितः ॥
lakshanaIast: ucchabdavācyāḥ prāṇādyā vāgādyā gīr itīritāḥ | annādyā tham iti proktās teṣūdgītho hariḥ sthitaḥ ||
meaningShort: In Chāndogya Upaniṣad, 'Udgītha' signifies Bhagavān Hari who abides indwelling within 'Ut' (Prāṇa and skies), 'Gīḥ' (Vedic speech), and 'Tham' (sustaining food/earth), and who is chanted aloft as Oṃ.
meaningDeep: A jewel of syllable-by-syllable Vedic nirukti (`ut + gīḥ + tham`) in Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.1.28: rather than treating Udgītha as mere ritual Sāma-chant, Madhvācārya unveils Hari Himself as the living Udgītha celebrated by every Sāma-singer.

padaccheda.gloss: 'Tham' signifying sustaining food; Hari indwelling all three is Udgītha

lakshanaDeva: ऋङ्नामा ज्ञानरूपत्वात् । ऋगर्चनायाः स्वीकाराद् भगवान् हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: ṛṅnāmā jñānarūpatvāt | ṛg arcanāyāḥ svīkārād bhagavān hariḥ ||
meaningShort: 'Ṛk' primarily names Bhagavān Hari Himself because His essence is pure Omniscient Knowledge ('jñānarūpatvāt') and because He graciously accepts all worship and praise ('arcanā').
meaningDeep: In Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.7.5 and Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.2.9, Madhvācārya shows that Ṛk, Yajus, and Sāman are not only the three Vedic corpora (`aparā vidyā` when read merely philologically, `parā vidyā` when read as revealing Viṣṇu — MUN 1.3), but direct names of Bhagavān!

padaccheda.gloss: named 'Ṛk' from being pure luminous Knowledge
and from accepting hymns of adoration (`√ṛc stutau`)

lakshanaDeva: यजुर्याज्यस्वरूपतः । शिरस्तस्य यजुर्नाम यज्ञानां हरणात् स्मृतम् ॥
lakshanaIast: yajur yājyasvarūpataḥ | śiras tasya yajur nāma yajñānāṃ haraṇāt smṛtam ||
meaningShort: 'Yajus' names Bhagavān Viṣṇu because He is the Supreme Object of sacrificial worship ('yājya-svarūpataḥ') and the Receiver of all yajñas.
meaningDeep: Pairing Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.7.5 (`yajur yājyasvarūpataḥ`) with Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.2.9 (`yajñānāṃ haraṇāt`), Madhvācārya grounds ritual action in loving adoration of Yajña-Puruṣa.

padaccheda.gloss: named 'Yajus' because He alone is supremely worshipful (`√yaj`)
and because He accepts all sacrificial offerings

lakshanaDeva: साम नित्यसमत्वतः । साम दोषात् समीकृतेर्भगवान् हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: sāma nityasamatvataḥ | sāma doṣāt samīkṛter bhagavān hariḥ ||
meaningShort: 'Sāman' names Bhagavān Hari from His eternal, unchanging perfection and impartiality across all forms, times, and places ('nitya-samatvataḥ'), and from completely eradicating faults.
meaningDeep: Echoing Bhagavadgītā 10.22 (`vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi`), Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.7.5, and MBTN 1.10 (`ekaḥ samo'py akhiladoṣasamujjhito'pi`), 'Sāman' highlights that every Avatāra and limb of Viṣṇu is equally plenary (`sama`).

padaccheda.gloss: named 'Sāman' from eternal equanimity and equal plenitude in all forms
and from utterly removing blemishes (`√ṣo antakarmani`)

lakshanaDeva: यः पश्यति स्वयं वाक्यं स ऋषिस्तस्य कीर्तितः । ऋषिश्च देवतैकोऽहं तारादीनां विशेषतः ॥
lakshanaIast: yaḥ paśyati svayaṃ vākyaṃ sa ṛṣis tasya kīrtitaḥ | ṛṣiś ca devataiko'haṃ tārādīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
meaningShort: A Ṛṣi is a Seer — not an author — who directly perceives ('paśyati') the eternal, uncreated Vedic mantra by yogic intuition (`ṛṣir darśanāt`); supremely, Bhagavān Viṣṇu Himself is the Primeval Ṛṣi of all Vedas.
meaningDeep: In Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.9, Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.1.21 (`ity uvāca svayaṃ viṣṇur vedadraṣṭā guṇādhikaḥ`), and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.17, Madhvācārya anchors `Veda-apauruṣeyatva`: Viāsa, Viśvāmitra, and Vasiṣṭha are mantra-draṣṭās (seers of pre-existing eternal mantras), never mantra-kartās.

padaccheda.gloss: he who directly intuits the eternal Vedic sentence
is declared the Seer (Ṛṣi) of that hymn

lakshanaDeva: स्त्रीगुणैः सर्वपूर्णत्वाद् बृहती तु सरस्वती । बृहत्त्वाद् बृहतीत्येव वायुप्रकृत्योर्लक्ष्म्याश्च नाम प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
lakshanaIast: strīguṇaiḥ sarvapūrṇatvād bṛhatī tu sarasvatī | bṛhattvād bṛhatīty eva vāyuprakṛtyor lakṣmyāś ca nāma prakīrtitam ||
meaningShort: Bṛhatī denotes the 36-syllable Vedic metre (embodying the 36,000 syllables of Aitareya Āraṇyaka), Goddess Śrī and Sarasvatī by plenitude of auspicious feminine virtues, and supreme Brahman.
meaningDeep: In Aitareya Bhāṣya 2.1.15, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Bhāṣya 1.3.20, and Anuvyākhyāna 1.4.22 (`strīśabdāś ca niṣedhārthāḥ sarve'pi brahmavācakāḥ`), Madhvācārya shows that even feminine Vedic nouns like Bṛhatī, Śrī, and Gāyatrī ultimately celebrate the boundless plenitude of Bhagavān alongside Ramā and Sarasvatī.

padaccheda.gloss: from vastness and completeness of auspicious excellences
celebrated in the Veda as Bṛhatī

englishGlosses: sacred utterances Bhuh Bhuvah Svah Mahah
lakshanaDeva: भूरादिव्याहृतीभिस्तु वाच्यं मूर्तिचतुष्टयम् । महोनामा वासुदेवोऽनिरुद्धो भूर्भुवः प्रद्युम्नः सङ्कर्षणः सुवर्नामा ॥
lakshanaIast: bhūrādivyāhṛtībhis tu vācyaṃ mūrticatuṣṭayam | mahonāmā vāsudevo'niruddho bhūr bhuvaḥ pradyumnaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ suvarnāmā ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: पूर्णो भूतिवरोऽनन्तसुखो यद् व्याहृतीरितः ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: pūrṇo bhūtivaro'nantasukho yad vyāhṛtīritaḥ |
secondaryLakshana.translation: He who is declared by the Vyāhṛtis as Plenary ('Mahaḥ'), Supreme Sovereign ('Bhūḥ'), Mightiest ('Bhuvaḥ'), and Infinite Bliss ('Svaḥ').

meaningShort: The four sacred Vedic Vyāhṛtis — Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and Mahaḥ — signify Bhagavān's four Vyūha forms (Aniruddha, Pradyumna, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Vāsudeva) and His fullness, sovereignty, and infinite bliss.
meaningDeep: In Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.1.13, Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.2, and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.11–12, Madhvācārya reveals that reciting `oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ` before Gāyatrī is not merely naming earthly and atmospheric regions, but invoking the four Vyūhas of Nārāyaṇa!

lakshanaDeva: न जायत इत्यजः, सर्वस्मादधिकत्वाच्चाकारवाच्यो भगवानजः ।
lakshanaIast: na jāyata ity ajaḥ, sarvasmād adhikatvāc cākāravācyo bhagavān ajaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अकारेणाधिकं प्रोक्तम् । अः इति ब्रह्म ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: akāreṇādhikaṃ proktam | aḥ iti brahma |
secondaryLakshana.translation: By the syllable 'a' is declared the Supreme Being who exceeds all ('adhika'); 'Aḥ' directly names Brahman.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Aja / Vāsudeva — the Unborn Fountainhead who surpasses ('adhika') all beings and animates every phoneme.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 ('अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशौ'), Chāndogyabhāṣya 1.1.1 ('अकारेणाधिकं प्रोक्तम्'), Aitareyabhāṣya 2.3.32 ('अकारो विष्णुरुद्दिष्टः'), and Gītābhāṣya 10.33 ('अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vāgdevī Sarasvatī (presiding Svara-abhimāninī) and kośa senses Caturmukha Brahmā and Rudra.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: In Mādhva Tāratamya, Viṣṇu alone is independent 'Aja'; Sarasvatī presides over 'a' as His devoted śakti, while Brahmā and Rudra bear 'a' derivatively as dependent cosmic regents born of Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: अः (पुं.) / अम् (नपुं.) · वासुदेवो रक्षणं प्राङ्गणं चरणः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: aḥ (puṃ.) / am (napuṃ.) · vāsudevo rakṣaṇaṃ prāṅgaṇaṃ caraṇaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vāsudeva (m.), protection/shelter, courtyard or sacrificial arena, foot/solar ray, and glory.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa 1 ('अकारो वासुदेवे स्यात्') and Medinīkośa; Amarakośa 3.4.28–29 treats 'a' under avyaya/nipāta formations.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sixfold nañ-tatpuruṣa prefix 'a-' (resemblance, absence, difference, paucity, impropriety, opposition), vocative/pity particle, and past-tense augment 'aṭ'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4.28 ('अथ नञ् निषेधे'); Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.2.6 ('नञ्'), 6.3.73 ('नलोपो नञः'), and 6.4.71 ('लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुड्यदातः').

meaningShort: The primal syllable 'a' signifies Bhagavān Aja — the Unborn, Supreme ('adhika'), and all-pervasive fountainhead of all speech. Unites Bhagavān Aja/Vāsudeva ('akṣarāṇām akāro'smi'), Tāratamya-governed Brahmā/Sarasvatī, Ekākṣarakośa senses of protection and radiance, and the sixfold Pāṇinian nañ-prefix 'a-'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #1 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] Standing first among all fifty-one varṇas (`akṣarāṇām akāro'smi` — BG 10.33), 'a' belongs to the Viśva-kalā of Praṇava. In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6, Madhvācārya assigns 'a' to Bhagavān Aja (never born, yet generator of Brahmā and cosmos), and in Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.1.1 derives it from 'adhikatva' (surpassing all beings).

padaccheda.gloss: the Unborn Lord; impeller of all
because He transcends and exceeds all beings

lakshanaDeva: आसमन्तान्नन्दति सर्वदोषाभावेन पूर्णसुखस्वरूप इत्याकारवाच्य आनन्दः ।
lakshanaIast: āsamantān nandati sarvadoṣābhāvena pūrṇasukhasvarūpa ity ākāravācya ānandaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशावुग्र ऊर्ज ऋतम्भरः ॥ ६ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: aja ānanda indreśāv ugra ūrja ṛtambharaḥ || 6 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.6), revealing 'आ' → Śrī ānandaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ānanda — He who rejoices fully on every side, wholly untouched by defect or sorrow.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 ('अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशौ') and Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya 1.11 ('आनन्दमात्रकरपादमुखोदरादिः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mahālakṣmī (reflecting Hari's plenary bliss) and Caturmukha Brahmā ('Pitāmaha').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('आकारस्तु पितामहः') names Brahmā 'āḥ', which Sarvamūla harmonizes via Gītā 11.39 ('प्रपितामहः'): Viṣṇu is Father even of Pitāmaha Brahmā, who holds secondary creative regency.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sudden recollection ('Ah, now I remember!'), sentence-reflection, compassion, affliction, and conjunction.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4.1–2 (Avyayavarga): 'आ स्मृतौ वाक्येऽनुकम्पायां समुच्चये' and 'प्रगृह्यमाः स्मृतौ कोपे पीडायाम्'.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Prefix 'āṅ' governing ablative for exclusive limit ('maryādā', up to) or inclusive pervasion ('abhividhi', all the way including), slight degree ('ā-pīta'), and directional reversal ('ā-gam').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4.32 ('ईषदर्थे क्रियायोगे मर्यादाभिविधौ च आ'); Pāṇini 1.4.89 ('आङ् मर्यादावचने') and 2.1.13 ('आङ् मर्यादाभिविध्योः').

meaningShort: The long vowel 'ā' signifies Bhagavān Ānanda — Plenary, boundless Bliss untouched by any trace of sorrow. Spans Bhagavān Ānanda (TSS 1.6), Pitāmaha Brahmā in Ekākṣarakośa, Amarakośa's avyaya senses of memory and compassion, and Pāṇini's boundary/pervasion prefix 'āṅ'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #2 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] With the prefix 'ā' denoting fullness on every side (ābhimukhyena samantāt pūrṇatvam), 'ā' names the second Mātṛkā-mūrti Ānanda, whose very body and limbs consist purely of infinite spiritual joy (`ānandamātrakarapādamukhodarādiḥ` — MBTN 1.11).

padaccheda.gloss: the long vowel syllable 'ā' denoting plenary fullness
Bhagavān whose essence is infinite, unalloyed bliss

lakshanaDeva: इदि परमैश्वर्ये । परमैश्वर्ययोगादिकारवाच्यो भगवानिन्द्रः ।
lakshanaIast: idi paramaiśvarye | paramaiśvaryayogād ikāravācyo bhagavān indraḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशावुग्र ऊर्ज ऋतम्भरः ॥ ६ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: aja ānanda indreśāv ugra ūrja ṛtambharaḥ || 6 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.6), revealing 'इ' → Śrī indraḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Indra — Possessor of absolute, independent cosmic sovereignty ('paramaiśvarya').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 and Ṛgbhāṣya passim: from Dhātupāṭha 'इदि परमैश्वर्ये', Viṣṇu is the primary bearer of 'Indra' and 'i'.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Kāmadeva (Manmatha) and Purandara-Indra as cosmic governors under Bhagavān Pradyumna.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('इकार उच्यते कामः'); in Tāratamya, Kāma and Indra rank at kakṣyā 6, wielding delegated beauty and rulership from Pradyumna-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Indignation/reproach, tender compassion, sorrow/regret, wonder, and perception.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) & Medinīkośa ('इ खेदे चानुकम्पायां कोपे विस्मयसूचने').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Verbal root √i ('iṇ gatau' — going, pervading, knowing) and primary agentive suffix '-i' forming stems like 'hari', 'kavi', and 'giri'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 2.36 ('इण् गतौ'), Pāṇini 1.1.14 ('निपात एकाजनाङ्'), and Uṇādisūtra 4.117–138 ('इञ्/कि').

meaningShort: The syllable 'i' signifies Bhagavān Indra — the Supreme Sovereign possessing absolute cosmic lordship (paramaiśvarya). Links Bhagavān Indra ('idi paramaiśvarye'), Kāma and Śakra in Tāratamya, Amarakośa's emotive avyaya 'i', and the Pāṇinian root √i ('to go, attain, know').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #3 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] While 'Indra' secondarily designates the chief of celestials, Madhvācārya shows throughout Ṛgbhāṣya and Tantrasārasaṅgraha that in parama-mukhya-vṛtti 'i' and 'Indra' denote Viṣṇu Himself (from √ind 'paramaiśvarye'), by whose fraction of power Śakra rules.

padaccheda.gloss: the Supreme Lord of unfathomable sovereignty

lakshanaDeva: ईष्टे नियमयति चराचरं ब्रह्मादिकमितीकारवाच्य ईशः ।
lakshanaIast: īṣṭe niyamayati carācaraṃ brahmādikam itīkāravācya īśaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशावुग्र ऊर्ज ऋतम्भरः ॥ ६ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: aja ānanda indreśāv ugra ūrja ṛtambharaḥ || 6 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.6), revealing 'ई' → Śrī īśaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Īśa — Supreme Ordainer who governs Ramā, Brahmā, Vāyu, Rudra, and all worlds.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 ('इन्द्रेशौ') and Īśāvāsyopaniṣadbhāṣya 1 ('ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वम्' — Hari alone is absolute Īśa).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Goddess Mahālakṣmī ('Īḥ' = Kamalā/Padmālayā), second only to Viṣṇu, followed by Sarasvatī and Rati.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('ईः पद्मालया प्रोक्ता'); in Tāratamya, Ramā is Nityamuktā (kakṣyā 2) eternally dependent on Īśa-Nārāyaṇa (kakṣyā 1).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ई (स्त्री. / अव्ययम्) · लक्ष्मीः कान्तिः रक्षा विषादो दया
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ī (strī. / avyayam) · lakṣmīḥ kāntiḥ rakṣā viṣādo dayā
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Fortune/sovereignty (f.), lustre, protection, and indeclinable of grief, perception, or compassion.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) and Hemacandra Ekākṣarakāṇḍa ('ई स्त्रियां कमलायाम्, अव्ययं तु रुजार्थके').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Feminine suffixes ṅīp/ṅīṣ/ṅīn ('devī', 'gaurī', 'nārī') and transformative suffix 'cvi' ('śuklī-karoti').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.5 ('ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप्'), 4.1.40–41 ('षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च'), and 5.4.50 ('च्विः').

meaningShort: The long vowel 'ī' signifies Bhagavān Īśa — the omnipotent Inner Ruler even of Brahmā, Lakṣmī, Vāyu, and Rudra. Harmonizes Bhagavān Īśa (TSS 1.6), Ekākṣarakośa's 'Ī = Mahālakṣmī', Amarakośa's avyaya senses of compassion/pain, and Pāṇini's feminine '-ī' (ṅīp/ṅīṣ).
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #4 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] From √īś ('aiśvarye'), 'ī' proclaims the Lord's effortless governance (`īśāvāsyam idaṃ sarvam`). Even eternally liberated Ramā and all deities act solely under the ordaining glance of Īśa.

padaccheda.gloss: rules and directs all sentient and insentient beings

lakshanaDeva: उत्कृष्टबलतेजस्त्वादसुराणां भयावहत्वाच्चोकारवाच्य उग्रः ।
lakshanaIast: utkṛṣṭabalatejastvād asurāṇāṃ bhayāvahatvāc cokāravācya ugraḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: उकारेणोच्चमुच्यते ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: ukāreṇoccam ucyate |
secondaryLakshana.translation: By the syllable 'u' is declared He who stands loftiest above all ('ucca').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ugra — Supremely Exalted ('ucca') above all tattvas and fierce against adharma.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 ('उग्र ऊर्जः') and Chāndogyabhāṣya 1.1.1 ('उकारेणोच्चमुच्यते' — 'u' in Oṃ proclaims Hari's supreme loftiness).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Rudra ('Śaṅkara'), Caturmukha Brahmā, and Soma as kośa deities subordinate to Hari.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('उकारः शङ्करः प्रोक्तः'); in Mādhva samanvaya, 'Śaṅkara' primarily names mokṣa-giving Viṣṇu and secondarily Rudra (kakṣyā 4), who meditates constantly on Ugra-Nṛsiṃha.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Calling/address, tender compassion, displeasure/command, and verse-completing particle.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) and Medinīkośa ('उ स्यात्सम्बोधने कोपे पादपूरणयोरपि').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Enclitic Vedic/classical particle 'u' ('kim u', 'atho = atha + u') and desiderative agent suffix '-u' ('mumukṣu', 'jijñāsu', 'bhikṣu').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.17–18 ('उञः'), 8.3.33, and 3.2.168 ('सनाशंसभिक्ष उः').

meaningShort: The syllable 'u' signifies Bhagavān Ugra — fierce in irresistible majesty and supreme loftiness ('uccatva'). Unites Praṇava's second phoneme ('ukāreṇoccam ucyate' / Bhagavān Ugra) with Tāratamya-governed Rudra/Brahmā and the Vedic-Pāṇinian particle 'u'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #5 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] As the second constituent of Praṇava (A-U-M) and fifth Mātṛkā letter, 'u' signifies both the Lord's transcendent elevation (`uccatva` — CHU 1.1.1) and His formidable, evil-shattering might as Ugra (`mṛgaṃ na bhīmam upahatnum ugram` — ṚV 1.154 / MBTN 1.62).

lakshanaDeva: ऊर्ज प्राणबलयोः । अपरिमितबलप्राणप्रदत्वादूकारवाच्य ऊर्जः ।
lakshanaIast: ūrja prāṇabalayoḥ | aparimitabalaprāṇapradatvād ūkāravācya ūrjaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशावुग्र ऊर्ज ऋतम्भरः ॥ ६ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: aja ānanda indreśāv ugra ūrja ṛtambharaḥ || 6 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.6), revealing 'ऊ' → Śrī ūrjaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ūrja — Infinite Reservoir of spiritual strength and Cosmic Protector ('ūḥ' from √av).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 ('उग्र ऊर्जः'); Dhātupāṭha 'ऊर्ज बलप्राणनयोः' and 'अव रक्षणे'.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa (supreme bearer of vital 'ūrj'), Candra (nourishing soma), and Rudra.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ऊकारो भैरवः स्मृतः, चन्द्रमाश्च'); in Tāratamya, Mukhyaprāṇa (kakṣyā 3) channels Hari's 'ūrja' to Rudra, Candra, and all jīvas ('वासुदेवबलाश्रयः').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ऊः (पुं./स्त्री.) / ऊ (अव्ययम्) · रक्षकः तन्तुः दया वागारम्भः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ūḥ (puṃ./strī.) / ū (avyayam) · rakṣakaḥ tantuḥ dayā vāgārambhaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Protector/preserver, woven thread, compassion, and particle initiating solemn utterance.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa & Amarakośa 3.4 ('ऊ रक्षणे दयायां च वागारम्भेऽव्ययं मतम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Monosyllabic root-noun 'ūḥ' formed from √av ('to protect, weave, satisfy') + zero-suffix kvip with 'ūṭh' vocalization.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.4.20 ('ज्वरत्वरस्रिव्यविमवामुपधायाश्च' — 'av' takes 'ūṭh' before kvip → 'ūḥ').

meaningShort: The long vowel 'ū' signifies Bhagavān Ūrja — inexhaustible vital vigour and infinite spiritual strength. Joins Bhagavān Ūrja (TSS 1.6) and Pāṇinian 'ūḥ = Protector' (√av + kvip) with Mukhyaprāṇa/Soma and Ekākṣarakośa senses of protection and compassion.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #6 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] Derived from √ūrj ('bala-prāṇanayoḥ'), 'ū' reveals Bhagavān as Ūrja: the self-sustaining reservoir of cosmic energy who invigorates Prāṇa, senses, and elements without ever diminishing.

padaccheda.gloss: Bhagavān as boundless vital strength and abundance
bestower of vigour and life-force to all

lakshanaDeva: ऋतं सत्यं वेदजातं यथार्थज्ञानं च बिभर्तीत्यृकारवाच्य ऋतम्भरः ।
lakshanaIast: ṛtaṃ satyaṃ vedajātaṃ yathārthajñānaṃ ca bibhartīty ṛkāravācya ṛtambharaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अज आनन्द इन्द्रेशावुग्र ऊर्ज ऋतम्भरः ॥ ६ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: aja ānanda indreśāv ugra ūrja ṛtambharaḥ || 6 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.6), revealing 'ऋ' → Śrī ṛtambharaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṛtambhara — Bearer of unerring cognition, eternal Veda, and moral-cosmic order ('ṛta').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.6 ('ऋतम्भरः') and Taittirīyabhāṣya 1.2.11 ('ऋतं ज्ञानततेर्दाता').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Ramā/Sarasvatī as Veda-mātā, Aditi (mother of Ādityas), and Sūrya-Agni guarding cosmic law.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ऋकारो देवमाता च वाणी सत्यं च कथ्यते'); harmonized in Tāratamya with Śrī as supreme Veda-abhimāninī under Ṛtambhara-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ऋ (स्त्री./अव्ययम्) · वाक्यं सत्यं स्वर्गो निन्दा हास्यम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ṛ (strī./avyayam) · vākyaṃ satyaṃ svargo nindā hāsyam
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sacred speech/maxim, truth, celestial realm, and interjection of derision or awe.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('ऋ वाक्ये हास्यनिन्दायां देवमातरि नाकिषु').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root √ṛ ('ṛ gatau prāpaṇe ca' — 1st & 3rd gaṇas: 'arati', 'iyarti') and vocalic stem ending of agent/kinship nouns ('dhātṛ', 'kartṛ', 'pitṛ').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 1.983 & 3.16 ('ऋ गतौ'); Pāṇini 3.1.133 ('ण्वुल्तृचौ').

meaningShort: The vocalic 'ṛ' signifies Bhagavān Ṛtambhara — the Upholder of cosmic order, unerring truth, and eternal Veda. Links Bhagavān Ṛtambhara (TSS 1.6), Deva-mātā/Vāk and Agni-Sūrya in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa senses of Veda and heaven, and the root √ṛ ('gatau prāpaṇe ca').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #7 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] In Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.2.11 (`ṛtaṃ jñānatater dātā`), Madhvācārya explains 'Ṛta' as exact, unerring knowledge and moral-cosmic order; 'ṛ' invokes Ṛtambhara Hari who bears and sustains truth in the hearts of seers.

padaccheda.gloss: sustainer of eternal truth and Vedic order

lakshanaDeva: ॠन् पापरूपानज्ञानसंघान् हन्तीति ॠकारवाच्यो भगवान् ॠघः ।
lakshanaIast: ṝn pāparūpān ajñānasaṃghān hantīti ṝkāravācyo bhagavān ṝghaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ॠ' → Śrī ṝghaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṝgha — Destroyer of hosts of sin, ignorance, and demonic obstructions.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('ॠघलृशौ') — closing the first octet (Viśva-pāda) of Praṇava-mūrtis.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhāratī-devī (dispelling inner darkness) and kośa sense Diti (kept in cosmic check by Viṣṇu).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ॠकारो दितिरीरिता'); Tattvavāda distinguishes auspicious Mātṛkā-presiding Bhāratī (kakṣyā 3) from Diti while showing Hari's absolute rulership over both.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Movement/course, auspicious welfare, utterance, and awe/terror inspired in foes.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa & Hemacandra Ekākṣarakāṇḍa ('ॠ भद्रे गमने वाक्ये भये दित्यां च कीर्तितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Long vocalic root √ṝ (9th class Kryādi: 'īrṇāti' — to go, pervade, scatter, or strike) and genitive plural sandhi vowel ('pitṝṇām').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 9.27 ('ॠ गतौ') and Pāṇini 6.4.3 ('नामि' — lengthening to 'ṝ').

meaningShort: The long vocalic 'ṝ' signifies Bhagavān Ṝgha — the destroyer of hosts of sin, affliction, and spiritual darkness. Unites Bhagavān Ṝgha (TSS 1.7, slayer of dark obstructions) with Tāratamya-governed Mātṛkā deities, Ekākṣarakośa senses of steadfastness/speech, and Pāṇini's root √ṝ.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #8 · Svara · Praṇava-Akāra (Viśva-pāda)] Completing the first octet (Viśva-varga) of Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 (`ṝghalṛśau`), 'ṝ' names the rare Tantric-Vaidika Mūrti Ṝgha (from 'ṝ' + √han → gha), who slays the obstructive forces besetting seekers.

padaccheda.gloss: slayer of afflictions and dark obstructions

englishGlosses: Ḷśa — Sovereign Lord of Bhūdevī & Śakti
lakshanaDeva: ऌर्भूमादेवीशैललोकानां शासक ईश इति ऌकारवाच्यो ऌशः ।
lakshanaIast: ḷr bhūmādevīśailalokānāṃ śāsaka īśa iti ḷkāravācyo ḷśaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ऌ' → Śrī ḷśaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ḷśa — Supreme Consort and Ruler of Bhūdevī, the worlds, and divine potencies.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('ॠघलृशौ') — first Mūrti of the Taijasa-pāda of Praṇava.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhūdevī (form of Nityamuktā Mahālakṣmī sustaining creation) and celestial mother Aditi.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ऌकारो भूमिरीरिता देवमाता च कथ्यते'); in Tattvasaṅkhyāna, Bhū-rūpiṇī Śrī is the immediate dependent consort of Viṣṇu.
