ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Earth/ground, mountain fastness, cosmic substratum, and tender maternal support.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Tantric Varṇakośa ('ऌर्भूमौ पर्वते शक्तौ').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vocalic phoneme in Śivasūtra 2 ('ṛḷk'), realized in √kḷp ('kṛpū sāmarthye' → 'kalpate', 'kḷpta') and Pāṇinian lakāra symbols 'lṛṭ' (future) and 'lṛṅ' (conditional).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Māheśvarasūtra 2 ('ऋऌक्'); Pāṇini 1.1.9 (savarṇa with 'ṛ' by kātyāyana-vārttika 'ऋऌवर्णयोर्मिथः सावर्ण्यं वाच्यम्') and 8.2.18 ('कृपो रो लः').

meaningShort: The vocalic 'ḷ' signifies Bhagavān Ḷśa — the Sovereign Lord of Bhūdevī, the terrestrial realms, and divine śakti. Connects Bhagavān Ḷśa (TSS 1.7, Sovereign of Bhūdevī), Bhū-tattva in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa senses of earth and mountain, and Pāṇini's vocalic 'ḷ' (√kḷp).
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #9 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] Opening the second octet (Taijasa-varga) of Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7, 'ḷ' denotes divine earth/support and śakti; combined with 'īśa', Ḷśa is Viṣṇu as Lord of Bhū-tattva and sustainer of worlds.

padaccheda.gloss: Lord of Earth (Bhū) and divine potencies

lakshanaDeva: ॡन् दैत्यान् लोकबाधकान् जयतीति ॡकारवाच्यो भगवान् ॡजिः ।
lakshanaIast: ḹn daityān lokabādhakān jayatīti ḹkāravācyo bhagavān ḹjiḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ॡ' → Śrī ḹjiḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ḹji — Ever-Victorious Conqueror of all worlds and demonic obstructors.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('लॄजिरेकात्मैरः') and Bṛhadāraṇyakabhāṣya ('अपरजिता सेना भगवान् जिष्णुरुत्तमः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Durgā-rūpiṇī Mahālakṣmī (unconquered presiding energy of Hari) and the Mātṛkā goddesses.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ॡकारो देवमातृका'); in Mādhva Tattvaviveka/MBTN, Durgā is first Śrī-tattva Herself executing Ḹji-Nārāyaṇa's triumph.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Spiritual accomplishment (siddhi), mother/origin, nature, and unshakable fortitude.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa & Varṇābhidhāna ('ॡकारः सिद्धिमोक्षयोः मातृकाप्रकृतिष्वपि').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ॡ (दीर्घसवर्णः) · अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः (ऌ + ऌ → ॡ)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ḹ (dīrghasavarṇaḥ) · akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ (ḷ + ḷ → ḹ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Long vocalic counterpart of 'ḷ' produced in Pāṇinian savarṇa-dīrgha sandhi ('hotṛ + ḷkāraḥ → hotṝkāraḥ / hotḹkāraḥ').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.101 ('अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः') with Siddhāntakaumudī savarṇa-prakriyā.

meaningShort: The long vocalic 'ḹ' signifies Bhagavān Ḹji — the ever-victorious conqueror of all worlds and daitya-forces. Crowns vocalic 'ḹ' with Bhagavān Ḹji (TSS 1.7, unconquered victor over daityas), Śrī-Durgā śakti in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa's maternal/siddhi senses, and Pāṇinian savarṇa lengthening.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #10 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 (`lṝjir ekātmaira`), 'ḹ' names Bhagavān Ḹji (with agentive `-ji` from √ji 'to conquer'), proclaiming His unconquered supremacy (`aparājitā senā bhagavān, jiṣṇur uttamaḥ` — BR 2.1.6).

lakshanaDeva: एकः सर्वोत्तमः स्वसमोपाधिरहित आत्मा स्वामीत्येकारवाच्य एकात्मा ।
lakshanaIast: ekaḥ sarvottamaḥ svasamopādhirahita ātmā svāmīty ekāravācya ekātmā |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ए' → Śrī ekātmā.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ekātmā — Peerless Supreme Self having neither equal nor superior and zero internal division across His forms.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('एकात्मैरः'), MBTN 1.11 ('स्वगतभेदविवर्जितात्मा'), and Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('एकारो विष्णुरुच्यते').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Ramā and Sarasvatī (uniting 'a' and 'i' guṇa-potencies) and Caturmukha Brahmā.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized in Tāratamya: where Advaita misreads 'Eka' as world-negation, Madhvācārya (AV & VTV) shows 'Eka' means 'pradhāna/sarvottama' — Viṣṇu supreme above real, dependent Ramā and jīvas.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ए (अव्ययम् / पुं.) · विष्णुः स्मृतिः आमन्त्रणं दया स्पर्धा
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: e (avyayam / puṃ.) · viṣṇuḥ smṛtiḥ āmantraṇaṃ dayā spardhā
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Lord Viṣṇu (m.); indeclinable of calling/address ('O!'), recollection, compassion, and challenge.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('एकारो विष्णुरुच्यते') and Amarakośa 3.4 / Medinīkośa ('ए स्मृतावामन्त्रणे दयायाम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Guṇa vowel ('adeṅ guṇaḥ', 'a + i → e'), 3rd sg. verb 'eti' ('goes/attains'), pronominal locative '-e' ('sarve', 'tasmin/grāme'), and ātmanepada ending '-e'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.2 ('अदेङ् गुणः'), 6.1.87 ('आद्गुणः'), and 3.4.79 ('टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे').

meaningShort: The vowel 'e' signifies Bhagavān Ekātmā — the Peerless One without equal or superior, completely unified across all His forms. Integrates Bhagavān Ekātmā (TSS 1.7) and Ekākṣarakośa's explicit 'ekāro viṣṇur ucyate' with Amarakośa's vocative/recollection particle 'e' and guṇa verb morphology.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #11 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] In Dvaita, 'Eka' does not negate the dependent world; it affirms that Nārāyaṇa is uniquely Peerless (`na tvatsamo'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyaḥ`) and devoid of internal division (`svagatabhedavivarjitātmā` — MBTN 1.11) across all Avatāras.

padaccheda.gloss: the Peerless, internally undivided Supreme Self

englishGlosses: Aira — Sovereign Impeller of Vedic Speech & Śrī
lakshanaDeva: इरायाः सरस्वत्या वेदवाण्या लक्ष्म्याश्च पतिः प्रेरक इत्यैकारवाच्य ऐरः ।
lakshanaIast: irāyāḥ sarasvatyā vedavāṇyā lakṣmyāś ca patiḥ preraka ity aikāravācya airaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ऐ' → Śrī airaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Aira — Sovereign Master and Impeller of Irā (eternal Vedic Speech, Śrī, and wisdom).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('एकात्मैर ओजोभृत्'); Viṣṇu alone is true 'Maheśvara' ('महेश्वरं लोकमहेश्वरं च' — BG 10/13 Bhāṣya).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sarasvatī ('Aim'-bīja Vāgdevī) and Rudra ('Maheśa' in Ekākṣarakośa).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ऐकारस्तु महेश्वरः'); in Mādhva Tāratamya, Sarasvatī (kakṣyā 3) outranks Rudra (kakṣyā 4), and both derive wisdom and lordship from Aira-Viṣṇu.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Calling aloud/invocation, sudden remembrance, displeasure, and wonder.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) & Medinīkośa ('ऐ स्मृतौ चामन्त्रणे च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vṛddhi diphthong ('vṛddhir ādaic', 'a + e → ai') forming taddhita derivatives ('ira → aira', 'deva → daiva') and instrumental plural '-aiḥ' ('devaiḥ').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.1 ('वृद्धिरादैच्'), 7.2.117 ('तद्धितेष्वचामादेः'), and 7.1.9 ('अतो भिस ऐस्').

meaningShort: The diphthong 'ai' signifies Bhagavān Aira — Lord and Sovereign Impeller of Irā (sacred Vedic Speech, Ramā, and Bhāratī). Harmonizes Bhagavān Aira (Lord of Irā/Vāk, TSS 1.7) with Ekākṣarakośa's 'Maheśa', Sarasvatī's Vedic speech domain, Amarakośa's vocative 'ai', and Pāṇinian vṛddhi.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #12 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] Formed with vṛddhi from 'irā' (Vedic Vāk / Ramā / nourishment), 'Aira' in Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 celebrates Viṣṇu as Master of all sacred speech and wisdom (`vedamātā-abhimāninī-patiḥ`).

padaccheda.gloss: Lord of Irā (sacred Vedic speech and Śrī)

englishGlosses: Ojobhṛt — Sustainer of Supreme Radiance & Prāṇa
lakshanaDeva: ओजः परं तेजः प्राणबलं च बिभर्ति धारयतीत्योकारवाच्य ओजोभृत् ।
lakshanaIast: ojaḥ paraṃ tejaḥ prāṇabalaṃ ca bibharti dhārayatīty okāravācya ojobhṛt |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ओ' → Śrī ojobhṛt.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ojobhṛt — Bearer of supreme spiritual radiance ('ojas') and interwoven plenitude ('ota').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('ओजोभृदौरसः') and Anuvyākhyāna 1.1.9 ('ओतत्ववाची ह्योङ्कारो वक्त्यसौ तद्गुणोतताम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Caturmukha Brahmā ('okāras tu pitāmahaḥ') and Mukhyaprāṇa (supreme locus of cosmic ojas among jīvas).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('ओकारस्तु चतुर्मुखः'); in Tāratamya, Brahmā and Vāyu (kakṣyā 3) bear Hari's delegated ojas to sustain creation.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Solemn address/invocation, compassion, sudden memory, and awe.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) & Medinīkośa ('ओ आमन्त्रणे दयायां च स्मृतौ विस्मयसूचने').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ओत् (प्रगृह्यः निपातः / गुणः) · आद्गुणः (अ + उ → ओ)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ot (pragṛhyaḥ nipātaḥ / guṇaḥ) · ādguṇaḥ (a + u → o)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Labial guṇa vowel ('a + u → o') exempt from sandhi when an 'ot'-ending nipāta ('o iti'), and visarga-sandhi outcome ('rāmaḥ + jayati → rāmo jayati').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.15 ('ओत्' — pragṛhya immunity), 6.1.87 ('आद्गुणः'), and 6.1.114 ('हशि च').

meaningShort: The vowel 'o' signifies Bhagavān Ojobhṛt — the Bearer of supreme spiritual radiance, cognitive brilliance, and vital power. Unites Bhagavān Ojobhṛt (TSS 1.7) and Oṅkāra's 'otatva' (interwoven plenitude) with Brahmā in Ekākṣarakośa and Amarakośa's compassionate/vocative 'o'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #13 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] Resonating directly with Oṃ (`otatvavācī hy oṅkāraḥ` — AV 1.1.9), 'o' names Bhagavān Ojobhṛt, who sustains the luminous ojas of sun, fire, Mukhyaprāṇa, and all indriyas.

padaccheda.gloss: bearer and sustainer of supreme radiance (ojas)

lakshanaDeva: उरसि भक्तानां हृत्कमले वसति नित्यानन्दरसपूर्णो वेत्यौकारवाच्य औरसः ।
lakshanaIast: urasi bhaktānāṃ hṛtkamale vasati nityānandarasapūrṇo vety aukāravācya aurasaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'औ' → Śrī aurasaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Aurasa — He who abides intimately in the heart ('uras') of devotees and descends as stainless Avatāras.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('ओजोभृदौरसः') and Gītābhāṣya 18.61 ('ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Ananta-Śeṣa ('aukāro'nanta ucyate') and Garuḍa serving as eternal couch and mount of Hari.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('औकारोऽनन्त उच्यते'); while Viṣṇu is absolute 'Ananta' (infinite across space, time, and guṇas — VTV), Śeṣa (kakṣyā 4) bears the name 'auḥ/Ananta' as His devoted attendant.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: औ (अव्ययम् / पुं.) · आह्वानं प्रतिज्ञा ध्वनिः सर्पराजः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: au (avyayam / puṃ.) · āhvānaṃ pratijñā dhvaniḥ sarparājaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Invocation/address, solemn vow, resonant sound, earth, and king of serpents.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 & Hemacandra Ekākṣarakāṇḍa ('औ स्यादामन्त्रणे ध्वनौ अनन्ते च महीतले').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vṛddhi labial diphthong ('a + o → au'), nominative/accusative dual ending ('rāmau', 'harī' < au), and i-/u-stem locative singular ('harau', 'gurau').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.2 ('स्वौजसमौट्...'), 6.1.88 ('वृद्धिरेचि'), and 7.3.119 ('अच्च घेः' → 'औत्').

meaningShort: The diphthong 'au' signifies Bhagavān Aurasa — He who dwells intimately in the heart-lotus ('uras') of His devotees and manifests as faithful Avatāras. Links Bhagavān Aurasa (indweller of the heart-lotus, TSS 1.7) with Ananta-Śeṣa in Ekākṣarakośa, Amarakośa's vocative 'au', and Pāṇini's dual/locative endings.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #14 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 (`ojobhṛd aurasaḥ`), 'Aurasa' points both to the Lord seated in the cave of the heart (`urasi sthitaḥ`) and to His pure, non-different Avatāras (`svāṃśa` / `pūrṇa-prādurbhāva`) who descend without material taint.

padaccheda.gloss: indweller of the heart ('uras'); pure self-manifestation
abides within the lotus of the heart

englishGlosses: Anta — Inner Ruler & Ultimate Goal Hari
lakshanaDeva: अन्तयति संहरति विश्वम्, अन्तर्गतो नियमयति च सर्वमित्यनुस्वारवाच्योऽन्तः ।
lakshanaIast: antayati saṃharati viśvam, antargato niyamayati ca sarvam ity anusvāravācyo'ntaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'अं' → Śrī antaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Anta — Indwelling Controller ('antaryāmī'), Final Goal of all Vedas, and Dissolver of worlds at mahāpralaya.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः') and Bṛhadāraṇyakabhāṣya 3.7 ('य आत्मनि तिष्ठन्... अन्तर्यमयति').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mahālakṣmī (presiding over Praṇava-bindu), Mukhyaprāṇa, and Soma-amṛta.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa links bindu 'aṃ' to Parabrahman and amṛta-soma; in Tāratamya, Ramā and Prāṇa mediate the bindu-kalā grace of Anta-Nārāyaṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Swiftly/quickly, auspiciousness, nectar-drop, and fullness.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) & Ekākṣarakośa ('अं परब्रह्मणि प्रोक्तममृते मङ्गलेऽपि च').

ekaksharaSenses.formIast: aṃ (anusvāraḥ) / -am (dvitīyā · ṇamul) · mo'nusvāraḥ ābhīkṣṇye ṇamul ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Anusvāra nasalization ('mo'nusvāraḥ'), neuter nom./acc. '-am' ('jñānam'), and iterative absolutive 'ṇamul' ('pāyam-pāyam', 'smāram-smāram').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.23 ('मोऽनुस्वारः'), 7.1.24 ('अतोऽम्'), and 3.4.22 ('आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल् च').

meaningShort: The anusvāra 'aṃ' signifies Bhagavān Anta — the Ultimate Consummation, Inner Controller ('antaryāmī'), and Dissolver of worlds at pralaya. Combines Bhagavān Anta (Inner Controller & Cosmic Consummation, TSS 1.7) with Praṇava-bindu, Ekākṣarakośa's auspiciousness/nectar senses, and Pāṇini's '-am' & 'ṇamul'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #15 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] As the fifteenth svara-unit (`anto'rdhagarbhaḥ` — TSS 1.7), 'aṃ' reveals Hari as Anta: both the final resting goal of all śāstras (`vedānta-vedya`) and the indwelling Antaryāmī who gathers all beings into His belly at mahāpralaya.

padaccheda.gloss: the Ultimate Goal, Inner Ruler, and Cosmic Dissolver

englishGlosses: Ardhagarbha — Cradler of Worlds in One Fraction
lakshanaDeva: अर्धे स्वांशे उदरैकदेशे गर्भीकृतं समस्तं जगद्येन स विसर्गवाच्योऽर्धगर्भः ।
lakshanaIast: ardhe svāṃśe udaraikadeśe garbhīkṛtaṃ samastaṃ jagad yena sa visargavācyo'rdhagarbhaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अः इति ब्रह्म । तत्रागतमहमिति ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: aḥ iti brahma | tatrāgatam aham iti |
secondaryLakshana.translation: 'Aḥ' is Brahman Himself; from resting in Him arises the name 'Aham'.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ardhagarbha & Parabrahman — He who holds all universes effortlessly within a tiny fraction of His infinite form ('Aḥ iti Brahma').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Aitareyopaniṣadbhāṣya 2.3.32 ('अः इति ब्रह्म । तत्रागतमहमिति'), Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः'), and Gītā 10.42 ('एकांशेन स्थितो जगत्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sarasvatī (completing the sixteen svara-kalās), Rudra, and Sūrya.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('अः श्रीकण्ठः सुरेश्वरः'); Madhvācārya's Aitareyabhāṣya establishes that 'Aḥ' is primarily Parabrahman Viṣṇu, while Rudra and Sūrya bear the title by His indwelling presence.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Creative emission (visarga), solar radiance, origin, and exclamation of awe or resolve.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('अः परब्रह्मणि प्रोक्तो विसर्गे तेजसि स्मृतः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Visarjanīya realized from final '-s / -r' before voiceless consonants or pause, marking masculine nominative singular ('devaḥ', 'hariḥ') and verbal dual/2nd sg.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.15 ('खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः') and 8.2.66 ('ससजुषो रुः').

meaningShort: The visarga 'aḥ' signifies Bhagavān Ardhagarbha — He who holds the entire cosmos effortlessly within a tiny fraction of His infinite being — and in Aitareya Śruti directly names Brahman ('Aḥ iti Brahma'). Crowns the 16 Svaras with Aitareya Śruti's 'Aḥ iti Brahma' and TSS 1.7's 'Ardhagarbha', harmonized with Tāratamya-governed Rudra/Sūrya and Pāṇinian visarga.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #16 · Svara · Praṇava-Ukāra (Taijasa-pāda)] Closing the sixteen Svaras, 'aḥ' carries dual majesty in Madhvācārya's works: in Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 He is Ardhagarbha (cradling all brahmāṇḍas in a fraction of His form, `ekāṃśena sthito jagat` — BG 10.42), and in Aitareya Bhāṣya 2.3.32 'Aḥ' is the primeval Vedic name of Parabrahman.

padaccheda.gloss: holding all worlds as an embryo in a fraction of His being

lakshanaDeva: कं सुखं ज्ञानं च पिलति ददाति पाति वेति ककारवाच्यः कपिलः ।
lakshanaIast: kaṃ sukhaṃ jñānaṃ ca pilati dadāti pāti veti kakāravācyaḥ kapilaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: कपिलो भगवानजः प्रोवाच ब्रह्मणे विद्याः ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: kapilo bhagavān ajaḥ provāca brahmaṇe vidyāḥ |
secondaryLakshana.translation: The unborn Lord Kapila imparted all sacred sciences unto Brahmā.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Kapila — Sovereign Bestower of plenary bliss ('ka') and tattva-jñāna; 'Ka' as Supreme Brahman in 'Kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('कपिलः'), Chāndogyabhāṣya 4.10.5 ('कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्म' — infinite bliss), and Ṛgbhāṣya / Gītābhāṣya ('प्रजापतिः क इति भगवान् विष्णुः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa ('marut'), Caturmukha Brahmā ('vedhas'), Sūrya ('bradhna'), Agni, and Yama.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3.1 lists Marut, Vedhas, and Bradhna; in Mādhva Tāratamya, Brahmā & Mukhyaprāṇa (kakṣyā 3) and Sūrya-Agni-Yama (kakṣyā 7) bear 'Kaḥ' because Bliss-Lord Kapila indwells and empowers them.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Masculine 'kaḥ': wind, Brahmā, sun, soul (ātman), peacock, fire, light; Neuter 'kam': head (śiras), water (ambu), and happiness/bliss (sukham).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3.1 (Nānārthavarga opening sūtra!): 'मरुते वेधसि ब्रध्ने पुंसि कः कं शिरोऽम्बुनोः' and Amarakośa 1.4.7: 'कं सुखम्' (plus Medinī: 'को वायौ ब्रह्मसूर्ययोः आत्मन्यग्नौ मयूरे च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Taddhita suffix '-ka / -kan' denoting diminution, affection, resemblance, or self-sense ('bālaka', 'putraka', 'svārthe kaḥ'), interrogative pronoun 'kaḥ' (< 'kim'), and Vedic particle 'kam'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.3.70–87 ('प्रागिवात्कः', 'अनुकम्पायाम्', 'अल्पे'), 7.2.103 ('किमः कः'), and Amarakośa 3.4 ('कम् वारिणि मूर्ध्नि शम्').

meaningShort: The first consonant 'ka' signifies Bhagavān Kapila — the giver of supreme bliss ('ka') and luminous wisdom, primal teacher of Sāṅkhya-tattvajñāna. Classic flagship ekākṣara: Bhagavān Kapila & 'Kaṃ Brahma' in Sarvamūla, plus Amarakośa 3.3.1's Vāyu, Brahmā, Sūrya, Ātman (m.) and head, water, bliss (n.), alongside interrogative 'kim' and taddhita '-ka'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #17 · Ka-varga · Praṇava-Makāra (Prājña-pāda)] Across Vedic koshas 'ka' denotes bliss (`kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma` — Chāndogya 4.10.5). Madhvācārya identifies 'ka' with Bhagavān Kapila, the canonical Jñānāvatāra who revealed authentic twenty-four-tattva ontology and bhakti-yoga to Devahūti and Brahmā.

padaccheda.gloss: the first velar consonant 'ka' (also denoting bliss)
Bhagavān Kapila, bestower of bliss and liberating knowledge

englishGlosses: Khapati — Sovereign Lord of Infinite Space & Senses
lakshanaDeva: खस्य आकाशस्येन्द्रियग्रामस्य मोक्षसुखस्य च पतिरिति खकारवाच्यः खपतिः ।
lakshanaIast: khasya ākāśasyendriyagrāmasya mokṣasukhasya ca patir iti khakāravācyaḥ khapatiḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ख' → Śrī khapatiḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Khapati — Sovereign Lord of infinite unmanifest space ('avyākṛtākāśa'), all ten cognitive/motor senses ('khāni'), and boundless liberation-joy ('khaṃ brahma').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('खपतिः') and Chāndogyabhāṣya 4.10.5 ('कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्म' — 'kha' = pervasive, limitless, space-transcending Ānanda of Viṣṇu).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sūrya ('khaḥ sūryaḥ'), Suparṇa-Garuḍa (lord of sky-flight), andākāśa-abhimāni Vināyaka.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: In Mādhva Tattvasaṅkhyāna & Tāratamya, Garuḍa (kakṣyā 4), Sūrya (kakṣyā 7), and Ākāśa-pati Gaṇapati (kakṣyā 10) govern sky and senses strictly under Khapati-Nārāyaṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sky/ether (ākāśa), sense-organ or aperture (indriya/chidra), heaven (svarga), happiness (sukha), mathematical zero (śūnya/bindu), city, and awareness.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.2.1 ('द्यौर्दिवोऽभ्रं व्योम पुष्करमम्बरं नभः... खम्'), AK 3.3 ('खमिन्द्रिये पुरे क्षेत्रे शून्ये बिन्दौ सुखे दिवि'), and Śrīmad Tattvasaṅkhyāna 9 ('खानि दश' — the ten indriyas).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ख- (उपपदम्) / ख (तद्धितः → ईन्) · खगः खचरः सुखादिषु
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kha- (upapadam) / kha (taddhitaḥ → īn) · khagaḥ khacaraḥ sukhādiṣu
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Productive first member in locative aluk/tatpuruṣa compounds ('kha-ga', 'खे-चर' — sky-farer: bird, sun, deva), 'su-kha / duḥ-kha', and Pāṇini's taddhita symbol 'kha' (replaced by '-īna', e.g., 'kulīna', 'grāmīṇa').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.48 ('अन्तःत्यन्ताध्वदूरपारसर्वानन्तेषु डः' / 'खच्'), 6.3.18 ('खेशये'), and 7.1.2 ('आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्' — 'kha → īna').

meaningShort: The syllable 'kha' signifies Bhagavān Khapati — Sovereign Lord of infinite space ('kha'), of the senses ('khāni'), and of Vaikuṇṭha. Bridges Chāndogya's 'Khaṃ Brahma' & TSS 1.7's 'Khapati' with Amarakośa's rich neuter senses of sky/ether, sense-faculty ('khāni daśa'), heaven, happiness, and mathematical zero.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #18 · Ka-varga · Praṇava-Makāra (Prājña-pāda)] In Sanskrit, 'kha' means expanse/ākāśa, the senses (`khāni daśa` — Tattvasaṅkhyānam 9), and unconditioned joy (`khaṃ brahma`). As Khapati (TSS 1.7), Viṣṇu governs both unmanifest space and every cognitive faculty.

padaccheda.gloss: the aspirate velar consonant 'kha' (space / senses / joy)
Lord of space, heaven, and the cognitive faculties

lakshanaDeva: गरुडे वेदात्मके सुपर्णे आस्ते इति गकारवाच्यो गरुडासनः ।
lakshanaIast: garuḍe vedātmake suparṇe āste iti gakāravācyo garuḍāsanaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: ॠघलृशौ लॄजिरेकात्मैर ओजोभृदौरसः । अन्तोऽर्धगर्भः कपिलः खपतिर्गरुडासनः ॥ ७ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṝghalṛśau lṝjir ekātmaira ojobhṛd aurasaḥ | anto'rdhagarbhaḥ kapilaḥ khapatir garuḍāsanaḥ || 7 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.7), revealing 'ग' → Śrī garuḍāsanaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Garuḍāsana — Enthroned upon Veda-winged Suparṇa, Supreme Goal ('gamya') of the liberated and Object of all Vedic song ('gāyatram').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7 ('गरुडासनः') and Gītābhāṣya / Viṣṇusahasranāma ('गायत्रीवल्लभः', 'सुपर्णो वायुवाहनः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Garuḍa (Vedic mount), Bṛhaspati, Vināyaka/Gaṇeśa ('gajānana'), and celestial Gandharvas.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('गकारो भगवान् गजः गन्धर्वो गणनायकः'); in Tāratamya, Garuḍa (kakṣyā 4) far excels Bṛhaspati (kakṣyā 8), Gaṇapati (kakṣyā 10), and Gandharvas, all serving Garuḍāsana-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: गः (पुं.) गन्धर्व-गणपयोः · गम् (नपुं.) गीतम् · गा (स्त्री.) वाणी
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: gaḥ (puṃ.) gandharva-gaṇapayoḥ · gam (napuṃ.) gītam · gā (strī.) vāṇī
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Gandharva/celestial musician (m.), Gaṇeśa (m.), sacred song/chant (n. 'gam'), metric long syllable (guru in Piṅgala-chandas), and praise-verse (f. 'gā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 & Medinīkośa ('गो गन्धर्वे च गीते स्याद् गणाधिपबृहस्पत्योः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada-kṛdanta '-ga' from √gam ('going/reaching': 'khaga', 'uraga', 'aga' = mountain/tree, 'durga') and from √gai ('singing': 'sāmaga' — Sāmaveda chanter).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.48 ('अन्तः... गमेर्डः') and Vārttika 'गमादीनामिति वाच्यम्' / 3.2.8 ('गापोष्टक्' — 'सामगः').

meaningShort: The syllable 'ga' signifies Bhagavān Garuḍāsana — He who rides enthroned upon Garuḍa, the winged embodiment of the three Vedas. Unites Bhagavān Garuḍāsana (TSS 1.7), Garuḍa/Bṛhaspati/Gaṇeśa in Tāratamya, Amarakośa's senses of song and Gandharva, and Pāṇini's ubiquitous compound-final '-ga' ('goer' & 'singer').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #19 · Ka-varga · Praṇava-Makāra (Prājña-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.7, 'ga' invokes Garuḍāsana Hari: moving swiftly (`√gam`) to rescue devotees like Gajendra, enthroned upon Suparṇa Garuḍa who personifies Vedic metre and hymnody.

lakshanaDeva: जिघर्ति द्योतयति तपति च विश्वं स्वतेजसेति घकारवाच्यो घर्मः ।
lakshanaIast: jigharti dyotayati tapati ca viśvaṃ svatejaseti ghakāravācyo gharmaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'घ' → Śrī gharmaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Gharma — Sacred Pravargya-Fire and Solar Indweller who warms, illumines, and destroys sin.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('घर्मो ङसारः') and Aitareyabhāṣya 2.2.1 ('य एष सूर्यमण्डले स्थित्वा तपति भगवान् स नारायणः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Agni and Sūrya (bearers of gharma-tejas) and Rudra (kośa 'ghaṇṭā/kāla-rudra').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('घकारः किङ्किणी घण्टा घनाघनो हरः स्मृतः'); harmonized in Tāratamya under Gharma-Hari, who empowers Rudra and Agni.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bell or rattling ornament (ghaṇṭā/kiṅkiṇī), rain-cloud, blow/striking, and resonant clang.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('घो घण्टायां प्रहारे च मेघे किङ्किणिकारवे').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: -घः (√हन् + टक् / क) · हननार्थे तरप्-आदेशे च (घ = इय)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: -ghaḥ (√han + ṭak / ka) · hananārthe tarap-ādeśe ca (gha = iya)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada agent/instrument '-gha' from √han ('striking/destroying', as in 'parigha', 'nidāgha', 'ṝgha') and Pāṇini's suffix 'gha' (> '-iya', e.g., 'rāṣṭriya').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.3.84 ('परौ घः'), 7.3.54 ('हो हन्तेर्ञ्णिन्नेषु' — h → gh), and 7.1.2 ('घ → इय').

meaningShort: The syllable 'gha' signifies Bhagavān Gharma — the effulgent Solar Fire and Pravargya-splendour illuminating the universe. Unites Bhagavān Gharma (Pravargya-solar radiance, TSS 1.8) with Agni/Rudra in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa's bell and cloud senses, and Pāṇini's '-gha' (< √han, 'slayer/striker').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #20 · Ka-varga · Praṇava-Makāra (Prājña-pāda)] Opening Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 (`gharmo ṅasāraḥ`), 'Gharma' refers to the sacred Vedic Pravargya radiance and solar heat (`ya eṣa sūryamaṇḍale sthitvā tapati bhagavān sa nārāyaṇaḥ` — AIT 2.2.1).

padaccheda.gloss: sacred solar-fire radiance; Bhagavān who warms and illumines
illumines all worlds by His own light

englishGlosses: Ṅasāra — Quintessential Indweller of Senses & Jīvas
lakshanaDeva: ङानां विषयाणां जीवानां च सार उत्तमो नियामक इति ङकारवाच्यो ङसारः ।
lakshanaIast: ṅānāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ jīvānāṃ ca sāra uttamo niyāmaka iti ṅakāravācyo ṅasāraḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ङ' → Śrī ṅasāraḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṅasāra — Supreme Quintessence ('sāra') governing all sense-objects ('ṅa') and conscious souls.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.5 & 1.8 ('घर्मो ङसारः') — proving every varṇa without exception names a distinct form of Viṣṇu.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Rudra/Bhairava (presiding over ahaṅkāra/manas) and the sense-presiding deities.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ङो भैरवे विषये च स्पृहायां च प्रकीर्तितः'); in Tattvasaṅkhyāna, Rudra and indriya-devas operate solely by Ṅasāra-Viṣṇu's inner rulership.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sense-object (viṣaya), ardent desire or yearning (spṛhā), and roaring sound.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('ङो विषये स्पृहायां च भैरवेऽपि प्रकीर्तितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root √ṅu ('ṅuṅ śabde' — to sound) and crucial Pāṇinian 'ṅit' diacritic triggering ātmanepada voice ('anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam') and blocking guṇa/vṛddhi ('ṅṅiti ca').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 1.1010 ('ङुङ् शब्दे'); Pāṇini 1.3.12 ('अनुदात्तङित आत्मनेपदम्') and 1.1.5 ('क्क्ङिति च').

meaningShort: The velar nasal 'ṅa' signifies Bhagavān Ṅasāra — the supreme quintessence ('sāra') within all sense-experiences and sentient beings. Demonstrates Mādhva 'sarvaśabdavācyatva' on rare velar 'ṅa': Bhagavān Ṅasāra (TSS 1.8), Rudra in Ekākṣarakośa, lexical 'sense-object' & 'desire', and Pāṇini's 'ṅit' marker.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #21 · Ka-varga · Praṇava-Makāra (Prājña-pāda)] Even rare grammatical nasals like 'ṅa', 'ña', and 'ṇa' bear explicit Bhagavad-rūpas in Madhvācārya's Mātṛkā system (`pañcāśadvarṇavācyās tāḥ` — TSS 1.5), proving `sarvaśabdavācyatva` — that no phoneme in existence is devoid of naming Viṣṇu.

padaccheda.gloss: the supreme Essence indwelling all objects and senses

lakshanaDeva: चारूणि निर्दोषानन्दमयानि सर्वाण्यङ्गानि यस्य स चकारवाच्यश्चार्वङ्गः ।
lakshanaIast: cārūṇi nirdoṣānandamayāni sarvāṇy aṅgāni yasya sa cakāravācyaś cārvaṅgaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'च' → Śrī cārvaṅgaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Cārvaṅga — Possessor of faultlessly enchanting, uncreated limbs composed wholly of consciousness and bliss.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('चार्वङ्गः') & 1.18 ('चिदानन्दैकदेहवान्') — refuting nirākāra impersonalism.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Candra/Soma (gladdening moon-deity) and Kāma, radiant with borrowed grace from Cārvaṅga-Hari.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('चकारश्चन्द्रमाः स्मृतः'); in Tāratamya, Candra (kakṣyā 7) shines solely by reflecting Viṣṇu's beauty ('तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Moon (m.), tortoise (m.), thief (m.), seed, and spotless purity.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('चश्चन्द्रे चौरकूर्मेषु निर्मले चाव्ययं मतम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Enclitic coordinator 'ca' expressing four canonical relations: secondary addition (anvācaya), collective unity (samāhāra), mutual pairing (itaretarayoga), and simple conjunction (samuccaya), plus dvandva formation.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4.4 (Avyayavarga): 'चान्वाचयसमाहारेतरेतरसमुच्चये' and Pāṇini 2.2.29 ('चार्थे द्वन्द्वः').

meaningShort: The palatal 'ca' signifies Bhagavān Cārvaṅga — He of surpassingly auspicious, non-material limbs composed purely of consciousness and bliss. Unites Bhagavān Cārvaṅga (TSS 1.8, faultless cidānanda form) with Candra in Ekākṣarakośa and Amarakośa 3.4's famous fourfold conjunctive avyaya 'ca'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #22 · Ca-varga · Praṇava-Bindu (Turīya-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8, 'ca' invokes Cārvaṅga: against impersonalism that denies divine form, Madhvācārya affirms that every limb of Hari is uncreated, faultless, and supremely enchanting (`cidānandaikadehavān` — TSS 1.18).

padaccheda.gloss: whose form is pure consciousness and bliss

lakshanaDeva: छन्दोभिर्निखिलैर्वेदैरेव सम्यग्गम्यो वेद्य इति छकारवाच्यश्छन्दोगम्यः ।
lakshanaIast: chandobhir nikhilair vedair eva samyag gamyo vedya iti chakāravācyaś chandogamyaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'छ' → Śrī chandogamyaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Chandogamya — Supreme Purport known rightly through all apauruṣeya Vedic metres ('chandas').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('छन्दोगम्यः'), Gītābhāṣya 15.15 ('वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यः'), and Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 1.1.3 ('शास्त्रयोनित्वात्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Gāyatrī-Śrī, Bhāratī, and Suparṇa-Garuḍa presiding over the sacred Vedic metres.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Taittirīyabhāṣya 1.1.12 ('छन्दसामधिपो हरिः'); under Him, Ramā, Sarasvatī/Bhāratī, and Garuḍa preside over Vedic chandas in Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pure/spotless (nirmala), tremulous, fragment/division (cheda), and shelter, house, or covering (cham).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('छो निर्मले तरले च छेदे गृहावृतावपि').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: छ (तद्धितः → ईय) · तुक्-आगमश्च (ह्रस्वस्य पिति कृति, छे च)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: cha (taddhitaḥ → īya) · tuk-āgamaśca (hrasvasya piti kṛti, che ca)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pāṇinian taddhita suffix 'cha' realized as '-īya' ('bhavadīya', 'pāṇinīya', 'śālīya') and sandhi trigger doubling to 'ccha' after short vowels ('che ca').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.2.114 ('वृद्धाच्छः'), 7.1.2 ('छ → ईय'), and 6.1.73 ('छे च' — 'tug-āgama').

meaningShort: The aspirate palatal 'cha' signifies Bhagavān Chandogamya — He who is approachable and known supremely through the sacred Vedic metres ('chandas'). Links Bhagavān Chandogamya ('vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ', TSS 1.8) with Vedic Chandas-devatās, Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa senses of purity, shade, and cutting, and Pāṇini's taddhita 'cha' (> '-īya').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #23 · Ca-varga · Praṇava-Bindu (Turīya-pāda)] Echoing Bhagavadgītā 15.15 (`vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ`) and Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.1.12 (`yo viśvarūpo bhagavāṃś chandasām adhipo hariḥ`), 'cha' names Chandogamya — reachable through apauruṣeya Veda.

padaccheda.gloss: knowable through the sacred Vedic hymns (chandas)

englishGlosses: born from / sprung of (-ja in paṅkaja, dvija)
lakshanaDeva: जनान् दुष्टानर्दयति सज्जनानां जन्मसंसारं च नाशयतीति जकारवाच्यो जनार्दनः ।
lakshanaIast: janān duṣṭān ardayati sajjanānāṃ janmasaṃsāraṃ ca nāśayatīti jakāravācyo janārdanaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ज' → Śrī janārdanaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Janārdana — Subduer of asuras, petitioned by the wise for release from birth, and Ever-Victorious Viṣṇu.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('जनार्दनः') and Aṇubhāṣya 1.6 ('मुख्यतः सर्वशब्दैश्च वाच्य एको जनार्दनः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pradyumna-Kāma, Indra's son Jayanta, and Bṛhaspati under Janārdana's victorious sovereignty.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Medinīkośa lists Viṣṇu, Śiva, and Kāma; Mādhva Tāratamya establishes Janārdana as independent 'Jaḥ' (never born, 'ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate') while devas are born ('jāta') from His will.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Conqueror (jetṛ), swift/impetuous (javana), born/produced (jāta), Lord Viṣṇu, and splendour.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 & Medinīkośa ('जो जेतृजवनोद्भूते विष्णौ तेजसि कीर्तितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: High-frequency upapada-kṛdanta '-ja' from √jan ('born in/from') with locative or ablative upapada ('paṅka-ja' lotus, 'dvi-ja' twice-born, 'anu-ja', 'agra-ja').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.97 ('सप्तम्या जनेर्डः') and 3.2.98–100 ('पञ्चम्यामजातौ', 'उपसर्गे च संज्ञायाम्').

meaningShort: The syllable 'ja' signifies Bhagavān Janārdana — Vanquisher of wicked forces, petitioned by devotees for liberation from birth ('janma'). Joins Bhagavān Janārdana (TSS 1.8 & Ekākṣarakośa 'jo viṣṇuḥ') with Amarakośa 3.3's 'born-of / swift / victorious' and Pāṇini's omnipresent upapada '-ja' ('paṅkaja', 'dvija', 'manuja').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #24 · Ca-varga · Praṇava-Bindu (Turīya-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 and Anubhāṣya 1.6 (`mukhyataḥ sarvaśabdaiś ca vācya eko janārdanaḥ`), Janārdana is both the crusher of asuras (`ardana`) and the One entreated (`yācita` — √ard 'gatau yācane ca') for eternal welfare.

padaccheda.gloss: subduer of evil; besought by all beings for mokṣa

lakshanaDeva: झटिति क्षिप्रमेवारीन् भक्तान्तरायान् नाशयतीति झकारवाच्यो झटितारिः ।
lakshanaIast: jhaṭiti kṣipram evārīn bhaktāntarāyān nāśayatīti jhakāravācyo jhaṭitāriḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'झ' → Śrī jhaṭitāriḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Jhaṭitāri — He who shatters the sins and enemies of His devotees in an instant ('jhaṭiti').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('झटितारिर्ञमः') — recalling Prahlāda's instantaneous deliverance by Narasiṃha.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Prabhañjana-Vāyu (mighty storm-wind shattering evil) and Deva-guru Bṛhaspati.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('झो बृहस्पतौ झञ्झावाते च'); in Tāratamya, Prabhañjana-Mukhyaprāṇa (kakṣyā 3) and Bṛhaspati (kakṣyā 8) execute Jhaṭitāri-Viṣṇu's swift command.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Tempest/gale (jhañjhāvāta), roaring waterfall, large fish (jhaṣa — cf. Matsyāvatāra), musical cymbal-beat, and lost object.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('झो झञ्झायां गुरौ ताले नष्टे जलचरेऽपि च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pāṇini's 3rd plural verb-ending symbol 'jha' replaced by '-anti / -ata' ('jhontaḥ' → 'bhavanti') and the 'jhaṣ / jhal' consonant pratyāhāras.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.78 ('तिप्तस्झि...') and 7.1.3 ('झोन्तः' — 'jha → ant').

meaningShort: The voiced aspirate 'jha' signifies Bhagavān Jhaṭitāri — He who swiftly ('jhaṭiti') shatters the inner and outer foes of His devotees. Unites Bhagavān Jhaṭitāri (instantaneous rescuer like Nṛsiṃha, TSS 1.8) with Bṛhaspati and tempest-Vāyu in Tāratamya, and Ekākṣarakośa's senses of tempest, cymbal-beat, and cascade.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #25 · Ca-varga · Praṇava-Bindu (Turīya-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 (`jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī`), 'jha' evokes instantaneous protective grace: like Narasiṃha bursting from the pillar in an instant (`jhaṭiti`), the Lord destroys obstacles to devotion.

padaccheda.gloss: instantaneous vanquisher of enemies and sins
swift protector of those who take refuge

englishGlosses: Ñama — Ordainer & Honourer of Chanting Devotees
lakshanaDeva: ञान् गायतो भक्तान् मानयति नियच्छति च सर्वमिति ञकारवाच्यो ञमः ।
lakshanaIast: ñān gāyato bhaktān mānayati niyacchati ca sarvam iti ñakāravācyo ñamaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ञ' → Śrī ñamaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ñama — He who honours chanting devotees ('ñān gāyataḥ') and regulates all beings.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('ञमष्टङ्की') and Gītā 10.22 ('वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Suparṇa-Garuḍa (whose wings are Sāman chants) and celestial singers praising Hari.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized in Tāratamya: all Vedic chant ('ña') offered by Suparṇa, Gandharvas, and sages ascends ultimately to Ñama-Nārāyaṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Singing/chanting (gāyana), bull/leader of the herd (vṛṣabha), and deep resonant chime.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('ञो गायने घरघरे वृषभेऽपि प्रकीर्तितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Crucial Pāṇinian 'ñit' marker conferring ubhayapada conjugation on roots ('pacati / pacate' from 'ḍupacaṣ') and initial/penultimate vṛddhi in suffixes ('aṇ', 'ghañ': 'rāghava', 'pāka').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.3.72 ('स्वरितञितः कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले'), 7.2.115 ('अचो ञ्णिति'), and 7.2.117 ('तद्धितेष्वचामादेः').

meaningShort: The palatal nasal 'ña' signifies Bhagavān Ñama — the Measurer, Ordainer, and Honourer of chanting devotees. Harmonizes Bhagavān Ñama (TSS 1.8, receiver of Sāma-praise and cosmic regulator) with Vedic singer-devas, Ekākṣarakośa's 'singing, bull, chime', and Pāṇini's 'ñit' marker.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #26 · Ca-varga · Praṇava-Bindu (Turīya-pāda)] From lexical 'ña' (chanting/praise, √gai) and √mā / √yam, Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 reveals Ñama as the Lord who receives Sāma-praise and regulates cosmic law.

padaccheda.gloss: ordainer and receiver of sacred chant

englishGlosses: Ṭaṅkī — Wielder of the Divine Axe/Chisel Hari
lakshanaDeva: अज्ञानपाषाणभेदनसमर्थष्टङ्कः परशुश्चक्रादिर्वा विद्यतेऽस्येति टकारवाच्यष्टङ्की ।
lakshanaIast: ajñānapāṣāṇabhedanasamarthaṣ ṭaṅkaḥ paraśuś cakrādir vā vidyate'syeti ṭakāravācyaṣ ṭaṅkī |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ट' → Śrī ṭaṅkī.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṭaṅkī — Iconographic Mūrti holding the divine chisel/axe ('ṭaṅka') in His left hand to cleave hard karmic bondage.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('ञमष्टङ्की') & 1.21 ('टङ्की दण्डी च धन्वी च तत्तद्युक्तस्तु वामतः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sudarśana-abhimāni Durgā/Śrī, Bhūdevī ('ṭā = pṛthvī'), and Mukhyaprāṇa.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('टा पृथिव्याम्'); in Tāratamya, Śrī-Durga presides over Hari's Sudarśana-ṭaṅka weapon while Bhūdevī upholds the worlds.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: टः (पुं.) ध्वनौ वामने पादे · टा (स्त्री.) पृथिव्याम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ṭaḥ (puṃ.) dhvanau vāmane pāde · ṭā (strī.) pṛthivyām
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Resonant twang or clang (dhvani), dwarf, quarter-part (m.); earth and hollowness (f. 'ṭā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('टो ध्वनौ वामने पादे टा पृथिव्यां प्रकीर्तिता').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pāṇinian 'ṭit' marker: (1) on suffixes ('ṭa', 'ṭhak', 'lyuṭ'), triggers feminine 'ṅīp' ('-ī', e.g., 'nadī-cara → nadīcarī', 'kuru-carī'); (2) on augments ('aṭ', 'āṭ'), places them initially ('ādyantau ṭakitau').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.15 ('टिड्ढाणञ्द्वयसज्दघ्नञ्मात्रच्तयप्ठक्ठञ्कञ्क्वरपः') and 1.1.46 ('आद्यन्तौ टकितौ').

meaningShort: The retroflex 'ṭa' signifies Bhagavān Ṭaṅkī — Wielder of the divine chisel/axe ('ṭaṅka') that cleaves the rock of ignorance and evil. Unites Bhagavān Ṭaṅkī (TSS 1.8 & 1.21, chisel/axe-wielding cleaver of ignorance) with Sudarśana/Vāyu, Ekākṣarakośa's bowstring-twang and earth senses, and Pāṇini's 'ṭit' marker (yielding feminine '-ī').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #27 · Ṭa-varga · Praṇava-Nāda (Ātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 & 1.21 (`ṭaṅkī daṇḍī ca dhanvī ca tattadyuktas tu vāmataḥ`), Madhvācārya explicitly describes the meditative iconography of Ṭaṅkī holding the divine ṭaṅka alongside knowledge-mudrā and abhaya.

englishGlosses: Ṭhalaka — Bestower of Lunar Coolness & Sky-Full Joy
object of worship & sphere of vision
lakshanaDeva: ठं चन्द्रमण्डलं व्योमपूर्णं वा आनन्दं लाति ददातीति ठकारवाच्यः ठलकः ।
lakshanaIast: ṭhaṃ candramaṇḍalaṃ vyomapūrṇaṃ vā ānandaṃ lāti dadātīti ṭhakāravācyaḥ ṭhalakaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ठ' → Śrī ṭhalakaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṭhalaka — Gracious Bestower ('√lā') of nectarine coolness and all-pervading spiritual felicity ('ṭha').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('ठलको डलको ढरी') and Gītā 15.13 ('पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Candra (presiding over the cooling lunar orb) and Rudra ('Maheśvara' wearing the crescent moon).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('ठश्चन्द्रमण्डले शून्ये महाध्वनौ महेश्वरे'); in Tāratamya, Rudra (kakṣyā 4) and Soma (kakṣyā 7) derive their cooling grace from Ṭhalaka-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Full disk of the moon or sun (maṇḍala), cipher/circle (śūnya), loud metallic sound, and idol/altar.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('ठो महेश्वरचन्द्रार्कबिम्बशून्यमहाध्वनौ').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ठक् / ठञ् (तद्धितः → इक) · ठस्येकः (धार्मिकः वैदिकः नैय्यायिकः)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ṭhak / ṭhañ (taddhitaḥ → ika) · ṭhasyekaḥ (dhārmikaḥ vaidikaḥ naiyyāyikaḥ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Major Pāṇinian taddhita suffixes 'ṭhak / ṭhañ / ṭha' systematically replaced by '-ika' with initial vṛddhi ('dharma → dhārmika', 'veda → vaidika', 'akṣa → ākṣika').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.4.1 ('प्राग्वहतेष्ठक्'), 4.2.60 ('क्रतूक्थादिसूत्रान्ताट्ठक्'), and 7.3.50 ('ठस्येकः').

meaningShort: The aspirate retroflex 'ṭha' signifies Bhagavān Ṭhalaka — Bestower of nectarine lunar coolness and sky-filling spiritual joy. Links Bhagavān Ṭhalaka (TSS 1.8, giver of nectarine joy) with Soma/Rudra in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa's 'moon-disk, circle, zero, booming sound', and Pāṇini's taddhita 'ṭhak' (> '-ika').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #28 · Ṭa-varga · Praṇava-Nāda (Ātma-pāda)] In Sanskrit ekākṣara tradition 'ṭha' denotes the full moon disk and resonant sphere; in Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 (`ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī`), Ṭhalaka is the soothing, nectar-giving form of Hari.

padaccheda.gloss: bestower (`√lā`) of nectarine coolness and bliss

englishGlosses: awe & fear inspired in foes (bhaya / trāsa)
lakshanaDeva: डयते सर्वत्र विहरति दलयति च भक्ताघमिति डकारवाच्यो डलकः (डरकः) ।
lakshanaIast: ḍayate sarvatra viharati dalayati ca bhaktāgham iti ḍakāravācyo ḍalakaḥ (ḍarakaḥ) |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ड' → Śrī ḍalakaḥ (ḍarakaḥ).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: डः · डलको डरको वा सर्वविहारी पापदलनो हरिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ḍaḥ · ḍalako ḍarako vā sarvavihārī pāpadalano hariḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ḍalaka (Ḍaraka) — He who soars unimpeded across all realms ('√ḍī') and tears apart devotees' sins while striking terror in adharma.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('ठलको डलको ढरी') and Kaṭhopaniṣadbhāṣya 2.3.3 ('भयादस्याग्निस्तपति' — cosmic awe of Hari's governance).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Suparṇa-Garuḍa (lord of aerial flight, √ḍī) and Rudra (wielder of the ḍamaru).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('डः शङ्करे भये शब्दे'); in Tāratamya, Garuḍa and Rudra (both kakṣyā 4) act as awe-inspiring lieutenants of Ḍalaka-Viṣṇu.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Hourglass drum (ḍamaru), roar/sound, fear/awe (trāsa), and submarine fire (baḍavāgni).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('डो डमरौ भये शब्दे शङ्करे बडवानले').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: डित् (अनुबन्धः) · टेः लोपः (डः → खगः पङ्कजम् विंशतिः)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ḍit (anubandhaḥ) · ṭeḥ lopaḥ (ḍaḥ → khagaḥ paṅkajam viṃśatiḥ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root √ḍī ('ḍīṅ vihāyasā gatau' — to fly) and Pāṇini's 'ḍit' marker deleting the stem's final vowel-rhyme ('ṭi-lopa'), enabling crisp monosyllabic finals like '-ga', '-ja', '-da', '-stha'!
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 1.1017 & 4.27 ('डीङ् विहायसा गतौ'); Pāṇini 6.4.143 ('टेः' — 'ḍiti ṭeḥ lopaḥ').

meaningShort: The voiced retroflex 'ḍa' signifies Bhagavān Ḍalaka (Ḍaraka) — He who soars unimpeded everywhere and tears apart the sins and terrors of devotees. Unites Bhagavān Ḍalaka/Ḍaraka (TSS 1.8, soaring everywhere and splitting sin) with Garuḍa and Rudra in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa's ḍamaru/roar/submarine-fire senses, and Pāṇini's 'ḍit' elision.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #29 · Ṭa-varga · Praṇava-Nāda (Ātma-pāda)] Connected to √ḍī ('vihāyasā gatau' — soaring aloft) and √dal ('vidāraṇe' — splitting asunder), Ḍalaka / Ḍaraka in Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 reveals the Lord who strikes awe in adharma and splits karmic knots.

englishGlosses: Ḍharī — Bearer of Cosmic Nāda & Protective Shield
lakshanaDeva: ढान् महानादान् ढक्कादिध्वनीन् महागुणांश्च राति धत्ते वेति ढकारवाच्यो ढरी ।
lakshanaIast: ḍhān mahānādān ḍhakkādidhvanīn mahāguṇāṃś ca rāti dhatte veti ḍhakāravācyo ḍharī |

secondaryLakshana.deva: घर्मो ङसारश्चार्वङ्गश्छन्दोगम्यो जनार्दनः । झटितारिर्ञमष्टङ्की ठलको डलको ढरी ॥ ८ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gharmo ṅasāraś cārvaṅgaś chandogamyo janārdanaḥ | jhaṭitārir ñamaṣ ṭaṅkī ṭhalako ḍalako ḍharī || 8 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.8), revealing 'ढ' → Śrī ḍharī.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ḍharī — Sustainer of cosmic Praṇava-nāda and impenetrable Shield protecting surrendered souls.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.8 ('ठलको डलको ढरी') — fourth Mūrti of the Nāda-pāda (ṭa-varga).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa (vital nāda-bearer), Rudra (sounding the ḍhakkā from which Māheśvara-sūtras issued), and Kubera.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized in Tāratamya: the fourteen Śivasūtras sounded from Rudra's ḍhakkā articulate the eternal varṇa-science whose sovereign Lord is Ḍharī-Viṣṇu.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ढः (पुं.) · ढक्का महाध्वनिर्निर्गुणः · ढम् (नपुं.) फलकं चर्म
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ḍhaḥ (puṃ.) · ḍhakkā mahādhvanirnirguṇaḥ · ḍham (napuṃ.) phalakaṃ carma
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Large double-drum (ḍhakkā), deep reverberating sound, serpent/dog, and warrior's shield (ḍhāla).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('ढो ढक्काध्वनिनिर्गुणे श्वनि चर्मफलकेऽपि च').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ढक् / ढञ् (तद्धितः → एय) · स्त्रीभ्यो ढक् (वैनतेयः कौन्तेयः गङ्गा → गाङ्गेयः)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ḍhak / ḍhañ (taddhitaḥ → eya) · strībhyo ḍhak (vainateyaḥ kaunteyaḥ gaṅgā → gāṅgeyaḥ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Major Pāṇinian metronymic/relational suffix 'ḍha / ḍhak' replaced by '-eya' ('vinatā → vainateya' Garuḍa, 'kuntī → kaunteya', 'rādhā → rādheya', 'pathin → pātheya').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.120 ('स्त्रीभ्यो ढक्') and 7.1.2 ('आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्' — 'ḍha → eya').

meaningShort: The voiced aspirate retroflex 'ḍha' signifies Bhagavān Ḍharī — Bearer of cosmic nāda-resonance and protective shield ('ḍhāla') of the worlds. Joins Bhagavān Ḍharī (TSS 1.8, bearer of cosmic nāda and protective shield) with Praṇava-nāda deities, Ekākṣarakośa's 'ḍhakkā drum, sound, shield', and Pāṇini's suffix 'ḍha' (> '-eya').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #30 · Ṭa-varga · Praṇava-Nāda (Ātma-pāda)] Belonging to the Nāda-kalā of Praṇava (`ṭa-varga`), 'ḍha' names Ḍharī (TSS 1.8), who holds primordial unstruck sound (anāhata-nāda) and shields devotees from calamity.

padaccheda.gloss: wielder of cosmic nāda and protective refuge
protector and sustainer of sacred sound

englishGlosses: cerebralized nasal (ṇatva after r / ṣ / ṛ)
lakshanaDeva: णो निर्वृतिरानन्दो ज्ञानं च, तदात्मकः स्वरूपभूतसुखज्ञान इति णकारवाच्यो णात्मा ।
lakshanaIast: ṇo nirvṛtir ānando jñānaṃ ca, tadātmakaḥ svarūpabhūtasukhajñāna iti ṇakāravācyo ṇātmā |

secondaryLakshana.deva: अर्यते ण आभ्यामित्यरणी ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: aryate ṇa ābhyām ity araṇī |
secondaryLakshana.translation: Because 'Ṇa' (the Lord of supreme bliss) is attained through Guru and Śiṣya, they are called the two Araṇī kindling-sticks.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṇātmā — He whose very essence is 'ṇa' (nirvṛti, supreme spiritual beatitude and omniscience), completing the names 'Kṛṣ-ṇa' and 'Nārāya-ṇa'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('णात्मा तारः'), Kaṭhopaniṣadbhāṣya 2.1.8 ('अर्यते ण आभ्यामित्यरणी'), and MBTN / Udyoga-parva nirukti ('कृषिर्भूवाचकः शब्दो णश्च निर्वृतिवाचकः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa ('Prā-ṇa', leading souls to Bliss-Lord 'Ṇa') and Sarasvatī.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: In Mādhva nirukti ('प्रकर्षेण अणति प्रापयति णं भगवन्तं वा'), Prāṇa (kakṣyā 3) is foremost guide leading jīvas to Ṇātmā-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: णः (पुं.) · निर्वृतिः ज्ञानं निश्चय आभरणं दानम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ṇaḥ (puṃ.) · nirvṛtiḥ jñānaṃ niścaya ābharaṇaṃ dānam
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bliss/emancipation (nirvṛti), knowledge (jñāna), certainty/resolution (niścaya), ornament, and gift.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('णो ज्ञाने निश्चये दाने निर्वृत्याभरणेऽपि च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pāṇinian retroflexion ('ṇatva': 'n → ṇ' after 'r, ṣ, ṛ, ṝ', as in 'nārāyaṇa', 'rāमेण/rāmeṇa', 'kṛṣṇa') and 'ṇit' marker triggering vṛddhi ('ṇvul', 'aṇ', 'ṇic').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.4.1–2 ('रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे', 'अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि') and 7.2.115 ('अचो ञ्णिति').

meaningShort: The retroflex nasal 'ṇa' signifies Bhagavān Ṇātmā — He whose very essence ('ātman') is supreme bliss and unclouded knowledge ('ṇa'). Pivotal Mādhva ekākṣara: 'ṇa = nirvṛti (supreme bliss) & jñāna' in TSS 1.9, Kaṭha Bhāṣya 2.1.8, and the Kṛṣṇa-nirukti, paired with Ekākṣarakośa's 'certainty/bliss/gift' and Pāṇinian ṇatva.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #31 · Ṭa-varga · Praṇava-Nāda (Ātma-pāda)] One of Tattvavāda's key ekākṣara roots! Both in Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 (`ṇātmā tāraḥ`), Kaṭha Bhāṣya 2.1.8 (`aryate ṇa ābhyām`), and the Kṛṣṇa nirukti (`ṇaś ca nirvṛtivācakaḥ`), 'ṇa' directly means nirvṛti — supreme spiritual felicity.

padaccheda.gloss: the retroflex nasal 'ṇa' denoting supreme bliss (nirvṛti)
whose essence is plenary bliss and wisdom

lakshanaDeva: तारयति संसारसागराद् भक्तान् गर्भजन्मजरामृत्युभयादिति तकारवाच्यस्तारः ।
lakshanaIast: tārayati saṃsārasāgarād bhaktān garbhajanmajarāmṛtyubhayād iti takāravācyas tāraḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'त' → Śrī tāraḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Tāra — Supreme Ferryman who carries devotees across birth, old age, and death into immortal bliss.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('णात्मा तारः') and Viṣṇusahasranāma ('तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa (boatman bearing souls to Hari), Candra (nectar-rayed), and Kubera.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: In Mādhva Tāratamya, Vāyu is the foremost 'tāraka-guru' (kakṣyā 3) ferrying eligible souls to Tāra-Nārāyaṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: तः (पुं.) अमृत-क्रोड-नावि चौरे · तम् (नपुं.) धर्मो रत्नम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: taḥ (puṃ.) amṛta-kroḍa-nāvi caure · tam (napuṃ.) dharmo ratnam
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Nectar (amṛta), lap/bosom (kroḍa), boat/ferry (nau — cf. 'tāra'!), tail, virtue, and jewel.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('तोऽमृते पुच्छक्रोडयोः नावि रत्ने च कीर्तितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Past passive participle '-ta' ('kta': 'kṛta', 'mukta'), ablative adverbial '-taḥ' ('tasil': 'sarvataḥ', 'mukhyataḥ'), demonstrative stem 'ta-' ('tad'), and abstract suffixes '-tva / -tā'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.26 ('क्तक्तवतू निष्ठा'), 5.3.7 ('पञ्चम्यास्तसिल्'), and 5.1.119 ('तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ').

meaningShort: The dental 'ta' signifies Bhagavān Tāra — the Saviour Ferryman who carries devotees across the ocean of transmigration. Unites Bhagavān Tāra (TSS 1.9, Deliverer across saṃsāra) with Mukhyaprāṇa-Tāra, Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa senses of nectar, lap, boat, and virtue, and Pāṇini's 'kta' ('-ta') & '-tva/-tal'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #32 · Ta-varga · Praṇava-Kalā (Antarātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 and Viṣṇusahasranāma, 'Tāra' is also a name of Praṇava itself because it ferries (`tārayati`) souls across birth and death; 'ta' invokes Hari as that saving power.

padaccheda.gloss: the Deliverer across the ocean of saṃsāra

englishGlosses: Thama / Thapa — Guardian of Auspicious Shelter
lakshanaDeva: थं रक्षणं मङ्गलं वा मिमीते पाति चेति थकारवाच्यः थमः (थपः) ।
lakshanaIast: thaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ vā mimīte pāti ceti thakāravācyaḥ thamaḥ (thapaḥ) |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'थ' → Śrī thamaḥ (thapaḥ).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Thama / Thapa — Unshakable Protector who measures out and guards the auspicious shelter ('tha') of all worlds.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('तारस्थमो दण्डी', v.l. 'थपः') and Viṣṇusahasranāma ('मङ्गलं परम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Presiding deities of Meru, Himavān, and protective sacred fords ('tīrtha') under Hari.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized via Gītā 10.25 ('मेरूः शिखरिणामहम्' — Viṣṇu's vibhūti in unshakable mountain-stability).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: थः (पुं.) शैले भक्षणे · थम् (नपुं.) रक्षणं मङ्गलं भयम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: thaḥ (puṃ.) śaile bhakṣaṇe · tham (napuṃ.) rakṣaṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ bhayam
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mountain (śaila, m.), eating/sustenance (m.); protection (rakṣaṇa, n.), auspiciousness (maṅgala, n.), and awe.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('थो गिरौ भक्षणे प्रोक्तः थं रक्षामङ्गले भये').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Uṇādi/kṛt suffix '-tha' forming core Sanskrit nouns ('ar-tha', 'tīr-tha', 'ra-tha', 'gā-thā', 'uk-tha'), ordinal '-tha' ('catur-tha', 'ṣaṣ-ṭha'), and 2nd pl./du. verbal '-tha / -thas'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.2.51 ('षट्कतिकतिपयचतुरां थुक्'), 3.4.78 ('सिप्थस्थ'), and Uṇādisūtra 2.2–6 ('उक्थगिरिअर्थतीर्थरथाः').

meaningShort: The aspirate dental 'tha' signifies Bhagavān Thama / Thapa — Guardian of stability, shelter ('tha'), and auspiciousness. Connects Bhagavān Thama/Thapa (TSS 1.9, guardian of stability and auspiciousness) with Himālaya/Meru devas, Ekākṣarakośa's 'mountain, protection, auspiciousness', and Pāṇini's '-tha' ('tīrtha', 'artha', 'caturtha').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #33 · Ta-varga · Praṇava-Kalā (Antarātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 (`tāras thamo daṇḍī`, v.l. `thapo`), lexical 'tha' denotes shelter, mountain-firmness, and auspicious protection; Bhagavān measures out and guards the refuge of all worlds.

padaccheda.gloss: dispenser and guardian of auspicious refuge

englishGlosses: Daṇḍī — Sceptre-Bearing Lord of Cosmic Justice
Yama / Dharma & Agni (regents of moral law)
lakshanaDeva: दुष्टदमनहेतुर्दण्डो न्यायः संन्यासदण्डो वा विद्यतेऽस्येति दकारवाच्यो दण्डी ।
lakshanaIast: duṣṭadamanahetur daṇḍo nyāyaḥ saṃnyāsadaṇḍo vā vidyate'syeti dakāravācyo daṇḍī |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'द' → Śrī daṇḍī.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: दः · दण्डी दुष्टदमयिता मोक्षदो वामनो हरिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: daḥ · daṇḍī duṣṭadamayitā mokṣado vāmano hariḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Daṇḍī — Wielder of the sceptre of cosmic dharma, Ascetic Vāmana, and sole Independent Giver ('daḥ') of liberation.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('दण्डी धन्वी') & 1.21, and Gītābhāṣya 10.38 ('दण्डो दमयतामस्मि').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Yama-Dharmarāja (wielding Hari's rod of justice) and Agni (purifier).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: In Mādhva Tāratamya, Yama and Agni (kakṣyā 7) enforce moral law solely by the authority of Daṇḍī-Nārāyaṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: दः (पुं.) दाने छेदने शोधने शैले · दा (स्त्री.) भार्या तापश्च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: daḥ (puṃ.) dāne chedane śodhane śaile · dā (strī.) bhāryā tāpaśca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Giving/munificence (dāna), cutting/destroying (chedana), purifying (śodhana), mountain (m.), and wife or austerity (f. 'dā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 & Medinīkośa ('दो दातरि च शैलार्थे छेदने शोधनेऽपि च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Canonical Pāṇinian compound-final '-da' from three ā-ending roots: √dā ('giving': 'jala-da', 'mokṣa-da', 'vara-da'), √do ('cutting': 'agha-da', 'pāpa-da'), and √dai ('purifying': 'avadāta').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.3 ('आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः' — 'गोदः, धनदः, मोक्षदः').

meaningShort: The voiced dental 'da' signifies Bhagavān Daṇḍī — Bearer of the sceptre of cosmic justice ('daṇḍa') and the ascetic staff as Vāmana-trivikrama. Unites Bhagavān Daṇḍī (TSS 1.9 & 1.21, bearer of the sceptre of cosmic justice and Vāmana's staff) with Dharma/Yama, Amarakośa's 'gift/purification', and Pāṇini's threefold upapada '-da' (giver, cutter, purifier).
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #34 · Ta-varga · Praṇava-Kalā (Antarātma-pāda)] Echoing Bhagavadgītā 10.38 (`daṇḍo damayatām asmi`) and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.21 (`ṭaṅkī daṇḍī ca dhanvī ca`), Daṇḍī holds the rod of moral order in His left hand while bestowing jñāna-mudrā and abhaya.

padaccheda.gloss: bearer of the staff of cosmic order and ascetic wisdom

lakshanaDeva: प्रणवात्मकं शार्ङ्गं कोदण्डं वा धनुर्विद्यतेऽस्येति धकारवाच्यो धन्वी ।
lakshanaIast: praṇavātmakaṃ śārṅgaṃ kodaṇḍaṃ vā dhanur vidyate'syeti dhakāravācyo dhanvī |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'ध' → Śrī dhanvī.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Dhanvī — Supreme Archer wielding Śārṅga and Kodaṇḍa, and All-Sustaining Dhātā ('dhātā vidhātā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('धन्वी नम्यः') & 1.21, Gītā 10.31 ('रामः शस्त्रभृतामहम्'), and Muṇḍaka 2.2.4 ('प्रणवो धनुः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Caturmukha Brahmā ('Dhātṛ'), Dharma, and Kubera (lord of wealth).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('धो ब्रह्मणि कुबेरे च धर्मे च परिकीर्तितः'); in Tāratamya, Brahmā (kakṣyā 3), Dharma (kakṣyā 7), and Kubera (kakṣyā 7) uphold cosmic order and wealth under Dhanvī-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Brahmā, Dharma/virtue, Kubera (m.); wealth/treasure (dhana) and merit (n. 'dham').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('धो ब्रह्मणि च धर्मे च धं धने सुकृतेऽपि च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada '-dha / -dhi' from √dhā ('holding/containing': 'mahīdhra/dhara', 'jala-dhi', 'ni-dhi', 'samā-dhi') and distributive numeral adverb '-dhā' ('ekadhā', 'bahudhā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.3 ('आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः'), 3.3.92 ('उपसर्गे घोः किः' → 'निधिः, विधिः'), and 5.3.42 ('संख्याया विधार्थे धा').

meaningShort: The voiced aspirate dental 'dha' signifies Bhagavān Dhanvī — Wielder of the invincible Śārṅga and Kodaṇḍa bow. Harmonizes Bhagavān Dhanvī (TSS 1.9 & 1.21, wielder of Śārṅga/Kodaṇḍa) with Brahmā and Kubera in Tāratamya, Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa's 'Brahmā, Dharma, Kubera, wealth', and Pāṇinian √dhā / '-dhā'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #35 · Ta-varga · Praṇava-Kalā (Antarātma-pāda)] In Upaniṣadic meditation (`praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hy ātmā brahma tallakṣyam ucyate` — Muṇḍaka 2.2.4) and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 & 1.21, Dhanvī speeds the soul-arrow unerringly to liberation while guarding righteousness.

padaccheda.gloss: wielder of the divine Śārṅga/Kodaṇḍa bow

englishGlosses: Namya — Universally Adored Apex of Tāratamya
lakshanaDeva: लक्ष्मीब्रह्मरुद्रेन्द्रादिभिः सर्वैर्नितरां नमसनीयो वन्द्य इति नकारवाच्यो नम्यः ।
lakshanaIast: lakṣmībrahmarudrendrādibhiḥ sarvair nitarāṃ namasanīyo vandya iti nakāravācyo namyaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'न' → Śrī namyaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Namya — The Asymmetric Summit of Tāratamya to whom Ramā, Brahmā, Vāyu, Rudra, and all beings bow ('namaḥ'), while He bows to none.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.1 ('जयत्यब्जभवेशेन्द्रवन्दितः कमलापतिः') & 1.9 ('नम्यः परः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa and Bhāratī (leading cosmic 'namaskāra' to Hari) and Vināyaka.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized in Tāratamya: salutations offered to any deity reach Namya-Keśava as their sovereign inner ruler ('आकाशात् पतितं तोयं यथा गच्छति सागरम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pearl/gem (ratna), praise (stuti), binding, unexhausted fullness (m.); wealth and welfare (n.).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('नो बन्धे च स्तुतौ रत्ने सौगतेऽव्ययमभावके').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Indeclinable 'na' denoting (1) negation ('not', Amarakośa 3.4) and (2) Vedic comparison ('like / as', Nirukta 1.4: 'mṛgo na bhīmaḥ' = fierce like a lion!), plus enclitic 1st pl. 'naḥ' ('dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4.12 ('नाभावने च'); Yāska Nirukta 1.4 ('नेति प्रतिषेधार्थीयो भाषायामुपयते, उभयमन्वध्यायम्' — negation & simile); Pāṇini 8.1.21 ('बहुवचनस्य वस्नसौ').

meaningShort: The dental nasal 'na' signifies Bhagavān Namya — the One worthy of universal prostration by Ramā, Brahmā, Rudra, and all souls, who bows to none. Unites Bhagavān Namya (TSS 1.9, bowed to by Ramā, Brahmā, Rudra, and all jīvas while bowing to none) with Amarakośa 3.4's negation AND Vedic simile 'na' ('like'), Ekākṣarakośa's 'jewel/wealth', and enclitic 'naḥ'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #36 · Ta-varga · Praṇava-Kalā (Antarātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.1 (`jayaty abjabhaveśendravanditaḥ kamalāpatiḥ`) and 1.9, 'na' (`√nam`) reveals the asymmetric apex of Tāratamya: every being bows upward along the hierarchy, culminating in Namya Hari alone.

padaccheda.gloss: supremely adorable and bowed to by all beings

englishGlosses: Para — Transcendent Supreme Beyond Kṣara & Akṣara
lakshanaDeva: जीवाक्षराभ्यां क्षराक्षराभ्यां च सर्वथा पर उत्कृष्ट इति पकारवाच्यः परः ।
lakshanaIast: jīvākṣarābhyāṃ kṣarākṣarābhyāṃ ca sarvathā para utkṛṣṭa iti pakāravācyaḥ paraḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'प' → Śrī paraḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Para — Supremely Transcendent Puruṣottama beyond both kṣara-jīvas and akṣara-Ramā, and Absolute Protector ('√pā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('नम्यः परः फली'), Gītābhāṣya 15.16–17 ('उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः'), and MBTN 1.2 ('नारायणः परतमः परमात् स एकः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa-Vāyu ('po vāyau' — cosmic purifier and life-protector) and Sūrya.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('पकारः पवनः स्मृतः'); in Tāratamya, Pavamāna-Vāyu (kakṣyā 3) is the foremost finite servant of Para-Vāsudeva.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: पः (पुं.) पवने शासके पत्रेऽण्डे · पा (स्त्री.) रक्षणे पाने च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: paḥ (puṃ.) pavane śāsake patre'ṇḍe · pā (strī.) rakṣaṇe pāne ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Wind/air (pavana, m.), prince/ruler (śāsaka), leaf (patra), egg, protection, and drinking.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 & Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('पः पवने दलेऽण्डे च रक्षणे पानकर्मणि').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: -पः (आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः) · पा-रक्षणे पा-पाने च (भूपः गोपः पादपः द्विपः)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: -paḥ (āto'nupasarge kaḥ) · pā-rakṣaṇe pā-pāne ca (bhūpaḥ gopaḥ pādapaḥ dvipaḥ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Classic upapada-kṛdanta '-pa' from two Pāṇinian roots: √pā (2nd class 'pāti' — protecting/ruling: 'bhū-pa', 'go-pa', 'lokapāla') and √pā (1st class 'pibati' — drinking: 'pāda-pa' tree, 'dvi-pa' elephant, 'soma-pa').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.3 ('आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः') on Dhātupāṭha 2.47 ('पा रक्षणे') & 1.972 ('पा पाने').

meaningShort: The labial 'pa' signifies Bhagavān Para — the Transcendent Supreme beyond both mutable souls ('kṣara') and immutable Śrī-tattva ('akṣara'). Unites Bhagavān Para (TSS 1.9, loftiest beyond mutable souls and immutable Śrī) with Mukhyaprāṇa-Pavana in Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa and Pāṇini's '-pa' ('protector' & 'drinker').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #37 · Pa-varga · Praṇava-Śānta (Paramātma-pāda)] Grounded in Bhagavadgītā 15.17 (`uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ`) and MBTN 1.2 (`nārāyaṇaḥ paratamaḥ paramāt sa ekaḥ`), 'pa' opens the Paramātma-varga with 'Para' — absolute transcendence.

padaccheda.gloss: Supremely Transcendent beyond kṣara and akṣara

englishGlosses: Phalī — Independent Bestower of Karma- & Mokṣa-Fruits
lakshanaDeva: निखिलकर्मोपासनानां धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाख्यफलप्रदाता फलति पूर्णसंकल्प इति वा फली ।
lakshanaIast: nikhilakarmopāsanānāṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyaphalapradātā phalati pūrṇasaṃkalpa iti vā phalī |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'फ' → Śrī phalī.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Phalī — Sole Independent Dispenser of all fruits of karma, jñāna, and bhakti, culminating in Mokṣa.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('परः फली') and Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 3.2.38 ('फलमत उपपत्तेः' — refuting Mīmāṃsā's autonomous insentient apūrva).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Prabhañjana-Vāyu (ripening and bearing offerings) and Kubera.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized in Tāratamya: devas distribute worldly boons strictly as agents ('द्वारभूत') of Phalī-Janārdana.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: फः (पुं.) झञ्झावाते विकासने फेने · फम् (नपुं.) फलं सिद्धिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: phaḥ (puṃ.) jhañjhāvāte vikāsane phene · pham (napuṃ.) phalaṃ siddhiḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Gale/storm-wind, blossoming/opening (vikāsana), foam/froth (phena), yawning, and fruit or accomplishment.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('फो झञ्झायां फूत्कारे च फलं फेने विकासने').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: फक् / फञ् (तद्धितः → आयन) · नडादिभ्यः फक् (गार्ग्यायणः आश्वलायनः)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: phak / phañ (taddhitaḥ → āyana) · naḍādibhyaḥ phak (gārgyāyaṇaḥ āśvalāyanaḥ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Major Pāṇinian gotra-patronymic suffix 'pha / phak / phañ' systematically replaced by '-āyana' ('garga → gārgyāyaṇa', 'aśvala → āśvalāyana', 'bādarāyaṇa'!).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 4.1.99 ('नडादिभ्यः फक्') and 7.1.2 ('आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्' — 'pha → āyana').

meaningShort: The aspirate labial 'pha' signifies Bhagavān Phalī — the sole Independent Bestower of all fruits of action, knowledge, and liberation. Links Bhagavān Phalī (TSS 1.9 & BS 3.2.38 'phalam ata upapatteḥ', sole granter of fruits and mokṣa) with Ekākṣarakośa's 'fruit, blossoming, storm-gale, foam' and Pāṇini's taddhita 'pha' (> '-āyana').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #38 · Pa-varga · Praṇava-Śānta (Paramātma-pāda)] Echoing Brahmasūtra 3.2.38 (`phalam ata upapatteḥ` — fruits come from the Lord, not from insentient karma-apūrva by itself), 'pha' invokes Phalī Hari, who awards every righteous fruit culminating in Mokṣa.

padaccheda.gloss: independent lord and dispenser of all spiritual and worldly fruits
granter of liberation and every attainment

lakshanaDeva: निरवधिकस्वतन्त्रबलवान् बलिनो निगृह्णाति चेति बकारवाच्यो बली ।
lakshanaIast: niravadhikasvatantrabalavān balino nigṛhṇāti ceti bakāravācyo balī |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'ब' → Śrī balī.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Balī — Embodiment of inexhaustible, independent omnipotence ('pūrṇāvyayātmabalacitsukhavīryasāraḥ') who subdues the arrogant.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('बली भगो मनुः') and MBTN 1.13.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: बः (पुं.) · मुख्यप्राणो भीमः वरुणश्च अपां पतिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: baḥ (puṃ.) · mukhyaprāṇo bhīmaḥ varuṇaśca apāṃ patiḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa-Bhīma (foremost bearer of bala among jīvas) and Varuṇa ('bo varuṇaḥ', lord of waters).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa / Ekākṣarakośa ('बकारो वरुणः प्रोक्तः'); in Tāratamya, Mukhyaprāṇa (kakṣyā 3, 'वासुदेवबलाश्रयः') and Varuṇa (kakṣyā 7) draw all strength from Balī-Viṣṇu.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Varuṇa (m.), water-pitcher/jar (kumbha), ocean, weaving, water, and binding.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('बो वरुणे च कुम्भे च वयने जलसञ्चये').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ब (जश्त्व-वर्णः · बवयोरभेदः) · झलां जशोऽन्ते (अप् + ज → अब्जम्)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ba (jaśtva-varṇaḥ · bavayorabhedaḥ) · jhalāṃ jaśo'nte (ap + ja → abjam)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Voiced labial stop arising regularly by Pāṇinian jaśtva sandhi from 'p / ph / bh' ('ap + ja → abja' lotus/conch, 'ap + da → abda' cloud/year) and lexical 'ba/va' alternation.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.39 ('झलां जशोऽन्ते') and 8.4.53 ('झलां जश् झशि' — 'labh + ta → labdha').

meaningShort: The voiced labial 'ba' signifies Bhagavān Balī — Possessor of boundless, self-grounded omnipotence ('bala') that sustains the cosmos. Unites Bhagavān Balī (TSS 1.9, boundless independent strength) with Mukhyaprāṇa and Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa's explicit 'baḥ = Varuṇa (lord of waters) & water-jar'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #39 · Pa-varga · Praṇava-Śānta (Paramātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 (`balī bhago manuḥ`) and MBTN 1.13 (`pūrṇāvyayātmabalacitsukhavīryasāraḥ`), Balī celebrates the Lord's effortless omnipotence by which Mukhyaprāṇa Himself derives strength (`vāsudevabalāśrayaḥ` — BR 1.3.16).

lakshanaDeva: ऐश्वर्यवीर्ययशःश्रीज्ञानवैराग्यात्मकषड्गुणपूर्णस्वरूप इति भकारवाच्यो भगः ।
lakshanaIast: aiśvaryavīryayaśaḥśrījñānavairāgyātmakaṣaḍguṇapūrṇasvarūpa iti bhakāravācyo bhagaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'भ' → Śrī bhagaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Bhaga — Living Ocean of the six boundless attributes (sovereignty, valour, glory, splendour, omniscience, detachment) and Self-Luminous Sun of Suns.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('बली भगो मनुः') and MBTN 1.24 ('षाड्गुण्यविग्रहं देवम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sūrya, the twenty-seven Nakṣatra-devatās, and Śukra/Bhṛgu.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa & Ekākṣarakośa ('भः शुक्रे'); in Mādhva samanvaya ('न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः'), stars and planets shine solely by Bhaga-Hari's light.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Neuter 'bham': star/constellation (nakṣatra — hence number 27 in astronomy) and zodiac sign (rāśi); Masculine 'bhaḥ': Śukra, bee (bhramara), lustre, and semblance.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.3.21: 'नक्षत्रमृक्षं भं तारा तारकाप्युडु वा स्त्रियाम्' and AK 3.3 / Medinīkośa ('भं नक्षत्रे च राशौ च भो भ्रमे भ्रमरे भृगौ').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada '-bha' from √bhā ('shining/appearing like': 'padmābha', 'sūryābha', 'pratibhā', 'gardabha/karabha') and Pāṇini's famous technical term 'bha' for stems before vowel/ya-initial suffixes!
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.3 ('आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः' on √bhā 'दीप्तौ') and 1.4.18 ('यचि भम्').

meaningShort: The voiced aspirate labial 'bha' signifies Bhagavān Bhaga — the radiant Plenary Perfection of sovereignty, valour, glory, splendour, wisdom, and detachment. Rich classical ekākṣara: Bhagavān Bhaga (TSS 1.9, sixfold divine perfection) + Amarakośa 1.3.21 & 3.3 ('bham' = star/nakṣatra/rāśi; 'bhaḥ' = Śukra/bee) + Pāṇini's 'bha-saṃjñā' & compound '-bha' ('shining like').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #40 · Pa-varga · Praṇava-Śānta (Paramātma-pāda)] Where ordinary beings have only sparks of virtue, 'bha' names Viṣṇu as 'Bhaga' Himself (`ṣāḍguṇyavigraha` — MBTN 1.24): His essence is not merely possessing 'bhaga', but being the living ocean of the six boundless attributes.

padaccheda.gloss: replete with aiśvarya, vīrya, yaśas, śrī, jñāna, vairāgya

englishGlosses: Mita — The One Known Through All Vedas (Oṃ's 'm')
Caturmukha Brahmā, Vāyu, Rudra, Candra & Yama (kośa)
