lakshanaDeva: मनुते सर्वं जानाति मन्त्रात्मा चेति मकारवाच्यो मनुः ।
lakshanaIast: manute sarvaṃ jānāti mantrātmā ceti makāravācyo manuḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: तथा मितं सर्ववेदैर्मकारेणाभिधीयते ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: tathā mitaṃ sarvavedair makāreṇābhidhīyate |
secondaryLakshana.translation: By the syllable 'ma' is signified He who is measured/known through all the Vedas ('mita').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Manu — All-Knowing Thinker ('√man'), Soul of all Mantras, and He who is measured/proclaimed ('mita') by all Vedas as Praṇava's 'ma-kāra'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('भगो मनुर्यज्ञः') and Chāndogyabhāṣya 1.1.1 ('तथा मितं सर्ववेदैर्मकारेणाभिधीयते').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mahālakṣmī ('Mā' — kakṣyā 2), Brahmā & Vāyu (kakṣyā 3), Rudra (kakṣyā 4), and Candra & Yama (kakṣyā 7).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Medinī & Ekākṣarakośa ('मो ब्रह्मविष्णुरुद्रेषु चन्द्रार्कयमवायषु'); Mādhva Tāratamya orders these exact deities strictly beneath Manu-Viṣṇu (kakṣyā 1), refuting any Trimūrti egalitarianism.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: मः (पुं.) काले चन्द्रे विधौ · मम् (नपुं.) जलं मङ्गलं सुखम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: maḥ (puṃ.) kāle candre vidhau · mam (napuṃ.) jalaṃ maṅgalaṃ sukham
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Masculine 'maḥ': time/measure (kāla), moon, Brahmā, Yama, wind, and anapaest foot (ma-gaṇa = 3 long syllables); Neuter 'mam': water, auspicious fortune, and happiness.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.28 ('इन्दिरा लोकमाता मा'), AK 3.3 / Medinīkośa ('मः शम्भौ वेधसि श्रेष्ठे चन्द्रे काले यमेऽनिले । मं जले मङ्गले प्रोक्तम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Superlative/ordinal/possessive '-ma' ('parama', 'uttama', 'madhyama', 'pañcama', 'dyuma'), prohibitive particle 'mā / māṅ' ('mā śucaḥ'), and 1st-person 'ma-' ('mama', 'mayi').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 ('मा निषेधे'); Pāṇini 3.3.175 ('माङि लुङ्'), 5.2.48 ('तस्य पूरणे डट्' + 'मट्'), and 5.2.94 ('तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्').

meaningShort: The labial nasal 'ma' signifies Bhagavān Manu — the Omniscient Thinker ('manute'), Embodiment of all Mantras, and the One known ('mita') through all Vedas. Crown jewel of Praṇava's third letter: Bhagavān Manu & 'Mitaṃ sarvavedaiḥ' in Sarvamūla, plus Amarakośa 3.3's famous pentad of deities (Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Yama, Candra) and time/fortune/water.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #41 · Pa-varga · Praṇava-Śānta (Paramātma-pāda)] As the third letter of Praṇava (A-U-M) and twenty-fifth consonant, 'ma' unites Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('Manu' — Omniscient Lord and Mantra-svarūpa) with Chāndogya Bhāṣya 1.1.1 ('mitaṃ sarvavedaiḥ' — truly cognized by all Vedas).

padaccheda.gloss: the labial nasal 'ma' (third constituent of Oṃ)
the All-Knowing Seer (`√man`) and Soul of Mantra

englishGlosses: Yajña — Supreme Worshipful Viṣṇu ('yajño vai viṣṇuḥ')
lakshanaDeva: इज्यते सर्वैर्यज्ञैर्यज्ञस्वरूपश्च स्वयं हरिरिति यकारवाच्यो यज्ञः ।
lakshanaIast: ijyate sarvair yajñair yajñasvarūpaś ca svayaṃ harir iti yakāravācyo yajñaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'य' → Śrī yajñaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Yajña — Supreme Sacrificer, Offering, and Ultimate Enjoyer of every Vedic rite and act of devotion.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('मनुर्यज्ञो रामः'), Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1.7.4 ('यज्ञो वै विष्णुः'), and Gītā 9.24 ('अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa-Vāyu ('yaḥ pavanaḥ', vāyu-bīja 'yam') and Yama-Dharmarāja.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('यकारः पवनः प्रोक्तो यमश्चैव प्रकीर्तितः'); in Tāratamya, Vāyu (kakṣyā 3) is the hotṛ-priest of cosmic yajña offering all acts to Yajña-Nārāyaṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Wind (vāyu), carriage/vehicle (yāna), fame/splendour (yaśas), barley, bacchius metric foot (ya-gaṇa), and journey/attainment ('yā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('यो वायौ यानयशसोस्त्यागे च परिकीर्तितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Relative pronoun 'yad' ('yaḥ... saḥ'), passive/bhāva stem suffix 'yak' ('-ya': 'gam-ya-te', 'dṛś-ya-te'), and gerundive 'yat' ('deya', 'jñeya', 'namya'!).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.1.67 ('सार्वधातुके यक्'), 3.1.97 ('अचो यत्'), and 7.2.102 ('त्यदादीनामः').

meaningShort: The semivowel 'ya' signifies Bhagavān Yajña — the Supreme Worshipful One ('yajño vai viṣṇuḥ') who is both Sacrificer, Offering, and Ultimate Recipient of every rite. Unites Bhagavān Yajña (TSS 1.9, 'yajño vai viṣṇuḥ') with Vāyu and Yama in Ekākṣarakośa, lexical 'chariot, fame, barley, light', and Pāṇini's relative stem 'yad' & suffixes 'yat / yak'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #42 · Antastha · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] Grounded in Śruti `yajño vai viṣṇuḥ` and Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 (`manur yajño rāmaḥ`), 'ya' teaches that every act of study, charity, breath, and duty becomes sacred Yajña when offered unto Viṣṇu.

padaccheda.gloss: Bhagavān Viṣṇu as Worship and Supreme Recipient

lakshanaDeva: रमन्ते योगिनोऽनन्ते नित्यानन्दे चिदात्मनि, रमयति च सर्वान् भक्तानिति रकारवाच्यो रामः ।
lakshanaIast: ramante yogino'nante nityānande cidātmani, ramayati ca sarvān bhaktān iti rakāravācyo rāmaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'र' → Śrī rāmaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Rāma (Mūlarāma, Paraśurāma, Balarāma) — Supreme Bliss in whom yogis rejoice ('ramante yogino'nante') and Fire consuming devotees' sins.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिः') and MBTN 1.2 & Rāma-carita chapters.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Agni ('ra-kāra' fire-deity, 'ram' bīja) and Sūrya bearing Hari's purifying brilliance.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('रकारः पावकः प्रोक्तः'); in Mādhva Gītābhāṣya 15.14 ('अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा'), Rāma-Nārāyaṇa is the inner Vaiśvānara empowering Agni (kakṣyā 7).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: रः (पुं.) वह्नि-तेजो-वेग-रतिषु · रा (स्त्री.) सुवर्णम् दानं च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: raḥ (puṃ.) vahni-tejo-vega-ratiṣu · rā (strī.) suvarṇam dānaṃ ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Fire (vahni/agni), heat/splendour (tejas), speed (vega), delight/love (rati), and gold or munificence ('rā' from √rā 'dāne').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 & Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('रो वह्नौ तेजसि प्रोक्तो रा दाने कनके स्त्रियाम्').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: -रः (रक् / रप्रत्ययः · धीरः नम्रः हिंस्रः) · रा-दाने धातुश्च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: -raḥ (rak / rapratyayaḥ · dhīraḥ namraḥ hiṃsraḥ) · rā-dāne dhātuśca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root √rā ('rā dāne' — to bestow: 'rāti') and primary/secondary suffix '-ra' forming adjectives of enduring quality ('nam-ra', 'hiṃs-ra', 'chid-ra', 'madhu-ra', 'mukha-ra').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 2.48 ('रा दाने'); Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.167 ('नमिकम्पिस्म्यजसकमहिंसदीपो रः') & 5.2.107 ('ऊषसुषिर... रः').

meaningShort: The liquid consonant 'ra' signifies Bhagavān Rāma — Supreme Spiritual Delight in whom liberated yogis rejoice eternally and who gladdens the cosmos. Famous agni-bīja ekākṣara: Bhagavān Rāma (TSS 1.9, ocean of eternal delight) + Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa's 'raḥ = fire (vahni), heat, speed, love' & 'ram = gold/wealth' + Pāṇini's '-ra' ('dhīra', 'namra').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #43 · Antastha · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 and Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya, 'ra' is the fire-seed that consumes sin and names Bhagavān Rāma (Mūlarāma, Paraśurāma, and Balarāma) — pure self-delighting Ānanda (`svarato'pi cāgre` — MBTN 1.2).

padaccheda.gloss: Supreme Delight in whom sages rejoice (`√ram`)

englishGlosses: Lakṣmīpati — Eternal Consort & Sovereign of Śrī
lakshanaDeva: नित्यमुक्तायाः सर्वजगन्मातुर्लक्ष्म्याः पतिरीश्वर इति लकारवाच्यो लक्ष्मीपतिः ।
lakshanaIast: nityamuktāyāḥ sarvajaganmātur lakṣmyāḥ patir īśvara iti lakāravācyo lakṣmīpatiḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'ल' → Śrī lakṣmīpatiḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Lakṣmīpati — Sole Eternal Beloved and Independent Master of Mahālakṣmī, Mother of all worlds.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.1 ('कमलापतिः') & 1.9 ('रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः') — corner-stone of Tattvavāda ontology.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: लः (पुं.) पुरन्दरो महेन्द्रः · ला (स्त्री.) श्रीः भूदेवी च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: laḥ (puṃ.) purandaro mahendraḥ · lā (strī.) śrīḥ bhūdevī ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mahālakṣmī / Bhūdevī ('pṛthivī-bīja') and Mahendra-Śakra ('lo mahendre').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('लकारः शक्र उच्यते, लं पृथिव्याम्'); in Tāratamya, Indra's very sovereignty ('aiśvarya-śrī') is a side-glance of Lakṣmīpati and Ramā.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: लः (पुं.) इन्द्र-लवनेषु · लम् (नपुं.) पृथिवी अमृतं च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: laḥ (puṃ.) indra-lavaneṣu · lam (napuṃ.) pṛthivī amṛtaṃ ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Indra (m.), cutting/reaping (lavana), short prosodic syllable (laghu in Chandas); earth and firmness ('lam').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('लः शक्रलवनयोः प्रोक्तो लं भूमौ लघुवर्णके').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada '-la' from √lā ('taking/bestowing': 'ṭha-laka', 'kam-bala'), taddhita '-la' ('vatsa-la', 'śīta-la', 'maṅga-la'), and Pāṇini's meta-symbol 'la' for all 10 finite verb tenses/moods ('laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve cākarmakebhyaḥ').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇinīya Dhātupāṭha 2.49 ('ला आदाने'); Pāṇini 3.4.69 ('लः कर्मणि च भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः') & 5.2.96–98 ('वत्सलादयः').

meaningShort: The dental lateral 'la' signifies Bhagavān Lakṣmīpati — Eternal Consort and Sovereign Lord of Mahālakṣmī, the ever-liberated Mother of the universe. Unites Bhagavān Lakṣmīpati (TSS 1.1 & 1.9, beloved Lord of Nityamuktā Ramā) with Indra and Bhūdevī in Ekākṣarakośa, verbal '-la' ('taking/giving', √lā), and Pāṇini's ten 'lakāra' tense-moods.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #44 · Antastha · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] Tantrasārasaṅgraha opens (`jayaty... kamalāpatiḥ`) and crowns 'la' (TSS 1.9) with Lakṣmīpati: while all other gods are subject to Śrī's command, Viṣṇu alone is Her eternal Beloved and Independent Lord.

padaccheda.gloss: Beloved Consort and Sovereign of Mahālakṣmī

lakshanaDeva: वरणीयतमो मुमुक्षुभिः श्रेष्ठत्वाद् वराणां दाता चेति वकारवाच्यो वरः ।
lakshanaIast: varaṇīyatamo mumukṣubhiḥ śreṣṭhatvād varāṇāṃ dātā ceti vakāravācyo varaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: णात्मा तारस्थमो दण्डी धन्वी नम्यः परः फली । बली भगो मनुर्यज्ञो रामो लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः ॥ ९ ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: ṇātmā tāras thamo daṇḍī dhanvī namyaḥ paraḥ phalī | balī bhago manur yajño rāmo lakṣmīpatir varaḥ || 9 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.9), revealing 'व' → Śrī varaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Vara — Supreme Treasure chosen above all worlds by seekers of liberation ('yam evaiṣa vṛṇute') and Gracious Boon-Giver.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.9 ('लक्ष्मीपतिर्वरः'), Kaṭha 1.2.23, and Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.2 ('पूर्णो भूतिवरोऽनन्तसुखः').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: वः (पुं.) · मुख्यप्राणो वायुः वरुणश्च यादसां पतिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: vaḥ (puṃ.) · mukhyaprāṇo vāyuḥ varuṇaśca yādasāṃ patiḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa-Vāyu and Varuṇa ('vo varuṇaḥ', presiding over amṛta-waters).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa / Ekākṣarakośa ('वो वरुणेऽनिले'); in Tāratamya, Vāyu (kakṣyā 3) and Varuṇa (kakṣyā 7) serve Vara-Vāsudeva.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Varuṇa, wind, ocean, dwelling/abode (nivāsa), tiger/strength (m.); auspiciousness and nectar-water (n.).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('वो वरुणेऽनिले सिन्धौ निवासे मन्त्रणे शरे').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Amarakośa's enclitic 'vā' expressing option ('or', vikalpa) and poetic simile ('like', upamā), 2nd pl. enclitic 'vaḥ' ('unto you / your'), possessive '-vat / -vin' ('bhagavat', 'māyāvin'), and zero-grade root suffix 'kvip/kvasu'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4.5 (Avyayavarga): 'वोपमाविधिविकल्पेषु' ('वा स्याद्विकल्पोपमयोरेवार्थे चापि दृश्यते') and Pāṇini 8.1.21 ('बहुवचनस्य वस्नसौ').

meaningShort: The labial-dental semivowel 'va' signifies Bhagavān Vara — the Most Choiceworthy Beloved sought by seekers of liberation, and Supreme Granter of boons. Unites Bhagavān Vara (TSS 1.9, supremely choiceworthy to mumukṣus) with Varuṇa and Vāyu in Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa, water/dwelling/welfare senses, and Amarakośa 3.4's 'vā' ('or / as').
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #45 · Antastha · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] Resonating with Kaṭha / Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (`yam evaiṣa vṛṇute` — mutual choosing of grace and devotion) and Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.2 (`pūrṇo bhūtivaro'nantasukhaḥ`), 'va' invokes Vara — the supreme treasure chosen above all worlds.

padaccheda.gloss: Supremely Choiceworthy (`√vṛ`) and Bestower of boons

lakshanaDeva: शान्ता नित्यनिर्विकारसुखरूपा संवित् प्रज्ञा स्वरूपं यस्य स शकारवाच्यः शान्तसंवित् ।
lakshanaIast: śāntā nityanirvikārasukharūpā saṃvit prajñā svarūpaṃ yasya sa śakāravācyaḥ śāntasaṃvit |

secondaryLakshana.deva: आसीदुदारगुणवारिधिरप्रमेयो नारायणः परतमः परमात् स एकः । संशान्तसंविदखिलं जठरे निधाय...
secondaryLakshana.iast: āsīd udāraguṇavāridhir aprameyo nārāyaṇaḥ paratamaḥ paramāt sa ekaḥ | saṃśāntasaṃvid akhilaṃ jaṭhare nidhāya...
secondaryLakshana.translation: Before creation abode the unfathomable ocean of noble attributes, Nārāyaṇa alone — serene blissful Consciousness ('saṃśāntasaṃvit'), holding the cosmos within.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Śāntasaṃvit — Serene, Unruffled Omniscient Consciousness brimming with eternal bliss.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 ('शान्तसंवित् षड्गुणश्च') and Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya 1.2 ('संशान्तसंविदखिलं जठरे निधाय').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Rudra ('Śiva / Śaṅkara' — kakṣyā 4) and Indra, bearing auspicious peace bestowed by Śāntasaṃvit-Hari.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('शकारः शङ्करः प्रोक्तः'); in Viṣṇusahasranāma & Brahmasūtrabhāṣya, 'Śiva' & 'Śaṅkara' primarily name Viṣṇu (untouched by sorrow, giver of mokṣa-śam) and secondarily Rudra.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: शम् (अव्ययम् / नपुं.) सुख-कल्याणयोः · शः (पुं.) शस्त्रे नाशके च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: śam (avyayam / napuṃ.) sukha-kalyāṇayoḥ · śaḥ (puṃ.) śastre nāśake ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Indeclinable/neuter 'śam': spiritual bliss, peace, and auspicious welfare; Masculine 'śaḥ': cutter/destroyer of evil, weapon.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.4.7: 'स्यादानन्दथुरानन्दः शर्म शं सुखम्' & AK 3.4: 'कम् वारिणि मूर्ध्नि शम्'; Medinīkośa ('शः शस्त्रे नाशके शम्भौ शं सुखे मङ्गलेऽव्ययम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada '-śa' from √śī ('resting/abiding in': 'giri-śa', 'kuśa/ambbu-śa') or √śo ('paring'), distributive taddhita '-śas' ('ekaśaḥ', 'sarvaśaḥ'), and present-stem vikaraṇa 'śap'.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.15 ('अधिकरणे शेतेः'), 5.4.43 ('संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायां शस्'), and 3.1.68 ('कर्तरि शप्').

meaningShort: The palatal sibilant 'śa' signifies Bhagavān Śāntasaṃvit — Serene, Unruffled Omniscient Consciousness brimming with peace and bliss. Unites Bhagavān Śāntasaṃvit (TSS 1.10 & MBTN 1.2 'saṃśāntasaṃvit') with Amarakośa 1.4.7's 'śam = bliss/auspiciousness', Rudra in Tāratamya, and Pāṇinian √śī / '-śa'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #46 · Ūṣman · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] Notice how Madhvācārya uses this exact compound in both Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 (`śāntasaṃvit`) and MBTN 1.2 (`saṃśāntasaṃvit`): 'śa' denotes śānti/śam (auspicious peace), revealing God's knowledge as eternally luminous and tranquil.

padaccheda.gloss: the palatal sibilant 'śa' denoting auspicious peace (śam)
whose essence is unruffled awareness and joy

englishGlosses: mokṣa / final release & loss of bondage
lakshanaDeva: निरवधिकैश्वर्यादिषड्गुणैश्वर्यपरिपूर्णः षकारवाच्यः षड्गुणः ।
lakshanaIast: niravadhikaiśvaryādiṣaḍguṇaiśvaryaparipūrṇaḥ ṣakāravācyaḥ ṣaḍguṇaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: शान्तसंवित् षड्गुणश्च सारात्मा हंसळाळुकौ । पञ्चाशन्मूर्तयस्त्वेता ममाकारादिलक्षकाः ॥ १० ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: śāntasaṃvit ṣaḍguṇaś ca sārātmā haṃsaḷāḷukau | pañcāśan mūrtayas tv etā mamākārādilakṣakāḥ || 10 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.10), revealing 'ष' → Śrī ṣaḍguṇaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ṣaḍguṇa — Replete with limitless sovereignty, valour, glory, splendour, omniscience, and detachment.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 ('शान्तसंवित् षड्गुणश्च') and Viṣṇupurāṇa / MBTN 1.24 ('ऐश्वर्यस्य समग्रस्य वीर्यस्य यशसः श्रियः ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश्चैव षण्णां भग इतीरणा').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Skanda/Ṣaṇmukha (commander of deva-armies, kakṣyā 9), Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Harmonized in Tāratamya: Skanda and Bṛhaspati manifest sparks of martial valour and wisdom from Ṣaḍguṇa-Hari.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: षः (पुं.) · विज्ञः श्रेष्ठो मोक्षो गर्भः कचः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ṣaḥ (puṃ.) · vijñaḥ śreṣṭho mokṣo garbhaḥ kacaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Wise/learned knower (vijña), most excellent (śreṣṭha), final release (mokṣa), embryo (garbha), and patience.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa & Medinīkośa ('षो विज्ञे च कचे श्रेष्ठे गर्भमोक्षक्षमासु च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pāṇinian retroflex sibilant conditioning ('s → ṣ' after i/u/ṛ/k: 'vi + sama → viṣama', 'rāमेषु / rāmeṣu', 'धनुष्'), numeral stem 'ṣaṣ' ('six'), and 'ṣit' marker triggering feminine '-ī' ('nartakī').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.3.59 ('आदेशप्रत्यययोः'), 4.1.41 ('षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च'), and 1.1.24 ('ष्णान्ता षट्').

meaningShort: The retroflex sibilant 'ṣa' signifies Bhagavān Ṣaḍguṇa — the Lord replete with the six boundless attributes (sovereignty, valour, glory, splendour, omniscience, and detachment). Joins Bhagavān Ṣaḍguṇa (TSS 1.10, replete with six boundless attributes) with Skanda/Sūrya in Tāratamya, Ekākṣarakośa's 'wise knower, best, mokṣa, embryo', and Pāṇinian retroflexion ('ṣatva') & 'ṣit'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #47 · Ūṣman · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 (`śāntasaṃvit ṣaḍguṇaś ca`), 'ṣa' directly recalls 'ṣaṭ' — the six archetypal divine excellences (`ṣāḍguṇyavigrahaṃ devam` — Pāñcarātra / MBTN 1.24) which encapsulate infinite auspicious guṇas.

padaccheda.gloss: possessor of plenary sixfold divine attributes

englishGlosses: Sārātmā — Quintessential Soul of Tattvas & Vedas
with / accompanied by (saha -> sa- in bahuvrīhi)
lakshanaDeva: सर्वतत्त्वानां वेदानां च सारभूत आत्मा स्वामीति सकारवाच्यः सारात्मा ।
lakshanaIast: sarvatattvānāṃ vedānāṃ ca sārabhūta ātmā svāmīti sakāravācyaḥ sārātmā |

secondaryLakshana.deva: शान्तसंवित् षड्गुणश्च सारात्मा हंसळाळुकौ । पञ्चाशन्मूर्तयस्त्वेता ममाकारादिलक्षकाः ॥ १० ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: śāntasaṃvit ṣaḍguṇaś ca sārātmā haṃsaḷāḷukau | pañcāśan mūrtayas tv etā mamākārādilakṣakāḥ || 10 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.10), revealing 'स' → Śrī sārātmā.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Sārātmā — Quintessential Reality ('sat / sāra') of all tattvas and Vedas, savoured by Haṃsa-paramahaṃsas.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 ('षड्गुणश्च सारात्मा') and Yatipraṇavakalpa / Bṛhadāraṇyaka ('सोऽहम्' = 'सः एव अहम् अहेयौ ईश्वरः', never jīva-brahma identity!).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: सा (स्त्री.) लक्ष्मीर्गौरी च · सः (पुं.) सुपर्णो वायुः हरश्च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: sā (strī.) lakṣmīrgaurī ca · saḥ (puṃ.) suparṇo vāyuḥ haraśca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mahālakṣmī ('Sā' — kakṣyā 2), Vāyu (kakṣyā 3), and Garuḍa & Hara/Rudra (kakṣyā 4).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('सः पक्षिणि हरे विष्णौ वायौ सा कमलाम्बयोः'); Mādhva Tāratamya harmonizes Viṣṇu as supreme 'Saḥ', Lakṣmī as 'Sā', and Vāyu-Garuḍa-Rudra as His retinue.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bird/Garuḍa, serpent, wind, moon, road/wall (m.); spiritual knowledge and meditation (n. 'sam'); Goddess Lakṣmī (f. 'sā').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 & Medinīkośa ('सः सर्पे पवने दर्भे विष्णौ पक्षिणि कीर्तितः । सा लक्ष्म्यां च भवान्यां च सं ज्ञाने ध्यानयोरपि').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: स- (तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे · सगुणः सचेतनः) · तदोः सः सौ च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: sa- (tena saheti tulyayoge · saguṇaḥ sacetanaḥ) · tadoḥ saḥ sau ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bahuvrīhi/avyayībhāva prefix 'sa-' (< 'saha' = 'with / possessing / same': 'sa-guṇa', 'sa-hetuka', 'sa-vayaḥ', 'sa-kṛt'), upasarga 'sam-', and nominative 'saḥ / sā' (< 'tad').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 2.2.28 ('तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे'), 6.3.80–82 ('द्वितीये चानुपाख्ये', 'वोपसर्जनस्य' — 'saha → sa'), and 7.2.106 ('तदोः सः सावनन्त्ययोः').

meaningShort: The dental sibilant 'sa' signifies Bhagavān Sārātmā — the Quintessential Reality ('sāra') of all tattvas, scriptures, and joys. Rich philosophical & lexical ekākṣara: Bhagavān Sārātmā (TSS 1.10, supreme marrow of Vedas), Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa's Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī ('sā'), Garuḍa, Vāyu, knowledge, and Pāṇini's 'sa-' (< saha) & 'saḥ'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #48 · Ūṣman · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] In Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 and Yatipraṇavakalpa, 'sa' denotes sat / sāra (pure unsublatable being and essence): Viṣṇu is Sārātmā, the supreme marrow whom Haṃsa-paramahaṃsas extract like cream from milk.

padaccheda.gloss: the Quintessential Self and Sovereign of all

lakshanaDeva: हन्ति समस्तान् दोषानज्ञानपापानि, सारमात्रभोक्ता परमात्मा चेति हकारवाच्यो हंसः ।
lakshanaIast: hanti samastān doṣān ajñānapāpāni, sāramātrabhoktā paramātmā ceti hakāravācyo haṃsaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: शान्तसंवित् षड्गुणश्च सारात्मा हंसळाळुकौ । पञ्चाशन्मूर्तयस्त्वेता ममाकारादिलक्षकाः ॥ १० ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: śāntasaṃvit ṣaḍguṇaś ca sārātmā haṃsaḷāḷukau | pañcāśan mūrtayas tv etā mamākārādilakṣakāḥ || 10 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.10), revealing 'ह' → Śrī haṃsaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Haṃsa — Defectless Swan-Lord, Destroyer of sins ('√han'), Enjoyer of pure bhakti-essence, and Fountainhead Guru of the Mādhva Paramahaṃsa lineage.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 ('हंसळाळुकौ') and Chāndogya / Paramahaṃsa-upaniṣad samanvaya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa (vital 'haṃsa' breath), Rudra ('haḥ śive'), and Candra.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ekākṣarakośa ('हकारः शिव उच्यते विष्णौ गगनचन्द्रयोः'); in Tāratamya, Prāṇa (kakṣyā 3) and Rudra (kakṣyā 4) constantly recite the Haṃsa-mantra adoring Haṃsa-Vāsudeva.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: हः (पुं.) विष्णु-शिव-चन्द्र-गगनेषु · हम् (नपुं.) ज्ञानमानन्दः परं ब्रह्म
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: haḥ (puṃ.) viṣṇu-śiva-candra-gaganeṣu · ham (napuṃ.) jñānamānandaḥ paraṃ brahma
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Viṣṇu, Śiva, moon, sky/ether, water, auspiciousness, pride/valour (m.); knowledge, bliss, and Supreme Brahman (n. 'ham').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 & Medinīkośa ('हः शिवे गगनेऽम्भसि शशाङ्के मङ्गले हरौ । हं परब्रह्मणि ध्याने').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: -हः / -हा (√हन् + ड / क्विप्) · ह (अव्ययम्) प्रसिद्धौ पादपूरणे च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: -haḥ / -hā (√han + ḍa / kvip) · ha (avyayam) prasiddhau pādapūraṇe ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Upapada '-ha / -han' from √han ('destroying/removing': 'pāpa-ha', 'duḥkha-ha', 'vṛtra-hā', 'śatru-ghna') or √hā ('relinquishing'), and Vedic/Upaniṣadic narrative particle 'ha' ('iti ha smāha').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga: 'ह प्रसिद्धौ स्मृतौ'); Pāṇini 3.2.49–50 ('आशिषि हनः', 'अपे क्लेशतमसोः' — 'kleśāpahaḥ, tamo'pahaḥ').

meaningShort: The aspirate 'ha' signifies Bhagavān Haṃsa — the Immaculate Swan-Lord free of all defects, Destroyer of sins, and primal Teacher of Paramahaṃsa wisdom. Sacred Paramahaṃsa-lineage ekākṣara: Bhagavān Haṃsa (TSS 1.10, primal Guru of Madhvācārya's paramparā), plus Amarakośa/Ekākṣarakośa's 'Viṣṇu, Rudra, sky, moon, bliss, knowledge', '-ha' ('remover'), and avyaya 'ha'.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #49 · Ūṣman · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] For Madhvācārya's own Paramahaṃsa lineage (beginning directly from Śrī Haṃsa-nāmaka Paramātman → Caturmukha → Sanakādi → Dūrvāsa → Acyutaprekṣa → Ānandatīrtha), 'ha' → Haṃsa holds supreme lineage reverence.

padaccheda.gloss: Bhagavān Haṃsa — pure, defectless destroyer of bondage
dispeller of blemish and enjoyer of pure devotion

lakshanaDeva: ळालयति लालयति स्नेहेन पोषयत्याश्रितान् भक्तानिति वैदिकळकारवाच्यो ळाळुकः ।
lakshanaIast: ḷālayati lālayati snehena poṣayaty āśritān bhaktān iti vaidikaḷakāravācyo ḷāḷukaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: शान्तसंवित् षड्गुणश्च सारात्मा हंसळाळुकौ । पञ्चाशन्मूर्तयस्त्वेता ममाकारादिलक्षकाः ॥ १० ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: śāntasaṃvit ṣaḍguṇaś ca sārātmā haṃsaḷāḷukau | pañcāśan mūrtayas tv etā mamākārādilakṣakāḥ || 10 ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Canonical Mātṛkā enumeration in Śrī Madhvācārya's Tantrasārasaṅgraha (TSS 1.10), revealing 'ळ' → Śrī ḷāḷukaḥ.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Ḷāḷuka — Fiftieth Praṇava-mūrti who tenderly cherishes, fondles, and nurtures ('√lal') His surrendered children.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 ('हंसळाळुकौ । पञ्चाशन्मूर्तयस्त्वेता ममाकारादिलक्षकाः') & Ṛgbhāṣya 1.1.1 ('अग्निमीळे' — praising adorable Nārāyaṇa).

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Iḷā / Bhūdevī (sacred earth and Vedic praise-goddess in Āprī hymns) and Agni ('īḷita').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ṛgbhāṣya on Āprī-sūktas ('इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीरमयोभुवः'): Bhū/Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī glorify Ḷāḷuka-Hari in Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ळः (पुं./स्त्री.) · लालनं वात्सल्यं शक्तिः भूमिः स्तुतिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ḷaḥ (puṃ./strī.) · lālanaṃ vātsalyaṃ śaktiḥ bhūmiḥ stutiḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Affectionate nurturing (lālana), maternal/paternal tenderness, sacred praise ('īḷā'), and earth.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Nighaṇṭu / Nirukta ('इळा = वाक् / भूमिः') & Varṇakośa ('ळकारः शक्तिवात्सल्यभूमिलालनवाचकः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Canonical Ṛgvedic/Śaunakīya retroflex lateral flap replacing intervocalic 'ḍa' (and 'ḍha → ḷha', e.g., 'īḍe → īḷe', 'mīḍhuṣe → mīḷhuṣe', 'ṣoḍaśa → ṣoḷaśa').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ṛgveda-Prātiśākhya 1.52 ('द्वयोश्चास्य स्वरयोर्मध्यमेत्य सम्पद्यते स डकारो ळकारः') & Padārthasaṅgraha 2.16.

meaningShort: The Vedic retroflex lateral 'ḷa' signifies Bhagavān Ḷāḷuka — the Tenderly Affectionate Lord who cherishes and nurtures His devotees like a loving parent. Distinctive Vedic fiftieth Praṇava-varṇa ('ग्निमीळे'): Bhagavān Ḷāḷuka (TSS 1.10, overflowing with parental vātsalya), Iḷā/Agni in Vedic kośa, and the Ṛgvedic Prātiśākhya 'ḍ → ḷ' rule.
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #50 · Ūṣman/Antastha · Praṇava-Atiśānta (Jñānātma-pāda)] Distinctive to Vedic Sanskrit (`agniṃ īḷe`, `mīḷhuṣaḥ`) and preserved prominently in Karnataka-Udupi Vedic recitation, 'ḷa' crowns the fifty Praṇava-mūrtis of Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1.10 (`haṃsaḷāḷukau`): the Almighty Sovereign is ultimately 'Ḷāḷuka' — overflowing with vātsalya (tender maternal-paternal affection) for His children!

lakshanaDeva: क्षपयति नाशयत्यशेषदुरितमसुराज्ञानं च, न क्षरतीति वा क्षकारवाच्यो भगवान्नृसिंहोऽक्षः ।
lakshanaIast: kṣapayati nāśayaty aśeṣaduritam asurājñānaṃ ca, na kṣaratīti vā kṣakāravācyo bhagavān nṛsiṃho'kṣaḥ |

secondaryLakshana.deva: वर्णा अकारादय एकपञ्चाशत् । प्रत्येकं व्याप्ता अनादिनित्याश्च ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: varṇā akārādaya ekapañcāśat | pratyekaṃ vyāptā anādinityāś ca |
secondaryLakshana.translation: The phonemes beginning with 'a' (down to 'kṣa') are fifty-one; each is all-pervasive and beginninglessly eternal.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha (Akṣa) — Imperishable Lion-Lord uniting 'ka' (Kapila's bliss) and 'ṣa' (Ṣaḍguṇa's sixfold majesty) to annihilate all sin and fear.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Padārthasaṅgraha 2.16 ('वर्णा अकारादय एकपञ्चाशत्'), Tantrasāra Mātṛkā-nyāsa, and Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('क्षो नृसिंहे' — explicitly naming Nṛsiṃha!).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: क्षः (पुं.) · प्रह्लादवरदो नृसिंहः, तदधीनौ शेष-रुद्रौ क्षमा च भूः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kṣaḥ (puṃ.) · prahlādavarado nṛsiṃhaḥ, tadadhīnau śeṣa-rudrau kṣamā ca bhūḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhūdevī ('Kṣamā' — all-forbearing earth) and Śeṣa-Rudra serving at Nṛsiṃha's command.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: In Mādhva Nṛsiṃha-stuti & MBTN, Brahmā, Vāyu, Garuḍa, Śeṣa, Rudra, and Indra stand with folded hands praising Prahlāda's Lord Nṛsiṃha.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: क्षः (पुं.) नृसिंह-रक्षो-विद्युत्सु · क्षम् (नपुं.) क्षेत्रं क्षयश्च · क्षा (स्त्री.) पृथिवी क्षमा
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kṣaḥ (puṃ.) nṛsiṃha-rakṣo-vidyutsu · kṣam (napuṃ.) kṣetraṃ kṣayaśca · kṣā (strī.) pṛthivī kṣamā
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Masculine 'kṣaḥ': Lord Nṛsiṃha, lightning, protector/farmer; Neuter 'kṣam': sacred field/body (kṣetra) and loss/dissolution (kṣaya); Feminine 'kṣā': earth and patience (kṣamā).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Puruṣottamadeva Ekākṣarakośa ('क्षो नृसिंहे च क्षेत्रे च रक्षोविद्युद्विनाशने । क्षा पृथिव्यां क्षमायां च') & Amarakośa 2.1.3 ('क्षा क्षमा अवनिः').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: क्ष (क + ष संयोगः · चोः कुः, आदेशप्रत्यययोः) · क्षि-क्षै-क्षिप् धातुवर्गश्च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kṣa (ka + ṣa saṃyogaḥ · coḥ kuḥ, ādeśapratyayayoḥ) · kṣi-kṣai-kṣip dhātuvargaśca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Conjunct 'k + ṣ' formed in Pāṇinian morphophonemics from velar/palatal/retroflex + 's' ('vac + sya → vakṣyati', 'dṛś → drakṣyati', 'duh + sa → dhukṣa') and root-family √kṣi ('dwelling' & 'waning' — whence 'a-kṣara').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.30 ('चोः कुः'), 8.2.41 ('षढोः कः सि'), and 8.3.59 ('आदेशप्रत्यययोः' — 'k + s → kṣ').

meaningShort: The fifty-first crowning syllable 'kṣa' (Meru-varṇa, uniting 'ka' + 'ṣa') signifies Bhagavān Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha (Akṣa) — the Imperishable Destroyer of all sin, fear, and ignorance. Crowning 51st Meru-syllable ('ka' Kapila + 'ṣa' Ṣaḍguṇa): Bhagavān Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha (Akṣa) in Mādhva Mātṛkā-nyāsa AND Puruṣottamadeva's Ekākṣarakośa ('kṣo nṛsiṃhe ca kṣetre ca')!
meaningDeep: [Varṇa #51 · Meru-Varṇa · Ekapañcāśad-Mātṛkā Culmination] Completing the fifty-one-syllable (`ekapañcāśad-varṇa`) Mātṛkā mala from 'a' (Aja) to 'kṣa' (`akṣamālā`), 'kṣa' fuses 'ka' (Kapila — supreme bliss) and 'ṣa' (Ṣaḍguṇa — plenary sixfold majesty) into the blazing Ekākṣara bīja of Bhagavān Nṛsiṃha, who annihilates (`kṣapayati`) all bondage.

padaccheda.gloss: annihilator of all evil and bondage

lakshanaDeva: स्वर्गेषुपशुवाग्वज्रदिङ्नेत्रघृणिभूजले । लक्ष्यदृष्ट्या स्त्रियां पुंसि गौः ॥
lakshanaIast: svargeṣupaśuvāgvajradiṅnetraghṛṇibhūjale | lakṣyadṛṣṭyā striyāṃ puṃsi gauḥ ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: गोभिरेव यतो वेद्यो गोविन्दः स उदाहृतः । गां विन्दते धारयतीति च ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: gobhir eva yato vedyo govindaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ | gāṃ vindate dhārayatīti ca ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Because He alone is supremely known through the 'Go's (sacred Vedic words) and sustains Earth, Heaven, and Senses, Bhagavān is celebrated as Govinda.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Govinda — He whom all Vedic words ('gāvaḥ') proclaim, who pervades ('gacchati') all worlds, and who rescued Earth as Adi-Varāha.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: MBTN & Bhagavadgītābhāṣya: 'गोभिर्वेदैर्वेद्यत्वाद् गोविन्दः'.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vāgdevī Sarasvatī/Bhāratī (presiding over speech), Bhūdevī (Earth), Vivasvān Sūrya (presiding over rays & sight), and Surabhi/Kāmadhenu.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ordered in Mādhva Tāratamya from Ramā → Sarasvatī/Bhāratī → Garuḍa/Śeṣa → Indra/Sūrya/Bhūdevī.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Ten classical nominal senses: (1) heaven, (2) arrow, (3) cow/bull, (4) speech/Veda, (5) thunderbolt, (6) spatial quarter, (7) eye/sense-faculty, (8) sunbeam, (9) earth, (10) water.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3.25 ('स्वर्गेषुपशुवाग्वज्रदिङ्नेत्रघृणिभूजले') & AK 2.9.57.

ekaksharaSenses.formIast: go (gamer ḍoḥ · uṇādi 2.67) · gopāyati / gotram / gocaraḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Derived from √gam ('to move/know') + Uṇādi suffix '-ḍo'; productive base of 'gocara' (sphere of sense-cognition), 'gotra' (lineage/mountain), and 'gopa' (protector).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.122–123 ('अवङ् स्फोटायनस्य') & Uṇādisūtra 2.67.

meaningShort: The supreme polysemous monosyllable of Amarakośa 3.3.25 — denoting nine classical domains (heaven, arrow, cattle, Vedic speech, thunderbolt, direction, eye/senses, light-ray, earth, and water) and culminating in Bhagavān Govinda.
meaningDeep: Among all monosyllabic words in Sanskrit lexicography, 'go' (`gauḥ`) stands pre-eminent in Amarasiṃha's Nānārthavarga (3.3.25). Śrī Madhvācārya shows across Brahmasūtrabhāṣya, Bhagavadgītābhāṣya, and Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya that every one of Amarakośa's nine senses converges on Viṣṇu as Govinda and Gopati: known through Vedic speech (`vāk`), Lord of Vaikuṇṭha/Svarga, Uplifter of Earth (`bhū`) as Varāha, Inner Director of eyes/senses (`netra/hṛṣīka`), and Effulgence within solar rays (`ghṛṇi`).

padaccheda.gloss: in Vedic speech, earth, rays, senses, heaven, cow

lakshanaDeva: भूर्भूमौ स्थानमात्रे च । बहुत्वाद् भूरितीरितो भगवान् ॥
lakshanaIast: bhūr bhūmau sthānamātre ca | bahutvād bhūr itīrito bhagavān ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: भूरिति वैश्वानरोऽग्निः, सर्वपूर्णत्वाद् भगवान् विष्णुः ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: bhūr iti vaiśvānaro'gniḥ, sarvapūrṇatvād bhagavān viṣṇuḥ |
secondaryLakshana.translation: As the first sacred Vyāhṛti, 'Bhūḥ' primarily names Bhagavān Viṣṇu from His infinite fullness ('bahutvāt / pūrṇatvāt'), and secondarily Agni and Earth.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Viṣṇu — Infinite Being ('bhūmā / bahutva') proclaimed by the first Mahāvyāhṛti of Gāyatrī.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Taittirīyabhāṣya 1.5 & Tantrasārasaṅgraha 1 ('बहुत्वाद् भूरितीरितः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Goddess Bhūdevī (aspect of Mahālakṣmī presiding over Earth) and Agni (presiding deity of the terrestrial plane under Hari).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Bhū-sūkta & TU 1.5 ('भूरित्यग्निः') ordered in Tāratamya beneath Viṣṇu.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Earth/soil, any site or locus ('sthāna-mātra'), sacrificial ground, and origination/birth.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 2.1.2 ('भूर्भूमिरचलानन्ता') & Medinīkośa ('भूर्भूमौ स्थानमात्रे च').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root-stem (`√bhū + kvip`) forming compounds meaning 'born from / existing as' (`svayambhū`, `padmabhū`), and indeclinable `bhūḥ` in Avyayavarga.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini 3.2.178–179 ('भुवः संज्ञान्तरयोः') & Amarakośa 3.4.

meaningShort: Both the primal Vedic Vyāhṛti ('Bhūḥ' = Plenary Bhagavān Viṣṇu) and the classic Amarakośa monosyllable denoting Earth, Bhūdevī, locus/ground, sacrificial site, and pure Being.
meaningDeep: Formed with root-zero suffix `kvip` from `√bhū sattāyām`, 'bhūḥ' functions simultaneously as an indeclinable Vedic Vyāhṛti (Amarakośa 3.4) and as a feminine root-noun (Amarakośa 2.1.2 `भूर्भूमिः अचला अनन्ता`). In Mādhva Vedānta, its highest sense is Bhagavān Viṣṇu (Aniruddha/Viśva) whose plenary existence grounds every locus (`ādhāra`).

lakshanaDeva: इन्दिरा लोकमाता मा क्षीरोदतनया रमा । मा निषेधे च माने च ॥
lakshanaIast: indirā lokamātā mā kṣīrodatanayā ramā | mā niṣedhe ca māne ca ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: मायाः पतिर्माधवोऽसौ मा विद्या च रमा मता ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: māyāḥ patir mādhavo'sau mā vidyā ca ramā matā |
secondaryLakshana.translation: Because 'Mā' denotes Mahālakṣmī and liberating Brahmavidyā, Her Eternal Lord is revered as Mādhava.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari — the Omniscient Measurer ('māti jānāti nirmimīte ca') of all cosmos and Vedas.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Chāndogyabhāṣya 1.1.1 ('मितं सर्ववेदैः') & BSB 1.1.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Goddess Mahālakṣmī (Nitya-muktā, untouched by sorrow, supreme among all dependent cetanas in Tāratamya), who measures out grace to jīvas.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.28 ('इन्दिरा लोकमाता मा क्षीरोदतनया रमा') & Tattvasaṅkhyānam ('अदुःखस्पृष्टा रमा').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: मा (स्त्री.) · लक्ष्मीः, विद्या, माता, शोभा, मानम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: mā (strī.) · lakṣmīḥ, vidyā, mātā, śobhā, mānam
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Fortune/prosperity, sacred knowledge (vidyā), mother, lustre/splendour, and accurate measure/standard.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.28 & Medinīkośa / Ekākṣarakośa ('मा लक्ष्म्यां मातरि प्रमायाम्').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: मा / माङ् (अव्ययम् · निषेधे) — मा शुचः, मा गमः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: mā / māṅ (avyayam · niṣedhe) — mā śucaḥ, mā gamaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Indeclinable particle of prohibition ('do not!'), governing augmentless aorist (`luṅ`) by Pāṇini's rule (`mā śucaḥ` — BG 18.66; `mā phaleṣu kadācana` — BG 2.47).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 ('मा निषेधे') & Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.3.175, 6.4.74 ('न माङ्योगे').

meaningShort: Famous Amarakośa monosyllable naming Goddess Mahālakṣmī ('Mā', AK 1.1.28), liberating knowledge/measurement ('māna'), mother, and the prohibitive particle 'do not' (AK 3.4).
meaningDeep: In Amarakośa 1.1.28, 'Mā' stands right at the head of Mahālakṣmī's names (`indirā lokamātā mā`), whence Viṣṇu is `Mā-dhava` (Consort of Mā) and `Mā-pati`. Simultaneously in Amarakośa 3.4 (`Avyayavarga`) and Pāṇini 3.3.175 (`माङि लुङ्`), `mā` is the canonical prohibitive particle (`mā śucaḥ` — 'grieve not!', BG 18.66).

lakshanaDeva: श्रीर्लक्ष्म्यां त्रिवर्गसम्पद्विभूतिशोभासरस्वतीषु । श्रयति हरिं श्रयन्ते च तामिति श्रीः ॥
lakshanaIast: śrīr lakṣmyāṃ trivargasampadvibhūtiśobhāsarasvatīṣu | śrayati hariṃ śrayante ca tām iti śrīḥ ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari Himself as Universal Refuge ('śrīyate sarvair muktaiḥ') and Fountainhead of all auspiciousness.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Viṣṇusahasranāma ('श्रीमान् श्रीधरः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीः') & BSB.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Eternally liberated Goddess Mahālakṣmī first, and secondarily Sarasvatī/Bhāratī as presiding deities of sacred wisdom.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Śrīsūkta & Tantrasārasaṅgraha; Ramā stands immediately below Viṣṇu and above Brahmā-Vāyu.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: श्रीः (स्त्री.) · वेदाः (त्रयी), राज्यसम्पत्, शोभा, बुद्धिः, विभूतिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: śrīḥ (strī.) · vedāḥ (trayī), rājyasampat, śobhā, buddhiḥ, vibhūtiḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: The three Vedas, royal glory, beauty/radiance, intellect, sacred ashes/opulence, and threefold virtue-wealth-joy.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.28, 3.3 (Nānārthavarga) & Medinīkośa ('श्रीर्लक्ष्म्यां सरस्वत्यां च वेदे शोभाविभूतिषु').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root-noun (`√śri + kvip` with long `ī` by Uṇādi 2.57) and honorific auspicious prefix (`śrī-`, `śrīmat` by Pāṇini 5.2.94).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Uṇādisūtra 2.57 ('श्रिणीभुवोऽनुपसर्गे') & Pāṇini 5.2.94 ('तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्').

meaningShort: Revered monosyllable of Amarakośa and Vedic Śrī-Sūkta denoting Mahālakṣmī, the Vedic Triad, royal majesty, intellect, beauty, auspicious wealth, and sacred grace.
meaningDeep: Derived from `√śriञ् sevāyām` ('to serve / resort to'), 'śrīḥ' is explained across Amarakośa (1.1.28 & 3.3 Nānārthavarga) and Medinīkośa as encompassing divine Ramā, the three Vedas, dharma-artha-kāma prosperity, beauty, and wisdom. In Mādhva theology, every auspicious splendour in creation is presided over by Mahālakṣmī, who eternally resorts solely to Śrīपति Nārāyaṇa.

lakshanaDeva: बुद्धिमनीषा धिषणा धीः प्रज्ञा शेमुषी मतिः । ध्यायतेऽनया धत्ते तत्त्वमिति धीः ॥
lakshanaIast: buddhir manīṣā dhiṣaṇā dhīḥ prajñā śemuṣī matiḥ | dhyāyate'nayā dhatte tattvam iti dhīḥ ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: tat savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: We meditate upon that supreme radiance of Lord Savitṛ-Viṣṇu, who alone awakens and impels all our faculties of wisdom ('dhiyaḥ').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari — Self-luminous Plenary Omniscience and Inner Awakener of all intellects ('dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ṛgbhāṣya & Tantrasārasaṅgraha Gāyatrī-prakaraṇa.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Caturmukha Brahmā, Sarasvatī, and Mukhyaprāṇa-Bhāratī, who preside over mahat/buddhi-tattva under Viṣṇu's command.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tattvodyota & MBTN Tāratamya of buddhi-abhimāni-devatās.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: धीः (स्त्री.) · प्रज्ञा, ध्यानम्, भक्तिः, वैदिककर्म च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: dhīḥ (strī.) · prajñā, dhyānam, bhaktiḥ, vaidikakarma ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Discriminative intellect (prajñā), contemplative absorption (dhyāna), devotion, and Vedic ritual/sacred work (Nighaṇṭu 2.1, 3.9).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.5.1 ('धीः प्रज्ञा शेमुषी मतिः') & Yāska Nighaṇṭu 2.1 / 3.9.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root-stem (`√dhyai + kvip` with samprasāraṇa `dhyā → dhī` by Pāṇini 6.1.16); forms bahuvrīhi compounds like `sudhīḥ` ('wise scholar') and `sthitadhīḥ` (BG 2.56).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.178 & 6.1.16 ('ग्रहिज्यावयिव्यधिवष्टिविचतिवृश्चतिपृच्छतिभृज्जतीनां ङिति च').

meaningShort: Canonical monosyllable of Amarakośa 1.5.1 and the Gāyatrī Mantra — signifying luminous intellect ('prajñā'), loving meditation, Vedic knowledge, and sacred action.
meaningDeep: Derived from `√dhyai cintāyām` (or `√dhā dhāraṇe`), 'dhīḥ' is placed at the heart of Amarakośa's Dhīvarga (`buddhir manīṣā dhiṣaṇā dhīḥ prajñā`) and Yāska's Nighaṇṭu (where `dhīḥ` denotes both `prajñā` and `karma`). In Śrī Madhvācārya's Gāyatrī-vyākhyāna and Ṛgbhāṣya, Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa is both the Inner Impeller (`pracodayitā`) of every soul's `dhī` and Plenary Consciousness itself.

lakshanaDeva: ब्राह्मी तु भारती भाषा गीर्वाग्वानी सरस्वती । गृणाति स्तौति हरिमनयेति गीः ॥
lakshanaIast: brāhmī tu bhāratī bhāṣā gīr vāg vāṇī sarasvatī | gṛṇāti stauti harim anayeti gīḥ ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Viṣṇu as Supreme Object of all praise ('gīrbhir īḍyaḥ') and as Ekākṣara Praṇava among all utterances (BG 10.25 'girām asmy ekam akṣaram').
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Bhagavadgītābhāṣya 10.25 & Ṛgbhāṣya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Sarasvatī and Bhāratī (consorts of Brahmā and Mukhyaprāṇa presiding over sacred speech), followed by Devaguru Bṛhaspati.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.6.1 & Mādhva Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Speech/voice, hymn of praise (stuti), language, scholarly learning, and renown.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.6.1 ('ब्राह्मी तु भारती भाषा गीर्वाग्वानी सरस्वती').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: गिर् (√गॄ + क्विप् · इत्व-रपरत्व-दीर्घाः) → गीः, गिरौ, गिरः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: gir (√gṝ + kvip · itva-raparatva-dīrghāḥ) → gīḥ, girau, giraḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root-noun from `√gṝ` + `kvip` (`ṝ → ir` by Pāṇini 7.1.100 `ṝta id dhātoḥ`, lengthened to `gīḥ` before word-final boundary by 8.2.76 `rvōr upadhāyā dīrgha ikah`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.100 & 8.2.76.

meaningShort: Consonant-stem Amarakośa monosyllable (`gir` → nom. `gīḥ`, AK 1.6.1) denoting sacred praise, Vedic speech, Sarasvatī/Bhāratī, and poetic utterance.
meaningDeep: From `√gṝ śabde` ('to proclaim, invoke, praise'), 'gīḥ' (`giraḥ` pl.) is Amarasiṃha's canonical synonym for articulate speech and Goddess Sarasvatī (`gīr vāg vāṇī sarasvatī`, AK 1.6.1; `gīṣpati` = Bṛhaspati/Brahmā). In Mādhva Vedānta (`akṣarāṇām akāro'smi... girām asmy ekam akṣaram` — BG 10.25), the highest `gīḥ` is Praṇava and the unauthored Veda praising Nārāyaṇa.

englishGlosses: four levels of speech (Parā, Paśyantī, Madhyamā, Vaikharī)
lakshanaDeva: वाग्वचस्यपौरुषेयवेदे सरस्वत्यां रमायां च । उच्यते परं ब्रह्मानयेति वाक् ॥
lakshanaIast: vāg vacasy apauruṣeyavede sarasvatyāṃ ramāyāṃ ca | ucyate paraṃ brahmānayeti vāk ||

ekaksharaSenses.formIast: vāk · sarvavācām abhidheyaḥ prerakaśca vākpatir hariḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari as Vākpati — Inner Impeller of speech (`kenaṣitaṃ वाचमिमां वदन्ति` — Kena Up. 1.1) and supreme referent of all words (`sarvaśabdavācya`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Kenopaniṣadbhāṣya 1.1 & BSB 1.1.4 ('समन्वयात्').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: वाक् (स्त्री.) · रमा, सरस्वती, भारती, अग्निर्वागाभिमानी च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: vāk (strī.) · ramā, sarasvatī, bhāratī, agnir vāgābhimānī ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mahālakṣmī (in Vāgāmbhṛṇī Sūkta), Sarasvatī, Bhāratī, and Agni (presiding over the organ of speech).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Ṛgbhāṣya on Vāgāmbhṛṇī Sūkta & Aitareyabhāṣya ('अग्निर्वाग्भूत्वा मुखं प्राविशत्').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: वाक् (स्त्री.) · वेदः, भाषा, वाक्यम्, शब्दब्रह्म च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: vāk (strī.) · vedaḥ, bhāṣā, vākyam, śabdabrahma ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vedic scripture, spoken language, sentence/maxim, voice, and eloquent discourse.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.6.1 ('गीर्वाग्वानी सरस्वती') & 1.6.2.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: वाच् (√वच् + क्विप् · चोः कुः → वाक्, वाग्भ्याम्)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: vāc (√vac + kvip · coḥ kuḥ → vāk, vāgbhyām)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Palatal-stem root-noun (`vāc`) shifting to velar `k/g` word-finally and before obstruents by Pāṇini 8.2.30 (`coḥ kuḥ`, hence `vāgīśa`, `vāṅmaya`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.30 ('चोः कुः') & Uṇādisūtra 2.57.

meaningShort: Foundational consonant-stem monosyllable (`vāc` → `vāk`, AK 1.6.1) signifying the unauthored Veda, Mahālakṣmī/Sarasvatī, articulate speech, and authoritative testimony.
meaningDeep: From `√vac paribhāṣaṇe`, `vāk` spans earthly utterance (`vaikharī`) up to the eternal, uncreated Vedic revelation (`nityā vāk` — ṚV 10.125 Vāgāmbhṛṇī Sūkta). In Śrī Madhvācārya's Viṣṇutattvavinirṇaya and Ṛgbhāṣya, `Vāk` is supremely Mahālakṣmī and Sarasvatī proclaiming the glory of Supreme Brahman (`yaṃ kāmaye taṃ tam ugraṃ kṛṇomi`).

lakshanaDeva: द्यौर्दिवोऽभ्रं व्योम पुष्करम् । द्यौः स्वर्गगगनद्युतिवासरेशु ॥
lakshanaIast: dyaur divo'bhraṃ vyoma puṣkaram | dyauḥ svargagaganadyutivāsareṣu ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: द्युभ्वाद्यायतनं स्वशब्दात् ।
secondaryLakshana.iast: dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ svaśabdāt |
secondaryLakshana.translation: He who is the supreme substratum of Heaven ('Dyauḥ'), Earth ('Bhūḥ'), and all worlds is Supreme Viṣṇu alone.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Self-effulgent Bhagavān Viṣṇu (from √div 'dyuti-krīḍā-vijigīṣāsu') and His uncreated luminous realm Vaikuṇṭha.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 1.3.1 & Ṛgbhāṣya ('तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Indra, Sūrya, and Dyāvā-Pṛthivī deities presiding over the celestial realm under Hari's sovereignty.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.6 & Mādhva Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Celestial heaven (svarga), visible sky/atmosphere (vyoman), day (divasa, esp. in oblique cases `divā`), and lustre.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.6, 1.2.1 ('द्यौर्दिवोऽभ्रं व्योम') & 3.3 Nānārthavarga.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Irregular Pāṇinian stem `div` taking `au` in nom. sg. (`dyauḥ` by Pāṇini 7.1.84 `diva aut`), `dyu-` before consonant endings (`dyubhiḥ`), and adverbial `divā` ('by day', AK 3.4).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.84 ('दिव औत्') & 6.1.131 ('दिव उत्').

meaningShort: Classic diphthongal nominative (`dyauḥ` from stem `div`, AK 1.2.1 & 3.3) denoting Heaven, Sky, Day, Radiance, and the luminous spiritual abode of Viṣṇu.
meaningDeep: From `√divu krīḍā-vijigīṣā-vyavahāra-dyuti-stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu` (Dhātupāṭha 4.1), the monosyllable `dyauḥ` (`div`) unites sky, celestial paradise, daylight, and divine play/radiance. In Brahmasūtra 1.3.1 (`dyubhvādyāyatanaṃ svaśabdāt`), Madhvācārya shows that `dyauḥ` rests in Paramātman and in highest Vedic usage (`divo viṣṇuḥ`, `parame vyoman`) denotes Vaikuṇṭha and luminous Hari.

lakshanaDeva: स्वर्गव्ययम् स्वर्गनाकत्रिदिवत्रिदशालयाः । सुष्ठु रमयतीति स्वः परमात्मा ॥
lakshanaIast: svar avyayam svarganākatridivatridāśālayāḥ | suṣṭhu ramayatīti svaḥ paramātmā ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari — Independently Blissful ('sva-rata / su-ramaṇa') and Bestower of liberation's unalloyed joy.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Taittirīyopaniṣadbhāṣya 1.5 & Tantrasārasaṅgraha.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Vivasvān Āditya (presiding over solar light per TU 1.5 'suvar ity ādityaḥ') and Purandara Indra (ruler of Svarga).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: TU 1.5 & Mādhva Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Celestial heaven, supreme Vaikuṇṭha/hereafter, sky above the sun, radiance, and felicity.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.1.6 ('स्वरव्ययं स्वर्गनाकत्रिदिवत्रिदशालयाः') & AK 3.4.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Headword of Pāṇini's `svarādi` indeclinable list (`svarādinipātam avyayam` 1.1.37), retaining `r` in compounds like `svarga`, `svarloka`, `svardhunī`.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.37 ('स्वरादिनिपातमव्ययम्').

meaningShort: Indeclinable Amarakośa monosyllable (`svar` → `svaḥ`, AK 1.1.6 & 3.4) and third Gāyatrī Vyāhṛti — signifying Self-Blissful Bhagavān, Mokṣa/Vaikuṇṭha, Svarga, and solar radiance.
meaningDeep: Listed first among all names of heaven in Amarakośa 1.1.6 (`svar avyayaṃ svarga-nāka-tridiva...`) and reiterated in Avyayavarga (3.4), `svaḥ` is also the third sacred Vedic Vyāhṛti (`bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ`). In Taittirīya Bhāṣya 1.5 and Tantrasārasaṅgraha, Śrī Madhvācārya derives `svaḥ` as naming Bhagavān Viṣṇu (Saṅkarṣaṇa/Prājña) who delights independently in His own essence (`sva-ramaṇa`) and bestows supreme bliss.

lakshanaDeva: दिशस्तु ककुभः काष्ठा आशाश्च हरितश्च ताः । दिशत्यादिशति धर्ममिति दिक् ॥
lakshanaIast: diśas tu kakubhaḥ kāṣṭhā āśāś ca haritaś ca tāḥ | diśaty ādiśati dharmam iti dik ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari — the Supreme Preceptor who ordains (`ādiśati`) Vedic dharma and encompasses all ten quarters (`viśvataś cakṣuḥ`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Bhagavadgītābhāṣya 11.16, 11.36 & BSB.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: The ten Digpālas and Mitra/Candra/Dig-devatās presiding over spatial orientation and the ear (`दिशः श्रोत्रम्`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.3.2–3 ('इन्द्रो वह्निः पितृपतिः...') & Aitareyabhāṣya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Cardinal/intermediate direction, unmanifest space, indicative example ('iti dik' = 'this suffices as a pointer'), and precept.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.3.1 ('दिशस्तु ककुभः काष्ठाः') & Padārthasaṅgraha (Avyākṛtākāśa).

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: दिश् + क्विप् → दिक्, दिशौ, दिशः, दिग्भ्याम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: diś + kvip → dik, diśau, diśaḥ, digbhyām
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root-noun (`√diś + kvip`) converting palatal `ś` to velar `k/g` word-finally (`dik`, `diggaja`, `digambara`) by Pāṇini 8.2.36 & 8.4.56.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.59 ('ऋत्विग्दधृक्स्रग्दिगुष्णिगञ्चुयुजिक्रुञ्चां च') & 8.2.36.

meaningShort: Consonant-stem Amarakośa monosyllable (`diś` → `dik`, AK 1.3.1) denoting spatial quarter, eternal Avyākṛtākāśa, scriptural directive, and the presiding deities of space and hearing.
meaningDeep: From `√diś अतिसर्जने` ('to point out, assign, instruct'), `dik` signifies the ten spatial directions (East, South-East, South, etc.) in Amarakośa 1.3.1. In Mādhva ontology (Padārthasaṅgraha & Anuvyākhyāna), pure spatial dimensionality (`dik` / `avyākṛtākāśa`) is eternal (`nitya`), real, and distinct from elemental `bhūtākāśa`, while Dig-devatās preside over both the quarters and the auditory faculty (`śrotra`).

englishGlosses: Nārāḥ — waters & tattvas indwelt by Nārāyaṇa
lakshanaDeva: आपः स्त्री भूम्नि वार्वारि सलिलं कमलं जलम् । आप्नोति रक्षति चाप्याययतीत्यापः ॥
lakshanaIast: āpaḥ strī bhūmni vār vāri salilaṃ kamalaṃ jalam | āpnoti rakṣati cāpyāyayatīty āpaḥ ||

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: आपः · सर्वव्याप्तो नारायणः ('आपो वा इदं सर्वम्')
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: āpaḥ · sarvavyāpto nārāyaṇaḥ ('āpo vā idaṃ sarvam')
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa — All-Pervasive Sustainer (`√āp vyāptau`, plural of majesty `pūjāyāṃ bahuvacanam`) praised in the Vedic Āpohiṣṭhā hymns.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Aitareyabhāṣya & Ṛgbhāṣya ('आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Varuṇa (presiding deity of elemental water and taste `rasa`) and Mukhyaprāṇa under Nārāyaṇa.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Varuṇa-nirukti & Tattvasaṅkhyāna-ṭīkā.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: आपः (स्त्री. बहु.) · जलम्, सोमरसः, पूर्वाषाढानक्षत्रं च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: āpaḥ (strī. bahu.) · jalam, somarasaḥ, pūrvāṣāḍhānakṣatraṃ ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Elemental water (`jala`), sacrificial libations, celestial cosmic ocean (`nārāḥ`), and the Āpya nakṣatra Pūrvāṣāḍhā.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.10.3 ('आपः स्त्री भूम्नि वार्वारि सलिलं कमलं जलम्').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: अप् → आपः, अपः, अद्भिः, अद्भ्यः, अपाम्, अप्सु (नित्यबहुवचनान्तः)
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: ap → āpaḥ, apaḥ, adbhiḥ, adbhyaḥ, apām, apsu (nityabahuvacanāntaḥ)
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Lengthened to `āp-` in nom. pl. (`āpaḥ`, Pāṇini 6.4.11 `aptrintṛc...`), substituting `t/d` before `-bhiḥ/-bhyaḥ` (`adbhiḥ` by 7.4.48 `apo bhi`), and taking `-a` in compounds (`antarīpa`, `dvīpa`, `abja`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.4.11, 7.4.48 & 6.3.97 ('द्व्यन्तरुपसर्गेभ्योऽप ईत्').

meaningShort: Pluralia tantum monosyllabic stem (`ap` → nom. pl. `āpaḥ`, AK 1.10.3) signifying water, the primordial Nāra-waters indwelt by Nārāyaṇa, Varuṇa, and All-Pervading Viṣṇu.
meaningDeep: Amarakośa 1.10.3 notes the strict grammatical signature of `ap`: feminine and obligatorily plural (`āpaḥ strī bhūmni`, acc. `apaḥ`, instr. `adbhiḥ`). Derived from `√āpḷ vyāptau` ('to pervade/obtain'), in Aitareya Bhāṣya and Āpohिṣṭhā Sūkta commentary Śrī Madhvācārya reveals that `Āpaḥ` in supreme Vedic usage denotes Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa who pervades (`āpnoti`) and nourishes all worlds.

lakshanaDeva: भाः कान्तौ रश्मिच्छायासु भं नक्षत्रे ग्रहेऽपि च । तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥
lakshanaIast: bhāḥ kāntau raśmicchāyāsu bhaṃ nakṣatre grahe'pi ca | tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Self-effulgent Consciousness of Supreme Brahman by whose light sun, moon, stars, and intellects shine (`tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Kaṭhopaniṣadbhāṣya 2.2.15 & Bhagavadgītābhāṣya 15.6, 15.12.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Goddess Bhāratī & Mukhyaprāṇa (eternally delighting in spiritual knowledge-light `bhā`) and luminous devas Sūrya, Agni, and Candra.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: MBTN Bhārata-nirukti & Mādhva Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Feminine `bhāḥ`: lustre, ray of light, beauty, shadow/reflection; Neuter `bham`: star, lunar mansion (nakṣatra), planet, and number 27.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.3.21, 1.3.30 ('भाः प्रभा रुक् रुचिः') & 3.3 Nānārthavarga.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: -भः (उपपद-कृत् · सादृश्ये दीप्तौ च) — सूर्यभः, पद्मभः, आभा
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: -bhaḥ (upapada-kṛt · sādṛśye dīptau ca) — sūryabhaḥ, padmabhaḥ, ābhā
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Root-derivative (`√bhā + ka` by Pāṇini 3.2.4) at the end of compounds meaning 'shining like / resembling' (`kanakabha`, `tārābha`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.4 ('सुपि स्थः' / 'आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः').

meaningShort: Luminous Amarakośa monosyllable (`bhāḥ` f. / `bham` n., AK 1.3 & 3.3) denoting spiritual and physical radiance, sunbeam, beauty, reflection, and star/planet.
meaningDeep: From `√bhā dīptau` (Dhātupāṭha 2.42), feminine `bhāḥ` signifies light, beauty, ray, and reflection, while neuter `bham` denotes asterism/nakṣatra and zodiacal sign (Amarakośa 1.3.21 `भं नक्षत्रम्`). In Kaṭha/Muṇḍaka Bhāṣya (`tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti`) and `Bhārata`-nirukti (`bhā-rata`), Śrī Madhvācārya shows that all cosmic illumination depends on Bhagavān's self-luminous `bhā` (jñāna-prabhā).

lakshanaDeva: द्रविणं तरमृक्थं श्रीः राः स्युरर्थसम्पदि । अग्ने नय सुपथा राये ॥
lakshanaIast: draviṇaṃ taram ṛkthaṃ śrīḥ rāḥ syur arthasampadi | agne naya supathā rāye ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Hari (from `√rā dāne` — Supreme Bestower) and the unfailing spiritual wealth (`rāye = muktaye`) sought in Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad 18.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Īśāvāsyopaniṣadbhāṣya 18 ('राये मोक्षधनाय').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Goddess Mahālakṣmī (sovereign mistress of both spiritual and material riches) and Kubera (treasurer of celestials under Hari).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Śrīsūkta & Mādhva Tāratamya.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Wealth, gold, cattle-wealth, opulence, and generous gift.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 2.9.90 & Ekākṣarakośa ('रा धने स्वर्णदाने च').

ekaksharaSenses.formIast: rai + su → rāḥ (rāyo hali 7.2.85) · rāye, rāyām, rābhiḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Pāṇinian stem `rai` (from `√rā dāne` + Uṇādi `-ḍai`) replacing `ai` with `ā` before consonant-initial case endings (`rāḥ`, `rābhyām` by Pāṇini 7.2.85 `rāyo hali`) while keeping `rāy-` before vowels (`rāyaḥ`, `rāye`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.2.85 ('रायो हलि').

meaningShort: Classical diphthongal Amarakośa monosyllable (`rai` → nom. sg. `rāḥ`, dat. `rāye`, AK 2.9.90) denoting spiritual and worldly wealth, gold, and the treasure of mokṣa.
meaningDeep: celebrated in the closing Vedic prayer of Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad 18 (`agne naya supathā rāye asmān` — 'O Agni-nāmaka Hari, lead us by the auspicious non-returning path to supreme spiritual wealth!'), `rāḥ` (`rai`) is explained by Śrī Madhvācārya in Īśāvāsya Bhāṣya as denoting foremost the imperishable wealth of Mokṣa (`mukti-sampat`) and Aparokṣajñāna, while Amarakośa 2.9.90 records its worldly sense of riches and gold.

padaccheda.gloss: treasure, gold, spiritual wealth of liberation
declined with ā before consonant endings

lakshanaDeva: धूः स्त्री क्लीबे तु यानाग्रे भारेऽग्रे चिन्तनव्यथे । जगद्धुरन्धरो विष्णुः ॥
lakshanaIast: dhūḥ strī klībe tu yānāgre bhāre'gre cintanavyathe | jagaddhurandharo viṣṇuḥ ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Viṣṇu — Effortless Sustainer of the universe's entire burden (`ananyāś cintayanto māṃ... yoga-kṣemaṃ vahāmy aham`) and Charioteer at the forefront (`ratha-dhūḥ`) of Dharma.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Bhagavadgītābhāṣya 9.22 & MBTN.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa (foremost `dhurīṇa` of all souls in service of Hari) and Ādiśeṣa (bearing Earth upon his hoods by Hari's power).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: MBTN 1–2 & Tantrasārasaṅgraha.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Yoke-end of a chariot/carriage, heavy responsibility/load, highest place/vanguard, and reflection.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 2.8.55 ('धूः स्त्री क्लीबे यानमुखम्') & 3.3 Nānārthavarga.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: धुर् → धूः, धुरौ, धुरः, धूर्भ्याम् · धुरीणः / धुरन्धरः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: dhur → dhūḥ, dhurau, dhuraḥ, dhūrbhyām · dhurīṇaḥ / dhurandharaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Lengthens `u → ū` word-finally and before consonant endings (`dhūḥ`, `dhūrbhiḥ` by Pāṇini 8.2.76 `rvōr upadhāyā dīrgha ikah`), forming `dhurya` and `dhurīṇa` (Pāṇini 4.4.77 `dhuro yat-ḍhakau`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.2.76 & 4.4.77.

meaningShort: Consonant-stem Amarakośa monosyllable (`dhur` → nom. sg. `dhūḥ`, AK 2.8.55 & 3.3) denoting chariot-yoke, burden of responsibility, forefront/summit, and the cosmic governance borne effortlessly by Hari.
meaningDeep: From `√dhurv / √dhṛ` ('to bear, sustain'), `dhūḥ` is the root of classical Sanskrit `dhurīṇa` and `dhurandhara` ('leader bearing the foremost responsibility', Pāṇini 5.2.64). In Bhagavadgītābhāṣya and Mahābhāratatātparyanirṇaya (where Kṛṣṇa takes the chariot-reins and yoke-front of Arjuna's ratha as Pārthasārathi while sustaining all worlds), Viṣṇu is the sole independent `Jagad-dhurandhara`, with Mukhyaprāṇa as foremost bearer among jīvas.

englishGlosses: the body as nine-gated temple of Puruṣa (śarīram)
lakshanaDeva: पूः स्त्री पुरी नगरी वा शरीरब्रह्माण्डदुर्गेषु च । पुरि शयनात् पुरुषो हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: pūḥ strī purī nagarī vā śarīrabrahmāṇḍadurgeṣu ca | puri śayanāt puruṣo hariḥ ||

secondaryLakshana.deva: नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन् । पुरि शयनात् पूर्णत्वाच्च पुरुषः परमात्मा ॥
secondaryLakshana.iast: navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan | puri śayanāt pūrṇatvāc ca puruṣaḥ paramātmā ||
secondaryLakshana.translation: Because Supreme Hari dwells sovereign within the nine-gated citadel ('pur') of every soul's body and cosmos as Antaryāmī, He is revered as Puruṣa.
secondaryLakshana.source: Bhagavadgītā 5.13 & Śrī Madhvācārya's Bṛhadāraṇyaka / Puruṣasūkta Nirukti

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Foundation of the name 'Puruṣa': Bhagavān Viṣṇu who fashions all body-citadels (`puraḥ`) and dwells untouched within every heart-lotus as Bimba.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Bṛhadāraṇyakabhāṣya 2.5.18 & Puruṣasūkta / Gītābhāṣya 15.17.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Mukhyaprāṇa (guardian watchman of the body-city's vital gates) and Rudra (`Tripurāri`, vanquisher of the three asura citadels through Viṣṇu's arrow-presence).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Praśnopaniṣadbhāṣya & MBTN Tripuradahana.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: City/capital, fortified stronghold, human/subtle body (`deha`), house, and abundance.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 2.2.1 ('पूः स्त्री पुरी नगरी वा') & 3.3 Nānārthavarga.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: पुर् (√पॄ + क्विप् · उदोष्ठ्यपूर्वस्य ७.१.१०२) → पूः, पुरौ, पुरः, पूर्भ्याम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: pur (√pṝ + kvip · udoṣṭhyapūrvasya 7.1.102) → pūḥ, purau, puraḥ, pūrbhyām
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: From labial-initial `√pṝ` (`ṝ → ur` by Pāṇini 7.1.102 `udoṣṭhyapūrvasya`, lengthened to `pūḥ` by 8.2.76).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.102 & 8.2.76.

meaningShort: Consonant-stem Amarakośa monosyllable (`pur` → nom. sg. `pūḥ`, AK 2.2.1 & 3.3) signifying city, citadel, fullness, and the living body (`pura`) indwelt by Bhagavān Puruṣa.
meaningDeep: From `√pṝ pālane pūraṇe ca` ('to protect and fill'), `pūḥ` (`pur`) is Amarasiṃha's opening word of Puravarga (`pūḥ strī purī nagaryau vā`, AK 2.2.1) and in Nānārthavarga denotes both town/fortress and the physical/subtle body (`deha`). Across Upaniṣad Bhāṣyas (`puraś चक्रे द्विपदः` — BṛU 2.5.18) and Bhagavadgītā 5.13, `pūḥ` is the sacred body-citadel governed from within by the Bimba-form of Viṣṇu (`Puruṣa`).

padaccheda.gloss: that which shelters and is filled; city or body
citadel, town, nine-gated body of Puruṣa

lakshanaDeva: भूतधात्री रत्नगर्भा जगती सागराम्बरा क्ष्मा क्षोणी ज्यावनिः । सर्वं क्षमत इति क्ष्मा ॥
lakshanaIast: bhūtadhātrī ratnagarbhā jagatī sāgarāmbarā kṣmā kṣoṇī jyāvaniḥ | sarvaṃ kṣamata iti kṣmā ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Bhū-Varāha / Kṣmāpati — All-forbearing Sovereign who uplifts Earth from the cosmic ocean and pardons repentant devotees.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: MBTN & Dvādaśastotra ('क्ष्मां यो दधार').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Goddess Bhūdevī (third aspect of Mahālakṣmī: Śrī, Bhū, Durgā), embodiment of maternal forbearance.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tantrasārasaṅgraha & Bhū-sūkta.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: क्ष्मा (स्त्री.) · पृथिवी, क्षमा, राज्यभूमिः, एकसङ्ख्या (१) च
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kṣmā (strī.) · pṛthivī, kṣamā, rājyabhūmiḥ, ekasaṅkhyā (1) ca
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Earth, sovereign territory (`kṣmā-pāla` = king; `kṣmā-bhṛt` = mountain/king), forgiveness, and numeral `1` in Jyotiṣa bhūtasaṅkhyā.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 2.1.2–3 ('क्ष्मा क्षोणी ज्यावनिर्मही') & Jyotiṣa Bhūtasaṅkhyā.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Syncopated feminine derivative of `√kṣam` ('to bear/forgive') forming classical compounds `kṣmāpati`, `kṣmādhara`, `kṣmātala`.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Kṣīrasvāmin's Amarakośodghāṭana on AK 2.1.3 ('क्षमत इति क्ष्मा').

meaningShort: striking three-consonant-onset Amarakośa monosyllable (`kṣmā`, AK 2.1.2–3) denoting all-forbearing Earth, Goddess Bhūdevī, royal realm (`kṣmāpati`), and the numeral 1 in Jyotiṣa.
meaningDeep: Compressed from `√kṣamūष् sahane` ('to endure patiently'), `kṣmā` is one of Sanskrit's boldest single-syllable nominals (`k + ṣ + m + ā`), celebrated in Amarakośa's Bhūmivarga (2.1.2–3) and classical kāvya (`kṣmābhṛt` = mountain or king). In Mādhva theology, Bhūdevī (`Kṣmā`) is the eternal Śakti-aspect of Ramā upheld by Lord Bhū-Varāha (`Kṣmāpati`).

lakshanaDeva: सत् सत्ये साधुविद्यमानप्रशस्तेषु । सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत् प्रयुज्यते ॥
lakshanaIast: sat satye sādhuvidyamānapraśasteṣu | sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sad ity etat prayujyate ||

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: सत् (ॐ तत्सत्) · निर्दोषपूर्णगुणः स्वतन्त्रो भगवान् विष्णुः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: sat (oṃ tat sat) · nirdoṣapūrṇaguṇaḥ svatantro bhagavān viṣṇuḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Viṣṇu — Proclaimed in 'Oṃ Tat Sat' (BG 17.23) and Chāndogya 6.2.1 ('sad eva somyedam agra āsīt') as the sole Independent, Blemishless Creator.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Chāndogyabhāṣya 6.2.1 & Bhagavadgītābhāṣya 17.23–27.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Realized Tattvajnānins and exalted Devatās headed by Brahmā-Vāyu (`santaḥ` = the wise devoted to Hari).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: BG 3.13 ('यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तः') & MBTN.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: सत् (त्रिषु) · विद्यमानम्, साधु, प्रशस्तम्, सत्यम्, नित्यम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: sat (triṣu) · vidyamānam, sādhu, praśastam, satyam, nityam
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Five classical Amarakośa senses across all three genders (`san` m., `satī` f., `sat` n.): (1) existent/present, (2) virtuous/saintly, (3) admirable/excellent, (4) true/authentic, (5) venerable/wise.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.3 (Nānārthavarga: 'सत् सत्ये साधुविद्यमानप्रशस्तेषु') & BG 17.26–27.

ekaksharaSenses.formIast: as + śatṛ → sat (puṃ. san, strī. satī, napuṃ. sat) · sat-saṃjñā 3.2.127
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Technical Pāṇinian meta-term `sat` naming both present participles (`śatṛ` & `śānac`, Pāṇini 3.2.127 `tau sat`) and prefix `sat-` for respect (`satkāra`, 1.4.63 `ādarānādarayoḥ sadasatī`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.2.127 ('तौ सत्') & 1.4.63.

meaningShort: Canonical monosyllable of Amarakośa 3.3 and Bhagavadgītā 17.26–27 — signifying Defectless Supreme Brahman, objective reality (`sadbhāva`), moral goodness (`sādhubhāva`), noble sages (`santaḥ`), and auspicious deeds.
meaningDeep: Formed as the present participle (`√as bhuvi + śatṛ` → `sat`) and expounded explicitly by Lord Kṛṣṇa in Bhagavadgītā 17.26–27 (`sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca...`) as well as Amarakośa's Nānārthavarga (`satya-sādhu-vidyamāna-praśasteṣu`), `sat` refutes illusionism in Mādhva Vedānta: Viṣṇu is `Svatantra-Sat` (Independent, Defectless Plenitude) while souls and cosmos are `Asvatantra-Sat` (genuinely existent dependents).

lakshanaDeva: चित् संज्ञाने चैतन्ये च निपातोऽनियमेऽपि च । चिदानन्दमयो हरिः ॥
lakshanaIast: cit saṃjñāne caitanye ca nipāto'niyame'pi ca | cidānandamayo hariḥ ||

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Bhagavān Viṣṇu whose very essence — not an adventitious quality — is boundless, self-revealing Consciousness (`satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Taittirīyabhāṣya 2.1 & Tattvodyota.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: All sentient beings (`cetana` — locus of Sākṣī-awareness) from Mahālakṣmī and Brahmā-Vāyu down to the smallest organism, eternally distinct from `jaḍa`.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Tattvasaṅkhyānam ('चेतनाचेतनात्मकम्').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Awareness/knowledge (`saṃvit`), waking intelligence, and ritual piling/arrangement (`√ciञ् cayane` + `kvip`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.5 & Medinīkośa ('चित् स्त्रियां ज्ञानचयनयोः').

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Enclitic particle appended to interrogative `kim`-forms to express indefiniteness ('someone, something, somewhere, sometimes', AK 3.4).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 3.4 (Avyayavarga) & Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 8.1.48 ('किम्वृत्ताच्चिच्चनौ').

meaningShort: Essential monosyllable of Vedānta and Amarakośa — denoting self-luminous Consciousness (`caitanya`), sentient beings (`cetana`), and the enclitic indefinite particle `-cit` (`kaścit`, `kiñcit`).
meaningDeep: Derived from `√citी संज्ञाने` ('to cognize, be conscious', Dhātupāṭha 1.38 + `kvip`), `cit` stands as the middle jewel of `Sat-Cit-Ānanda`. In Mādhva Siddhānta, Viṣṇu is `Svatantra-Cit` (Infinite, Untainted Self-Luminous Omniscience), Lakṣmī is `Nitya-muktā Cit`, and Jīvas are atomic `Pratibimba-Cit` distinct from insentient `jaḍa` matter (`acetana`).

lakshanaDeva: खमिन्द्रिये पुरे क्षेत्रे शून्ये बिन्दौ विहायसि । संवेदने देवलोके शर्मण्यपि नपुंसकम् ॥ कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्म ॥
lakshanaIast: kham indriye pure kṣetre śūnye bindau vihāyasi | saṃvedane devaloke śarmaṇy api napuṃsakam || kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma ||

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: खम् ('कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्म') · आकाशवद्व्याप्तः पूर्णसुखो हरिः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kham ('kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma') · ākāśavadvyāptaḥ pūrṇasukho hariḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Supreme Brahman taught by the sacred Fires to Upakosala (ChU 4.10.5): infinite spatial pervasion (`kha`) united with infinite bliss (`ka`).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Chāndogyopaniṣadbhāṣya 4.10.5 & BSB 1.2.15.

ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Deities presiding over the sense-apertures (`khāni` — Kaṭha Up. 2.1.1) and Ākāśa-abhimāni Gaṇapati under Khapati Viṣṇu.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Kaṭhopaniṣadbhāṣya 2.1.1 ('पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूः') & Tantrasārasaṅgraha.

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: खम् (नपुं.) · आकाशम्, इन्द्रियम्, शून्यम् (०), स्वर्गः, सुखम्, संवेदनम्, छिद्रम्
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kham (napuṃ.) · ākāśam, indriyam, śūnyam (0), svargaḥ, sukham, saṃvedanam, chidram
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Nine kośa senses: (1) sky/ether, (2) sense-faculty, (3) zero/bindu in mathematics, (4) heaven, (5) happiness, (6) awareness, (7) aperture/cavity, (8) field/body, (9) city.
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Amarakośa 1.2.1 & Medinīkośa ('खमिन्द्रिये पुरे क्षेत्रे शून्ये बिन्दौ विहायसि').

ekaksharaSenses.formDeva: ख-यौगिकपदानि · खगः, खेचरः, सुखम्, दुःखम्, खहरः
ekaksharaSenses.formIast: kha-yaugikapadāni · khagaḥ, khecaraḥ, sukham, duḥkham, khaharaḥ
ekaksharaSenses.gloss: Locative `khe` retained aluk in `khecara` (Pāṇini 6.3.18 `śayavāsavāsiṣv akālāt`), compound base of `khaga` ('bird / sun'), `sukha`, and Bhāskara's `khahara` (division by zero).
ekaksharaSenses.samanvaya: Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.3.18 & Yāska Nirukta.

meaningShort: Classic neuter Amarakośa & Chāndogya monosyllable (`kham`) — uniting space/sky, sense-organ, heaven, zero/dot, cognition, happiness, and All-Pervasive Blissful Brahman (`kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma`, ChU 4.10.5).
meaningDeep: In Amarakośa 1.2.1 (`vyoma puṣkaram ambaraṃ nabhaḥ kham`) and the Nānārtha kośas, `kham` spans nine concrete and philosophical domains: sky, sense-organ (whence `su-kha` = agreeable to spiritual/inner sense, `duḥ-kha`, `hṛṣīka`), zero (`ख-हर`), heaven, cavity, and consciousness. In Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.10.5 (`kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahma`), Śrī Madhvācārya explains that `Kham` names Supreme Brahman because He is infinitely pervasive like space and replete with unalloyed bliss!

padaccheda.gloss: sky, sense-organ, zero, joy, All-Pervasive Brahman
